Picked this up on the gold box deal. Moved from my 25$ a month plan on my LG Optimus V to this one.

In hindsight, while I am not entirely happy with the phone, it is a step up and I kind of don't regret losing the cheaper plan I was grandfathered in on.

Pros!
Battery life is pretty nice.
Screen is bright, looks great.
TONS of room to install apps. As I mentioned above, my old phone was an LG Optimus and had a whopping 200~ megs to install them.
Beats Audio is actually pretty nice.

Cons!
Worst wifi I have ever used in my life. My touchpad, android tablet, old LG phone, etc all got 2-3 signal bars out of 3 while in my house. I barely even get the first little dot indicator on this one.
Not exactly a thorough instruction manual (moving from 2.2 to 4.0 is fairly different).
Phones shape is just, odd to me. It's not flat, and that little bar at the bottom pokes out strangely to me. That being said, I didn't take off any stars from the review for design issues. If it works, it works.
Cell camera is kinda "bleh" but then again all of em are. BRIGHT LED flash lights up the subjects but also washes out the photos.
Worse/slower data than my old LG on the same network.

Basically, as I mentioned before, while I don't entirely regret losing my 25$ monthly plan and moving off my old LG, paying 10$ a month more for literally the same thing stings a bit when I don't like the reason I moved that much. It's a great phone, but there are some fairly strong cons to me about it, the major one being the weak wifi signal.

Still, it cost me 50$ on the gold box deal, so if you can find it for around 50-60 and are upgrading from an older phone model, it's probably worth it. I would not, however, pay MSRP for this thing or anywhere near it.

Virgin Mobile does have some awesome reps though, and when I called in to transfer my phone (mid month, and I wanted to see if I could keep my old month or if I had to start a new one), they peeked at the call record and saw I had only used ~20 minutes. Had me swapped out and going in about 5 minutes and the phone was working for texts in about 10 mins.

4 stars for virgin mobile, 3 for the phone. If the buggy wifi gets fixed soon, then it'd be a 4 to 5 star phone. That slower data than my older device is really what kills the review for me.

The sound from this bar is clean, clear, crisp and LOUD! A very decent amount of BASS, with a sub woofer output should you want to connect one. I found out I ordered a longer bar than is recommended. How did I find out? The packaging for this bar states that it is for a 42" or larger TV. I purchased it for a 32" TV. The concern, I believe, is that if the speakers are too far from the TV's center it will not seem as though the audio is coming from the actors. My brain is making the leap and tricking me so all is well. I use my TV for music for the most part anyway (Comcast Music Choice and Fire TV Music).
It is disappointing that Fire TV Music has such poor audio quality since it is there that I can make personal music choices unlike Comcast. Fire TV just sounds plain bad. It did on the TV speakers and now on the bar; it is just un-listenable. Safe to call it "LOW FIDELITY"
As far as connecting an input to this bar from your TV you have many options and most all the cables you may need are included. I really liked that they included the cord to to connect the bar to a sub. This cord is over and above what is required to connect the bar to the TV...very nice touch VIZIO. Now I need to go to my storage and try to find my sub :-)
My TV only offers 2 audio outputs, head phone and optical. Included with the bar were a headphone-to-2 RCA connector cord, and a fiber optic patch cord, among others. That allowed me what would be considered the worst quality connection and the best quality connection possibilities. If you don't have OPTICAL OUT on your TV do not despair...the worst possible option (headphone-to-RCA patch cord) sounds FANTASTIC! I can detect no loss of fidelity between the two. You will not be missing out.
Now to the reason I gave it 3 stars rather than 5. The back of the remote just keeps sliding off. It is not broken in any way. Just poorly designed. I often use the sound bar in dark or nearly dark conditions. It is taking time to train myself to not go where I normally would to use the any of the buttons. So how about the POWER button? It is not the top left button on the remote as you will see and are used to on any other remote in your home. For some strange reason instead of the power button being in the far upper left of the remote they felt this was a good place to position the INPUT button. Power is upper right. Volume UP/DOWN is traditionally placed on the left side of the remote with a paddle switch or separate buttons. Located in the standard volume UP/DOWN positions are the TruVolume and the TruSurround HD. The volume UP/DOWN are located on a FLAT 1-3/8" (34.9mm) x 1-3/8" (34.9mm) multi-function EVER SO SLIGHTLY RAISED square. To be honest I can't even tell that it IS raised at all most of the time. If you go for the volume in low light you may operate any of 3 other function controls. Lastly, if you were hoping the VOLUME controls are the 2 well raised buttons on the right (traditional location) you would be wrong. Those are your BASS/TREBLE controls.
I am not sure I would buy this bar again knowing what I do now about the remote. As I said I often use the remote in low or no light. The problems I mention here may just be my own...but I doubt it. All of these tiny buttons and controls are all scrunched into a small 2-3/8" (60.3mm) x 1-3/8" (34.9mm) upper 40% of this little remote and they are not raised enough and not far apart enough to be used just by touch. I well believe that just 3 functions on the remote will account for 90% of it's use. POWER (that CAN be felt but it is in the wrong place...you'll get used to that) and the VOLUME UP/DOWN that exist on a square, fully smooth (NO tactile feedback...I'd hate to see a blind person trying to operate), 4-function piece of plastic that is raised about 1/32" (0.8mm). On the bright side for me, I found out fairly quickly that my cable box remote controls the basic functions of the sound bar. I hope you get so lucky.
Knowing what I know now I should have purchased a bar in the 28"-32" (71mm-81mm) class looking for features such as the control panel on the bar being mildly illuminated and a proper remote perhaps with illumination itself. My roommate may buy mine from me for a location that is always well lit and has a 42" TV. I'll lose $20 on the deal but I can get the absolute right bar for me.. I don't return items that are not what I would like due to my own failure in researching. So, for better or worse, the bar is mine. There is one thing you cannot fault; THIS THING SOUNDS AMAZING!
- Good Shopping!!!

The GOOD:
These work well for hearing dialog and hushed speaking, or when it's accompanied with a lot of background noise in certain movies and tv shows. Also work well if someone is hard-of-hearing, so that you don't have to crank up the volume on the tv (the volume of each headset is individually adjustable). We've found it also works well if one person watching tv while others in the room are playing games or watching something else on their tablets.
The BAD:
These are extremely Line-Of-Sight. The base unit has to be aimed directly where you're seated, and if you're sitting just a couple/few feet to either side, you'll start getting more & more static. If I stand up to grab something from the other side of the room, the static will overtake the tv audio dialog completely and I have to take them off my head. Seems strange that the technology is so limited on these, requiring near perfect seating placement. I'll even get brief blasts of static just by raising my hand up to my face, as it seems to partially block the signal coming from the base unit.
Overall worth having but could definitely be improved.

I read a review that got 300+ 'helpful' votes for this item that said that the sound specifications exceeded that of even the Air Pods Pro, which incentivized me to buy this, along with the fact that it stays in the ear better. (However there are attachments for pretty low cost you can get for Apple Air Pod pros that provide the same little hook piece that slips under a ridge in the ear to hold it in place like the Beats Fit Pro has).

Using the Beats Fit Pro with iPhone 13 Pro Max, running the latest iOS as of this writing, 15.3.1... I can say definitively and on no uncertain terms, that the sound was blatantly and immediately noticeable as having high treble, low base; a distinctly and irritable inescapable lack of fullness, or 'thin and tinny' sound, that I have since read others reported online as well. And adjusting the Music App EQ (e.g. going to the iPhone Music app settings and adjusting the equalizer to add more bass) didn't do much to give it the rich full sound I get with Apples Air Pods and Air Pods Pro.

After losing my Air Pods Pro, I had to use my Air Pods (which don't stay in my ears well enough), prior to getting the Beats Fit Pro I'm reviewing here, and even Apple's cheaper Air Pods (non-pro) sounds WAY better than the Beats Pro Fit do.

The Beats Pro Fit boasts apple's H1 chip which is suggestive of higher compatibility with iOS devices, allowing things like Siri (although I never tried that), but somehow the H1 chip doesn't seem to translate to high quality sound, and sound quality is the primary thing I expect from ear buds, followed by secure comfortable fit, and then all the other usability conveniences.

I wanted to find a cheaper alternative to my wife's wireless Bose headset, something with decent noise cancelling for flights and work. So far I've used Bose, the MPOW H5, Treblab, and Woltix with ANC.

The sound on these are first class - really great highs, mids, and lows - tons of clarity (when active noise cancel is on...otherwise it sounds a bit muggy). Very comfortable and light. BUT - I got these because they are wireless with active noise cancellation, and although the ANC is effective, if you are in a quiet room you'll hear a slight hiss when the ANC is on - many people report the same thing in reviews, and it's true - you'll hear it. You won't notice this when music is on or during a flight. I often use these at coffee shops just to zone out and focus on work, and I could notice the slight hiss in quieter environments.

I've also used Bose, the MPOW H5, and Woltix with ANC. I didn't want to buy another Bose headset when my wife and I travel together. Nothing will compare to Bose noise cancellation, but the MPOW H5 and Woltix are actually really nice for the money. The MPOW H5 don't have as good audio clarity as the Treblab, but at the end of the day I got noise cancelling headphones for the noise canceling. I ended up returning the Treblab and the MPOW H5 and I kept the Woltix because they are more comfortable than the MPOW and had the best low-price ANC. The MPOW also had some sound interference issues randomly when the ANC was on.

So:

Bose: Best noise cancellation, good audio, comfortable, but definitely expensive!
Treblab: Best audio, worst noise cancellation (you can hear a slight hiss when turned on), comfortable, but large and they don't fold down too small.
MPOW: Good audio, good noise cancellation, but was getting some weird sound interference with the ANC on sometimes. Tight on ears.
Woltix: Good audio, good noise cancellation, most comfortable (way lighter and less tight on the ears than the MPOW), and fold down the smallest.

Although it's a great price on Amazon, I'd spend the extra $40 and get yourself a decent car stereo.

I used this in 2 different situations:

1) in camera audio capture, connected directly to D7000, 7D & 5DII bodies. It produced great audio, but many times I forgot to turn the mic on, which resulted in zero sound.
2) I used this in conjunction with an external audio device, such as the Zoom H1, to get more specifically located audio. Again, it did the job good enough.

But compared to the Nikon ME-1, you're missing a lot of handy features from the VideoMic. For example:

Nikon ME-1 is stereo. VideoMic is mono.
Nikon ME-1 is bus-powered. VideoMic requires on switch and 9V battery.
Nikon ME-1 is compact and small. VideoMic is large and bulky.
Nikon ME-1 is cheaper than the VideoMic.

After using both of them I sold my VideMic promptly. The Nikon ME-1 does the job much better.

Finally the included Fuzzy Windjammer on this kit doesn't do much more than the already included foam on the VideoMic. I compared the two in light wind situations and found the sound to be nearly the same.

Save some money and trouble, get the Nikon ME-1.

I used to be a big Ultimate Ears guy from the aughts before they were bought by Logitech who killed their best product lines and replaced it with stuff like... THIS. The tiresome photos of impossibly gleeful adult-babies listening to music underwater and having the times of their lives thanks to this f——g speaker really gets cloying when it’s printed on literally everything except the device itself. But that’s Logitech for you. Of all things I have to complain about with this speaker, the sound isn’t one of them. Unlike its predecessors and smaller cousins, the Megaboom 3 doesn’t peak out the bass quite so much when it would otherwise be distorted. (This is the most common bit of digital audio gimmickry to fool you into think it sounds “crystal clear”.) The people complaining about this speaker in these reviews who say other brands are better are just brands more notorious for “loudness fakery” to make the sound seem more bass-heavy but is really just slick audio post-processing. It’s makes hip hop sound a little better but everything else is a murky mess. But I digress. This speaker does all of the digital trickery, sure, but at least the actual amplifier and speaker drivers aren’t rubbish so that’s I plus. I was playing System of a Down cranked in my bedroom and it sounded amazing, especially compared to my former Boom speaker which someone nicked from my garage. Where the Boo crumpled trying to product screeching highs and thumping lows the Megaboom 3 dominated. Of course I don’t use any of the EQ tomfoolery and let it play as close to how the music was engineered to play and its just dandy. Okay then, good sound: check.
The problem with this speaker, like all of the other UE speakers, is the brain-dead user interface and obnoxious audio feedback that you can’t properly adjust without hacking the device configs (allegedly). There is literally a single on/off switch for all audio feedback. Wut? No relative volume of system sounds compared to music, or selection of which sounds you want to hear and which ones you don’t, like that HORRIBLY OBNOXIOUS LOUD BEEP it makes that’s louder than the music if you accidentally lean in on your volume up button? Of course every sound is as loud as or louder than the music your playing. That’s just great. Furthermore, if you are listening to music through your iPad or iPhone, it decides to insert little beeps for certain feedback notifications that never happen when you are just using your device without the speaker. It’s horribly distracting and unnecessary, but worse is that you NEED audio feedback on if you want to be able to Bluetooth connect to it as audio feedback is the only feedback you get.

Ugh. Sorry, had a bit of a rant there.

It’s tough because I think the speak sounds decent and almost worth the price, but the UI team at Logite... excuse me... Ultimate Ears are clearly huffing paint fumes as each product they subsequently release is even more unpleasant to use than the last. Don’t let the coked-out looking teens with bright, expensive clothing printed on the box fool you.

I was reasonably impressed with this amp's fidelity, especially using dual driver headphones which the dinky DA converters Apple's builds into their hardware simply don't come close to cutting the mustard and end up distorting any low end sound, even at nominal volumes. With this amp I had the volume at levels which sustained listening would have caused hearing loss, but just to test it I could detect zero low end distortion that would indicate an underpowered amp. On the other hand, midrange performance is only mediocre. There is some faint crackle. It’s not terrible but it’s occasionally noticeable and shouldn’t be for a $69 accessory. This sort of amp is absolutely necessary for the ERJIGO KZ ZS6 (best value ever at less than $50 for dual-driver 15Ω earbuds). Unless you're an audiophile who wouldn't bother listening to music through an iPhone anyway, this is an okay solution but there are better DAC amps out there for less money.
Also, the lack of the in-line microphone function is a drag, but this is nothing new for in-line amplifiers. You can hear calls just fine, but you need to use the iPhone's built-in microphone as the headphones' in-line mic will be inactive. I only mention this because some miscreant's Q&A responses for this product indicates just the opposite, but I assure you this is NOT the case. The controls are nice, but the in-line microphone signal on your headphones will NOT be recognized for calls or making voice memos so I am not sure what the heck that person was smoking when he said that. Anyway, aside from that, this is a decent amp though a bit overpriced for what it does.

Purchased this about 3 weeks after getting a 47 in LG LED tv. Didn't want anything too high end, nor anything with a big bulky sub woofer so settled on the LG NB2520A to keep the brand the same with the TV. While this has built in sub woofers (as tiny as they are) the bass leaves a whole lot to be desired. This is great for the room it is in, and for those in my house who are actually using it, but this is clearly a quick fix upgrade. The number of HDMI imputs is fine, given one will be for a cable box, another for 3D blu-ray player and the third for an Xbox/PS3, as well as AUX imput for an ipod or any music player i wish to play through the speakers. The thing that is most bothersome is the sound bar remote does integrate with the LG tv, but both still need to powered on and off separately (there are 2 separate power buttons on the remote, one for the sound bar and one for the TV power). Another bizarre thing is there is no auto or off dim setting for the display on the sound bar. Every time the sound bar is turned on the lcd will stay on, the only way to shut off the lcd is by hitting the sleep button on the sound bar remote once. Granted, not a deal breaker, but something as menial as that is an option on many other sound bars on the market today. For the price i paid (approx $100) i cannot complain, it is an upgrade decent enough for the occasional action flick or sporting event.

I'm uploading a photo of the box. Green type on a black background. Not really a great design. Generally type and packaging tells you more about a product than the manufacturer might have intended. Just not that sophisticated.

Overall there are better dashcams out there. The ability to use WiFi to download video from the camera seemed promising, but I couldn't get it to work at all. The audio feedback from the device was far too loud and I couldn't turn it off. The mounting idea was dead on arrival, not happening.

Disappointing. Cannot recommend this product. A swing and a miss, as they say in baseball.

Sound quality and fit is perfect but the power on process kills it. You need to hold down AND release the power button to turn the earbuds on, but the problem is there is no sound/light that gives you feedback on when you can release the button. And if you hold down the button too long, it won't power on at all. Not only that, the power-on sound only plays a couple seconds AFTER releasing the power button. Essentially, these ear buds are a pain to turn on especially if you put them down for a little bit and you don't know if they're already on, or already off.

Down grading from 5 stars to 3 stars because it turns out there might be a bug in the mouse that once you pair it with 2 different computers over bluetooth, you cannot reset the mouse to use the wireless dongle. If you're tried of replacing batteries, this mouse is for you! I'm impressed by how long a single AA battery lasts in this mouse. Today I removed the unit from my front steps where it has been since I first received it almost 2 years ago. It had been causing the indoor alarm unit to sound without ceasing. I removed the batteries to see what might be the problem, and I found ANTS had taken up residency inside the sensor unit. After clearing as many ants as possible, I put the unit in a plastic bag that is sealed. It will be several days before I open the unit to clean the circuit board as well as the housing. Then I will attempt to seal all openings so that I can use the sensor. It may not operate reliably once all the openings are sealed, but I have no other choice.

The second sensor is not giving me any problem because it is in a location that ants will not frequent.

As for locating the sensor in my mailbox so I will know when someone has opened the mailbox door, that won't work. The metal mailbox prevents a signal from being transmitted the 100 feet to the alarm. Also, ants like to use the mailbox which makes me spray an insecticide when I see them, and that's usually once a year.

The picture of this is awesome. The 4k is the best I'd ever seen anywhere. Event 1080 games look fantastic.

When I first got this TV I have live PD on in the background while I making dinner. I got spooked because I heard sirens and it sounded like a cop car was in my drive way! Super trippy to have sound quality that is that good.

All around this is a fantastic TV. But I do have one issue with it, which is why I didn't give it 5 stars.
The smart TV Apps are WAY to buggy.
Everytime you leave the TV idle for an hour or so it cuts internet connection. Which makes sense. Helps save energy. BUT it seems a lot of apps struggle with re-connection issues.
A big one is sling. 7/10 times when I came back to my TV after I had been previously watching sling, it refuses to load any channel unless I do a hard reboot or changed apps. Even when it does work, I often get buffering or dropped frames. Which is def the TVs fault as I do not get this on any other device!
Netflix also locked up on me once when my TV went idle in the search menu and I came back. I could not exit the search or click on any titles. I have to restart my TV.
Honestly, Sony need to realize that making smart TV apps is not a simple task and they can't just leave it to a team of sloppy careless outsourced developers and expect good results.

However the smart TV apps being awful isn't a huge issue as I have a backup firestick and my xbox one that can do the same job but actually work :)

But still, for 3.5k I expected everything to be perfect.

Pros--
-Very comfortable and secure fit even during high intensity exercise
-Solid Bluetooth connection
-Good noise canceling
-Hear thru mode is useful
-Sleek, low profile look
-Decent battery life, charging case is nice
-mic works well for calls or voice commands
-LOTS of bass (I consider this a major negative, but some people will like the bass heavy sound)

CONS-
-Below average sound quality (WAY too much bass, even after using the EQ to turn down the bass its still more than I would prefer for most types of music, the default out of the box sound is the worst I have ever heard on a pair of headphones in this price range.. but that said you can make them sound pretty decent after a bit of tweaking with the EQ)
-Not loud enough, the maximum volume is barely adequate for high external noise situations like airplane (even with the noise cancellation which works pretty well)
-Sealed design is not good for 'active' pursuits because of microphonic effect amplifying internal sounds whenever you move around
-software can be buggy, occasionally when I change settings and they appear to be changed in the software but do not apply to the buds

I think there are certain people who will love these buds, especially if you listen to a lot of rap/hiphop or other bass heavy music as the default sound seems to be tuned for that kind of music. Personally I just can't really get into the sound of these, even after tweaking with the EQ there is too much bass and the soundstage is flat and lifeless. I do like a lot of things about them though, the fit is comfortable and very secure, much better than airpods or galaxy buds on that front.

Fits pretty snugly on our 10 inch galaxy note.  It seems pretty flimsy for a 'rugged exoskeleton' but it does afford some level of protection against dropping the tablet.  I would give it 4 stars if it had a stand flap on both sides, as-is I have to choose between having the power/volume buttons accessible when in the upright position, or having the charging port accessible.  If I want to use the other side while its upright I have to remove the case and flip it around.

The previous generation of these headphones were well regarded among some audio geeks due to their value. Their sound quality compared favorably to many other entries in the <$100 price range, and especially in comparison with other sealed headphones in that price range.

On this new version they have made a number of upgrades and also raised the price quite a bit. Unfortunately, not all of the changes to this version are improvements in my opinion and the higher price puts these in close competition with other headphones in the $150 range which are only slightly more expensive but have significantly better sound quality and construction.

I've never owned the previous version of these headphones but I have a friend who owns them and I have listened to them side by side with the new version. To my ears they sound very similar, both have a great high end and excellent staging for a sealed headphone but they are both bass heavy which I am not particularly a fan of. I would say the aurvana 2 seems to be even more bass heavy than the original so those who like lots of bass will probably enjoy these headphones.

I do like the new removable cord and the fact that the cord is only on one side of the headphones. I'm not really a fan of the red plastic design element, the old version was very nondescript whereas the new model tries to be flashy but looks kind of cheesy in my opinion. I do think the new shape is more comfortable though and also seems to offer improved noise isolation compared to the original model.

Pros:
Nice high end and midrange, good separation and staging for a sealed headphone in this price range
detachable cord w/ built in mic
comfortable design
good noise isolation (recently used them on a plane trip and they worked well)

Cons:
Excessive bass
Cheap looking plastic design elements
Old version sounds just as good and is quite a bit cheaper
Notably better headphones available from sennheiser, beyer, denon, etc. for only slightly more

I really wanted to like this product, it has good build quality and nice aesthetics but it suffers from a few design flaws which make it unusable for me.

Pros:
* Very nice keyboard (I have not been a fan of many recent logitech keyboards but this one felt very nice to me, slightly mushy but with a subtle tactile response. The integrated wrist cushion is very comfortable)

* Extra powered USB Ports (Despite what some reviewers have written, the external power supply is *not* required to use the keyboard, it is only for the powered USB ports)

* Works with 17" laptops

* Compact and easily portable when folded up

* Overall build quality, aesthetics

Cons:
* Not height adjustable (The height is good on some tables but on my desk the screen stands about 4" above the height of my 24" monitors which is just too high, killing any ergonomic benefits. I returned it and got an XBrand XB-1001 which is adjustable)

* USB cable which connects to the computer is too short, it could barely reach the USB port at the front side of my laptop.

* No integrated audio jacks, front of stand blocks the onboard audio jacks on most laptops which now have the jacks on the front rather than the side, making it impossible to use external speakers.

I bought mine direct from Samsung and ultimately returned them. I found that I had to fiddle with them constantly to hit the sweet spot for the music to sound like it should instead of like I was listening through a tin can, and while fiddling with them the touch controls become an annoying hassle because you are trying to get the fit right and the music is turning on and off and pausing and skipping, etc, because you are touching them. The buds can't seem to differentiate at all between an actual hold/grip to manipulate them in your ears, and a tap as you would do to actually use a touch control feature.

Don't quote me on this because it's not like I counted every review that appeared male vs female, but I found that they hurt and I think it might be because they were designed by somewhat larger-eared males. I originally assumed the hurty issue was likely because they were designed by some 60 year old man engineer with huge ears (because ears grow our whole lives) and so they were only made to fit kind of older larger ears. I even wrote on my Samsung review that they should have made the fit for the age group of their customer. But now, reading these Amazon reviews, I am noticing that the people saying they fit great seem to mostly be male names and those saying they hurt seem to mostly be female-normative names, so I still think they were designed for larger ears, but maybe for males they will fit better - I truly don't know how different in size male vs female ears are though; it's just a random observation of these reviews of hurt vs feel great.

Bottom line, they hurt my ears and were too picky about being perfectly aligned in my ear. On the rare occasion I hit that sweet spot they sounded great and never felt like they were going to fall out. Too bad it took so much effort to find that spot.

This could be a good unit but falls short.

If this did Bluetooth Media Streaming and had a dimmer option/button/anything I would have kept it. I had it for 28 days and returned it. I never thought I would care about a dimmer on a head unit until I was flipping blinded by blue light for an hour on my way home from work. Fail.

I needed a sound bar for my computer because my cat knocked over my other book shelf type speakers. I purchased this at a sale price of $15.00. At that price point, this speaker is adequate. However, at the list price I’d say that the bass isn’t very good, it’s muffled sounding and you can buy something from JBL that sounds better.

First unit lasted 4 months it just quit working. When it was working it had a great sound.  I called Vizio and was treated super!  They gladly sent a replacement and sent a label for free return of the broken unit.  Keeping fingers crossed that I will get many years of service from the new sound bar so I can come back and give it 5 stars.  I'm very pleased.

No problems so far; the volume could be stronger, but given this is a universal design flaw (speakers pointing down or back instead of out front), it's simple enough to modify with a sound bar.
Hooked up to wall, looks great...

Used the month for approximately a month for daily driver, after the month the amp would turn on but no sound. I disconnected everything and reconnected thinking is could be a connection. The amp would have power but no sound, I then decided to check the fuse , why not I had already checked everything else... So it appears the fuse socket on the amp may have a design flaw. I moved the fuse back and forth and the sound would come on and off for my subwoofer. Again this amp may have a short where the fuse is located I'm not sure if this is a common issue or not but I was able to request a replacement with 5days left to return the amp so hopefully the second amp does better. Will update.

The biggest thing is that these are meant to be true wireless stereo headphones, and they're not - all the manual says is that they will automatically connect to each other after turning on and before connecting to a phone; I left them in TWS pairing mode for several minutes without them connecting.
I was able to connect to them as two separate devices and got mono sound through both simultaneously. The sound quality wasn't as bad as I've heard on cheap headphones, but it was in the lower 20% - they're basically just very small (and cheap) speakers that sit above the ear canal. There is no bass, and mids/treble are a bit flat. They also do not get very loud due to the design. I will say that I like the concept of having them fit into the top part of the ear and project down and into the canal, but the execution was poorly done.
If I wanted to run dual-output every time I use them, I think they would work well for audiobooks and podcasts, as the vocal range are the frequencies the headphones favor most, and I typically don't feel the need to crank the volume on my audiobooks.

I ordered one, the back was bulged out like when a battery expands and I returned it. I then ordered 2 for the stereo pairing. Both have the same bulge. Upon examination it is caused by poor assembly: the battery appears fine, but there was a glob of silicon under the battery that looked as if it had spilled over from the waterproofing and was keeping the battery from seating properly. End result is the back case doesn't quite fit right and I'm a bit skeptical if it is still waterproofed. Even after removing the excess silicon and seating the battery properly, the case is still bowed out.
The sound is AMAZING for such a small package. They've used two speakers, presumably one to fill in the lows. It by no means thumps, but watching movies and playing games sounds very good. Getting the stereo pairing set-up was a bit tricky, and once it was set up it sounded out of sync occasionally. I mostly use these to have sound come from the monitor a video is on instead of my main computer.
The sound is not as good as I was expecting based on other reviews but it is a good enough headset for the times when my wireless headset is recharging.

Expensive. But it is nice to have a tablet In the dash of a 2007 Escalade. Haven't got the video out feature to work yet. The temp setting you see on the top of the screen doesn't work so I found it in settings and disabled it. You can send email to tech support for help and wait for replies and generic answers and sometimes go in circles. It was plug and play for my vehicle without all the expensive adapters you see in other videos you watched. SOME steering wheel controls work for. The most frustrating thing for me is the unit freezes up and you're stuck on whatever screen you were on and no way to reboot without turning off vehicle. Major pain when you're on the highway or turnpike. So wire in a separate on/off button hidden somewhere for this scenario. Sometimes it freezes and goes to black screen so you lost Waze or Google Maps. I tether to my hotspot on phone with Visible Wireless and been working for me. Another complaint is about the screen customization. Not many. You can change your default apps when you click the map icon or radio icon etc. My Android Auto did work but I don't use it. The Android Auto is made so you do not use phone while driving.  The Easy Connection does mirror my Galaxy S10 Fe 5g but with the default screen the way it is you're not going to see it any bigger than your smart phone display. I have no complaints with the sound (factory Bose in Cadillac)  You do have Eq settings and time delay options to play with. The installation instructions if you want to call it that are ridiculous. But if you ever installed a stereo you will figure it out  I do not believe this unit has dual zone feature so that's a huge bummer.  And if the video out feature doesn't work it will get exchanged.  A purchase is only as good as the tech support when needed. That's why my rating is what it is.  Can't drag and change the screens as seen on other units. The XM app is either full screen or minimized. There's limitations like that. I don't like the big band across the top and bottom and not allowing the user to adjust it more. we done need the huge buttons for the phone. Definitely nice things to like about the unit though.  Will update more as time goes on.

I've been using these for a couple of months and find that while I like them, I prefer a competitor's product in terms of sound quality and the ability of the product to stay in my ear. I have tried the different options that come with them to get a better fit and stay in my ear tighter to no avail.

For outdoor activity, I cannot wear these. They fall out of my ear and I lose them. However, indoors I love the Alexa integration. If they could make them in a way they stay in my ear, they would be perfect. Last night, one fell out and went into the garbage disposer. Luckily, it was not on and water wasn't running or it would have been gone.

As they work loose quickly, sound quality and volume diminishes. They do have good bass response when tightly fitted in your ear. If I am sitting still listening to music or an audio book, they work great. As I start to move around, they loosen up and sound poor and are at risk of falling out.

Overall, I do have a use for them. I love the ability to use Alexa. I wish they could do Alexa independent of a mobile device via wi-fi, which they cannot. I love the ability to recharge them from the case when traveling. The case is hard shell and very protective of the earbuds. The case is probably the best part of the product.

This works.  It's the typical run of the mill bluetooth speaker, though.  The sound quality is fair.  It isn't great and it isn't bad.  The battery seems to last a good while.  I did have some trouble pairing, initially.  But after a few tries it took off and worked fine.  I use this for travel.
Poor picture quality, sound not very good!

I purchased this for two reasons: a convenient way to display recipes that didn't require my phone being out, and streaming movies for when I'm in the kitchen for hours at a time.

I rely heavily on streaming during the holiday seasons while I bake to fulfill orders, and while the video quality was good, and the sound was AMAZING, the rest of the device was too troublesome to be worth it.
Example: Open amazon video, and it gives you 4 categories to go through, or your library. I go to my library (severe lag every single time) and I find the movie I want. I hit play, severe lag again, and it plays. Quality is not bad at all, especially for the price, but heaven forbid you have to pause. Once you pause for ~2-3 minutes, it goes to a screen saver. And when you unlock it, you have to go through the process of finding the movie all over again. It's a pain in the butt. They could at least have a "continue watching..." at the beginning of the prime menu, but it doesn't.

Secondly, our household has 3 users on our hulu account--if there was a way to switch users through the Echo, I didn't see it. I googled it, thinking I was overlooking it, and nothing. We all have very different tastes for shows/movies, and never use each others accounts for this reason. To have not one, but two streaming services being out of the question/too inconvenient to use, I couldn't handle it.

The integration was wonky at best. I have an echo dot that resides on a window sill about 3 feet from where I had my echo. My echo was off for voice recognition, but when I'd talk to my dot, it would display on my echo. This was cool except for two things: 1. It did it intermittently. 1 out of 3 times it would mirror to the echo. 2. if you were streaming something when the echo mirrored what the dot was telling you, guess what, YOU HAVE TO FIND THE MOVIE AGAIN. It was a nightmare.

Maybe down the road they'll figure out a more user friendly programming for this, but until then I'm returning it. It was meant to be a gift for family, but if I, an electronic savvy 30-something, can't figure it out, I wouldn't be comfortable giving it to my grandparents, which was the end goal.

Update 5/2020:

When it comes to a wireless camera, it’s great. But the system often stops recognizing motion with no rhyme or reason, with the camera working just fine. You either have to turn the cameras off and back on or remove the battery, rebooting the system is too hit and miss for fixing the problem.

Also the AI leaves a lot to be desired, I have it set to not alert on vehicles and that’s 95% of the alerts we get.

The recognition software also stops working and you have to unsubscribe and resubscribe to get it to work again (only happened to me once).

We’ve only had the system for 6 months and there are days I’d rather be without it because it can be incredibly frustrating. That being said it was definitely better than having to hardwire a camera system

Original review: So far really great. Will update my review as time progresses but the alerts are quick, the sound quality is impressive, and the resolution is far greater than i anticipated from a wirefree setup. being able to see the calendar and click a date to see the videos from that day is really convenient, as well.

It works, but not well if you have a heavier phone. At least, I hope that's the reason.

Item boasts that it is appropriate for iPhone XR but it's finicky to say the least.

First, the prongs that go into the vent are very thick and i had to actually force my vent opening wider for this to fit. The holder has two different tensions, 1 and 2, so if 1 isn't holding it, 2 should. The problem is, when I had it on 1 it was falling off my vent and when i had it on 2 i had a heck of a time getting it to swivel at all, even after loosening the screw on the back of it.

To top it off, if I hit a bump and i had the phone angled up, it immediately slams down as far as it can go, generally hitting my radio dial and turning the radio off. I'm sure you're all thinking "Well, move it up to the top part of your vent," but just dangles oddly if I move it higher. If it's lower, it can at least rest against the dash slightly if I need it to.

If there's no phone in it, and the sound of plastic rattling drives you crazy, avoid it. It rattles so much when it's empty.

My car is too old to justify installing a bluetooth enabled stereo, and i hate having cords hanging everywhere to use the aux input. This little transmitter did the job, but unfortunately only for about two months.

It's a pain-free setup, and it does work, but I wouldn't buy it again, and I'd recommend a different route should you be in the market for one.

I've tried this in three different vehicles--in all three, the background static you get when it's transmitting is distracting. If it were quiet, I could ignore it but it's enough to interrupt anything I'm listening to. I've tried changing it to a multitude of empty radio stations, even tried it on a fully broadcasting radio station, and the static was horrible regardless.

Secondly, it is a pain in the butt to get out of the ashtray. The directions suggest you unplug it since it can drain your battery, but I had a heck of a time getting it out EVERY time. It had very tight contacts in all vehicles, to the point where if I don't gently wiggle it out, it can (and will) dislocate my ashtray drawer. That's a bit excessive in my opinion, as I've had other ashtray based devices with no tension issues like that.

I traded out my FIRST GENERATION Echo Pluses for two of these FOURTH GENERATION Echos. The sound quality was terrible in comparison to a model released YEARS ago. They did respond to my voice commands at more rapid rate, but for music, I feel like I just did a massive downgrade. The same goes for the Echo Dot 3 vs. 4. The entire 4th generation of Echo speakers seems like crap to me and I am so incredibly disappointed in Amazon. This makes me want to switch to Google smart speakers. I hope the next generation redeems these product lines.

Unfortunately, this product will not work from an optical source straight to a headphone jack on an external speaker. You still need one of the white and red audio wires that go into an independently powered block to convert sound to a 3.5mm audio jack. Basically, this cable is not capable of transferring the power necessary to successfully transfer sound from your optical port.

Bought this for my kitchen. The echo flex doesn’t always recognize me and perform the commands I ask. Often the commands are confused for something else. The sound isn’t very loud (we hoped it would compare to our echo dot without taking up counter space). Overall it’s just okay, but it comes in handy when it does work. I don’t know that I would buy another one again, but we make due with this one for now!

Pros:
Radio is surprisingly good.
Sound is quite good for such a small cube.
Overall, very sturdy design. Difficult to break.

Cons:
Playing mp3 from USB or MicroSD is not reliable. Sometimes it refuses to read media which works fine on other devices.
You have to turn off the annoying flashing light manually every time you turn it on. It would be much better if the light stayed off once you turned it off across power cycles.
The rechargeable battery is not replaceable.
Cheap but fun speaker.  Poor sound and low battery life but our kids love the minions so it served its purpose.

This radio has a nice compact size, about the size of a deck of cards. Reception is surprisingly good for a lightweight, relatively inexpensive radio. I live 30 miles from the radio stations that I listen to and stations are strong and clear. Sound quality through the speaker is good for talk radio (news, sports, etc), but too noisy for music.

My main complaint about this radio is that it uses 2xAAA batteries. The batteries are not included. Battery life is poor. If you listen to this radio regularly, you will need to replace the batteries every 1-2 weeks. In the modern era when everything is rechargeable, they really should have built-in rechargeable batteries and let you listen to the radio while the batteries are charging.

Also, the radio does have a clock feature and radio station presets, but the clock dies every time I change the batteries and the controls to set and use the presets are too confusing for me to figure out.

I like over-ear headphones. I find them to be more comfortable and better sounding than most on-ear or earbud headphones. These headphones are comfortable to wear, even on my larger head or when I am wearing glasses. They are not too heavy or too bulky when I am wearing them. I like that they fold up compactly for travel. I would prefer a hard case, but the included soft bag is better than nothing.

These headphones pair easily with the Bluetooth on my phone. I like that I can also use wired mode which I like to use when I'm watching movies on my PC.

The sound is clear and noise-free. It sounds natural in the midrange and higher frequencies. Bass is unfortunately mediocre compared to other over-ear headphones that I own. This is more important for rap or dance music than for pop or rock or classical music. Unfortunately, the included SXFI app does not work with streaming music. There is no equalizer app like many other headphones are including these days.

This mount is all plastic. I tried to use it with my Google Pixel 6 phone which I suppose is one of the bigger phones on the market right now. The mount does not work. The arms that grip the phone are too short to hold the phone securely, even when I'm not using a case. In addition, the arms push down on the phone's volume buttons, which interfere with the phone's camera functionality. Amazon sells other camera mounts that are all metal and much sturdier and also have bigger grip arms that work much better with my phone.

If you own OnePlus smartphone, these earbuds are easy to recommend. The budget-friendly $80 price matches the demographic that OnePlus has been cultivating. More importantly, some of the features of these earbuds only work with OnePlus phones. This includes Dolby Atoms and low-latency gaming playback.

Sound quality is clear, but very bass heavy. Unlike more better quality earbuds, these have no equalizer feature to help you get a more natural sound profile. Curiously, these earbuds do have the AAC CODEC for iPhones, but no aptX that Android phones prefer.

Noise cancellation is pretty good for this price range, though it does reduce your battery life somewhat. Battery life without noise cancellation is about average for the budget-price point, but not as good as what more expensive earbuds offer.

There is no wireless charging, though I'm not a huge fan of that anyway, especially for headphones.

I give 5 stars for OnePlus phone owners, but only 3.5 stars for everyone else.

At just $15, these earbuds are inexpensive, especially for a USB-C connector. They work OK with my Google Pixel 6 phone with clear audio and no minimal static. The sound isn't very rich, but no worse that expected for the $15 price. Build quality is good for $15, especially with the carrying case included. I'll use them for listening to sports and audio podcasts, but the sound quality isn't good enough for listening to music.

We have a couple of other pairs of binoculars; one cost $300 and the other cost $100. This set is far cheaper that our others and you get what you pay for. On the plus side, I have a larger face and I have no problem focusing these binoculars despite what some other reviewers say. However, despite the binoculars having adjustable eye cups, they are not adjustable enough for me to focus while wearing eye glasses. I have to take my glasses off then adjust the eye cups all the way out to get a clear image.

In bright sunlight, these binoculars give me a reasonably colorful and clear but not especially sharp image. There is some distortion and chromatic aberration, even in the center of the image. In lower light conditions, like around sunset when the wild animals I want to watch are more active, these binoculars give me dim image with poor detail. All compact binoculars degrade quickly in lower light conditions, but cheaper ones like this especially so.

The field of view is advertised as 342 feet at 1000 yards. That number is printed on the front of the binoculars. However, in use the field of view is much smaller than our Nikon 10x25 binoculars that also advertise as 342 feet field of view. These Pronite binoculars are semi-sharp and clear over a much smaller portion of the field of view than our Nikon as well.

In summary, you get what you pay for. These binoculars are near the cheaper end of binoculars that I would consider usable. They are somewhat usable, especially if you don't need great clarity. These binoculars can help you figure out which way a road or trail heads through the valley ahead. They may not be able to distinguish one species of bird from another if you are looking at the shape and colors of the bird.

I got a chance to try both the Soundcore A1 and Soundcore A2 earbuds. The price difference between these 2 models is relatively small, but I think additional features on the A2's is more than worth the price. The A1's might be a little over-priced at $60, while the A2's are a bargain at $80.

The A2's have noise cancellation, many more equalization settings that are easy to set via the smartphone app, upgradable firmware, and larger speaker drivers. The Soundcore smartphone app does not work with the A1's. All the extra features give the A2 earbuds noticeably better sound quality while also being easier to use. The A1's have decent sound quality, but there are a lot of $50 wireless earbuds that are just as good. On the other hand, the A2's feature and sound combination is better than any other $80 wireless earbuds that I have tried.

I am using these earbuds with my Google Pixel 2 phone's USB-C port. These are the cheapest USB-C earbuds that I own. They do not sound terrible. They are loud and not noisy. Musical quality is mediocre with worse clarity and worse bass than other USB-C headphones that i own. The earpieces don't fit all the way into my ear canals, so they do let in background sound, which is fine for listening to announcements on the train, but it also lets in noise that I don't want.

This adapter works fine to connect stereo speakers or headphones to my Google Pixel 2's USB-C port. Sound output is clear with only a little noise when I'm not playing anything. I'm only giving it 3 stars, however, because this is just as expensive as genuine Google or Apple USB-C adapters that are easily found for under $9 each. I don't see any point to buying generic products that are not significantly cheaper than the known brands.

This adapter works fine to connect stereo speakers or headphones to my Google Pixel 2's USB-C port. Sound output is clear with only a little noise when I'm not playing anything. I'm only giving it 3 stars, however, because the price is higher than genuine Google or Apple USB-C adapters that are easily found for under $9 each. I don't see any point to buying off-brand products that are more expensive than the known brands.

This adapter works fine to connect stereo speakers or headphones to my Google Pixel 2's USB-C port. Sound output is clear with only a little noise when I'm not playing anything. I'm only giving it 3 stars, however, because the price is higher than genuine Google or Apple USB-C adapters that are easily found for under $9 each. I don't see any point to buying off-brand products that are more expensive than the known brands.

There are a lot of different external camera microphones on the market, ranging in price from under $20 to hundreds of dollars. They differ in build quality, sound quality, and noise isolation. Compared to other microphones I have used, this one has average build quality and noise isolation for the price, but below average sound quality for this price level. Other microphones will give you a better dynamic range, especially when recording music or more than one person's voice. Still it is much better than the built-in microphones when using my cameras to record videos. It mounts easily on the camera's hot shoe. One non-rechargeable battery is included and this is required when using the microphone on most cameras.

These earbuds are small and light; very comfortable to wear. Volume is loud enough. Battery life is great. Unfortunately, sound quality is mediocre. There is decent bass, but higher frequencies are more muddy than crisp. Not very enjoyable for the music I like to listen to. Even at this budget price level, I rate these earbuds are below average because of the sound clarity.

These headphones are relatively inexpensive for build quality, compared to the name brands. They look and feel solid. Comfort is fine. Splashproof/sweatproof design is great for use outdoors or in a noisy gym. The bluetooth syncs quickly and easily with my Android smartphone. My phone shows the headphone power level so I can remember to recharge them. They conveniently fold up and fit into the included carrying bag. Actual sound quality is mediocre, as is typical of bluetooth headphones in this price range. Vocals are fine, but music detail is a little muddy. If you're looking for inexpensive comfortable over-the-ear headphones for use while jogging or working out or working in the yard, these are worth checking out. If you want to listen to music from a high quality player in a quiet room in your house, I think investing more money in your headphones is a good idea.

I also own and enjoy LG Tone and Motorola Buds necklace-style bluetooth earbuds. These iHome earbuds are cheaper than LG and Motorola, but you get what you pay for. Battery life on the iHome product is much worse than LG or Motorola (6-7 hours vs 10-12 hours) and long battery life is one of the main reasons I prefer the necklace-style earbuds vs the simpler styles. Music volume is louder on the iHome buds, but LG and Motorola were loud enough for me. At similar volumes, iHome has noticeably lower clarity than the other brands.

EDIT: Sony sent me a replacement unit under warranty because of the broken charger. The new unit works as advertised, so I'm upgrading my review to 3 stars. Some users may rate this more highly because of your needs. I give it 3 stars because they are difficult to use, uncomfortable to wear, have mediocre battery life, and are very expensive.

I wanted to give these a fair and thorough test, but unfortunately quality seems to be lacking and it died after just 2 days. First, the rubber ear tip on the right side kept falling off every time I took the earpiece out. Maybe I'm clumsy or maybe it is too fragile, but either way this is really annoying. Second, the battery life is terrible. The battery life indicator dropped from 70% to 30% after just 20 minutes of listening to music. Finally, the charger died. One of the little pins that connected the charger device to the earpiece broke off (or never was attached). Without it, I cannot recharge the right earpiece and since this is a non-standard charger, the whole thing is now useless.

Even if the headphones were 100% functional, here are some general thoughts:
1. Sound quality is very good for headphones that allow you to hear your surroundings. I don't have to take the headphones off to talk to someone standing next to me.
2. That is great because getting these things on or off is much more cumbersome than any other headphone I have ever tried.
3. The user manual really wants you to control these things using finger and head gestures. Maybe my memory is poor, but I can never remember all those things. Even when I'm reading the manual and trying to use the gestures, half the time they don't work.
4. This headset is expensive if all you can do is listen to music and phone calls. They are heavily advertising the "personal assistant" feature as well. The personal assistant feature asks for all kinds of permissions so it can read your messages and emails to you. After the recent Facebook hack, I am really reluctant to grant all these permissions.
5. The personal assistant works best if you have the headphones on all the time instead of just occasionally when you listen to music. However, the advertised battery life of these headphones is only 2-4 hours and my experience is less than that. Constantly recharging these things is a real hassle. Even taking them on and off several times a day is a real hassle.
6. The headphones are cumbersome to take on and off and wear and they are cumbersome entirely because they want to remove the wire between the 2 sides that cheaper headsets have. I don't think that tradeoff is worthwhile if you're not wearing these constantly and you can't wear them constantly because of the battery life.

These have pretty good sound for the price, though volume is a little weak, but I cannot get the hook things to work. I'm not a fast runner, but these keep falling out when I'm running and running is specified in the product description. Also, the long cord between the 2 ear pieces bounces around uncomfortably, no matter how I adjust the included tightening gizmo.

These are not great earbuds, but for the $20 price, they are average. Soft ear tips and angled ear pieces are comfortable to wear for long periods. The volume and pause buttons work properly with my Samsung Android phone, unlike most headphone controls that only work on iphone. The flat wires don't tangle as easily as thin round cables, but are still lightweight enough not to bounce around uncomfortably when running. Sound quality is mediocre, however. Bass is strong, but midrange lacks clarity. For about the same price, there are more popular brands with better sound quality (especially midrange clarity).

These are OK for the $20 price, but could be better. The short cable between the 2 ear pieces make these best for small-to-medium sized heads. I wear a size 7.5 hat (large, but not extra large) and the cable is too short to wrap around my ears like the advertising photo shows. Sound quality is only average with less clarity than in-ear type Bluetooth earbuds (available for about the same price on Amazon), though this type of headphone that doesn't fit all the way in your ear may be more comfortable for some people.

On the plus side, this headset pairs easily with my phone and is very compact and easy to store (unlike headphones with long wires that are always tangling or snagging). No case is included, however.

Some Bluetooth speakers cost more than $200. This one costs a fraction of that amount and has built-in clock radio and phone charging functions, so I tried to lower my expectations when trying it.

My first impression is that if you are not technically competent, you may have a real hard time using this device. Some assembly is required and if you are using an iphone, you will have to provide your own charging cable. The instructions are printed in tiny print on one big sheet of paper in 3 different languages, so you really have to focus to figure out how to configure this device. It is not too hard if you have previous Bluetooth experience, but first timers will have to be very patient.

As expected, the sound quality is mediocre; not awful, but noticeably lacking in clarity compared to other compact Bluetooth speakers. Maximum volume is also weak, though probably good enough for desktop or bedside use.

Even though this device is advertised as a "clock radio", be warned that it is FM only. News and sports are usually only on AM radio, so those are out. Also, I could not figure out from the instructions if there is anyway to use Bluetooth for the alarm clock function (playing music from your phone as your "alarm").

Finally, I find the phone charging connections to be somewhat clunky. The phone is essentially resting on the charging connection, which is not very stable and may or may not overly stress your phone. Why can't they include a sturdier cradle with this gadget? It does charge my phone quickly without having to use a separate wall charger. Note that the charging function only works if your charger port is on the bottom and center of your phone.

Summary: this device has lots of limitations, but also a moderate price that is probably suitable for the performance level

Additional thought: since all smartphones have good alarm clock functions already (not counting the iphone leap year bug), do you really need clock radio, especially one with no AM radio and mediocre sound quality? Mini-bluetooth speakers with better sound quality can be bought for cheaper prices than this.

I own one of these Soul bluetooth speakers as well as the Cambridge Soundworks Oontz Curve. Both are Bluetooth speakers with similar size and weight. Both have sturdy and good-looking metal shells. The Soul costs $20 and the Oontz costs $30 (both on Amazon right now). Both are very easy to pair with my Android smartphone. Both have similar volume levels, which is OK as a speakerphone or for background music, though neither will fill a living room with sound. Controls on both devices are similar; you really have to pick up the speaker to see and use most of the controls (forward/back, volume up/down, pause/play). The Oontz does have a well marked speakerphone button on the top, while the Soul puts that on the bottom with the other controls. I'm not an audiophile, but the Oontz has noticeably clearer sound to me at all volume levels. In summary, to me the Oontz is a better product in every way except for the 50% higher price, so you can make your own value judgement.

Reviews of this product are understandably mixed. Buy it because it has great features for the price, but don't buy it if you want a painless experience. The first one I got from Amazon was DOA. It would not produce sound (either through the speaker outputs or the headphone jack) no matter what I did. Tried updating the firmware, rewiring the inputs, etc with no luck. Returned it to Amazon, which is a big hassle because of the size of the box. Second unit worked OK for a while, then started having problems with the HDMI video freezing up (sound was OK). Updated the firmware again. If you update the firmware, make sure you completely unplug the power cord for 15 minutes (don't just press the power button). Updating the firmware is a minor hassle because you cannot do it by WiFi, only by USB flash drive. Unit seems to work fine now, crossing my fingers. If you do buy this, make sure you have enough time to baby it for a while (possibly months). Don't buy it for your grandmother unless you want her to call you regularly for help. Note that used units are sold for half price here on Amazon. Avoid those at all costs because of the chance of a DOA unit that is out-of-warranty.

The polarizer glass in this filter is questionable quality and can cause distortion or glare. Do yourself a favor and get the threaded version of this product for $30 directly from Carry Speed. Then you can screw in your own high quality filters. With the threaded version, you are not limited to polarizer filters. ND filters are very useful, especially for video. You can also mount hoods, which are very useful in many situations.

The description makes these speakers sound interesting for general purpose use. Since they are USB powered, you don't need a separate power outlet and charger for them. Just plug them into your laptop's USB port and you're good to go. Even when you don't have a power outlet, you can run them off you laptop's battery (for some period of time).

Unfortunately, they don't live up to expectations. These speakers are kind of bulky, with 2 large pieces and a big collection of wires. They won't fit into slimmer briefcases and will take up a good amount of space no matter what bag you put them in to. Sound quality is mediocre. They are fine for listening to spoken voices, like video conferencing or podcasts. They are probably also fine for computer game sound effects. Music quality is poor at medium or higher volumes, though.

The low price might might make them attractive to someone who uses their computer in one place most of the time and doesn't care too much about portability. Just don't expect much sound quality.

I got the HD 8 as a replacement to my old Kindle keyboard that died on a camp trip. I had such high hopes this device would fit the bill. I am not going to go into the nitty gritty of pros and cons but will sum up my experience highlights.

- the Audio performance is amazing. It is a quantum improvement from the audio I get on my iPad Mini. The sound experience is really something Apple should strive for. It did knock my socks off.

- setup was easy and efficient, but I think the OS and maybe even the device has problems. I have had to call tech support about twice a day on days I use the device. It is usually a lockup or hang or feature that does not work. I think I have isolated the problem to the fact the device can't keep the OS stable on battery. They always have me plug the device into the adapter for any support call (regardless of its charge level) and it always starts behaving itself once it is on DC power vs battery. I have also seen it burn through battery pretty fast at times. Not sure what it is doing but it ate 10% sitting on standby in my pack on the commute to work this morning!

- I do think the read aloud smarts have been improved since the older model (kbd) as it reads much cleaner now for me. (Less stops, more in the right locations, etc).

My end-game is that I will probably return it. If it does not work reliably on battery then it is not a mobile device. Period.

Major dependency - you better have port X.X.X.254 open on your network; it parks there when it boots and that's where you have to get it to configure it to reside elsewhere if that's your plan.  If (like me) you had another device using that port, then you're hosed until you can either free it up, or make up another network for it to be born in, so you can configure it with a static IP to work cooperatively with the rest of your network.  It is so promising and at less than $30 a pop it's an amazing option but the UI is nothing as seamless to configure as an Apple Airport Express/Extreme.  Really hoping when I finally get it functional - it will prove itself reliable.

Its neat for this price.  Plugs directly to aux out.  Has colorful lights on front.  Groovy volume knob for setting just the right sound.  Its very affordable and probably great for kids.  Have mine plugged in front of the 32in Tv.

I use the walkies in the house to communicate with my disabled family member.  The sound quality is good,  but I have to charge them everyday which is inconvenient.  It is better than replacing with new batteries all the time though.  Just wish they would last a little longer before having to charge.
The sound is a bit staticy and lacks bass.

The sound GREAT! The range is CRAP!

I have a Sounsblaster Roar that I use as my primary BT speaker for outside. This thing sounds like a mini version of that, but I literally have to be in the same room as the speaker to use the BT.

3 STARS.
This works but I can barely hear the audio even though both my phone and car volumn are turned up high.

Based on Vizio M65 - C1 4K Ultra Smart TV with 240 Htz.

As a few others I have experienced the picture going black on the set after a few hours of operation followed by in my case a loud snapping noise. I lowered my rating based only on this phenomenon . Amazon as always stood by the sale and made everything more than right . IF it had not been for the going to black concern , my rating would have been five stars .Contacting Vizio resulted in being asked to perform a bunch of resets and chanting magic incantations ( joke ) . That was considered when raring the product too. When not going black , the picture is amazing ! Sporting events in particular pop off the screen and the detail seen is incredible. First time ever my cable box has registered 1080P . I can't speak to the 4K aspect as I have not attempted to watch anything in that range . The black range is as crisp as I have ever seen on any set. Setup is very easy and uncomplicated. The remote includes a key pad on the back to make entering information and searching easier. Again , would be a five if not for the picture going black issue.

Con: The speakers are tiny and are facing the rear . Not sure why they choose to go the cheap route and skimp on the sound. By no stretch am I an audiophile but one does notice the lack of depth to the sound and the volume level needs to be up to hear dialog clearly. A sound bar is almost a requirement and I did see that some retailers are packaging one with their Vizio TV'S to,address this concern.
The remote has a quick access buttons for Amazon , Netflix and of all things IHeart Radio. They must have got a kick back from I Heart . The quick connect feature loose a plus for choosing I Heart. Hulu or the like would have been a better choice .

I would not be afraid to buy this set. I would strongly suggest that the purchase be supported by a vendor you trust and will support the sale after the fact. Some of these are through a third party and directly through Amazon . I always select the direct Amazon route because of the support after the sale. I needed it in this instance and as always was not disappointed by Amazon customer service.

Good sound for the money and does what I expected. Skip to the summation if you are looking for reasons not to purchase.

Might be a better choice especially if you own a Panasonic TV as the set up is designed for a Panasonic product line. I had to use their support call service a few times and as most companies today, some are very good and can understand and help, but most will read a prewritten script and hope they hit on the problem you are experiencing. Cons: Had to go buy after market speaker wires due to the lack of length that comes with the system and splice the wires to place the rear speakers. Also had to buy an audio connector to allow the system to produce TV sound. This really ticked me off and Panasonic should really step up and correct these issues. The system also needs to modernize and add another HDMI connection ( and the cable ...really? ) to allow for a cleaner install. Another con is the system will not produce sound while watching the Internet based VUDU movie channel. Panasonic wanted me to buy another movie and call them to "try" some fixes while the movie played! It does work with my cable provided paid movie service. The system would also not work with my top of the line wireless router and had to buy a cable and run wires to their system. One must also buy another adapter ( Dingle) to receive wireless signals that may or may not work or a connecting cable. Check to see see the distance from your router to the system and if it is physically possible to fish the wire to the sound system from the router before you buy the cable.

Summation: "You get what you pay for". If you can splice wires and figure out how to add cables to make TV audio work and the internet work then it's ok. You will need to spend more money on items that should be included from Panasonic and it is best to own a newer Panasonic TV for easier installation. Panasonic kind of ruined what should be a great experience by cutting corners to save money on wire and connections. Panasonic should provide more installation on information "needs" as part of their product description if they aren't not going to provide long enough speaker wire, HDMI connectors and inputs,or audio cables,or internet Dingle or cable.

This is a moderately high-end headset with a price to match. The manufacturer claims that it supports multiple devices at the same time, that it has a long range of 490 feet, that the battery charge lasts "all day," which most of us would interpret as 8-12 hours or more, and that it has a noise-cancelling microphone and enhanced speakers to create "crystal-clear calls" in noisy work environments.

I have tried to pair it to both my phone and TV transmitter at the same time, and the TV transmitter does pair if the phone is paired. The range isn't as far as advertised. The battery charge lasts about 4-6 hours. It has excellent sound quality for receiving calls and listening to TV, but persons on the other end of a phone call often complain that they have trouble hearing me, so the mic doesn't work very well. This headset is really uncomfortable to wear, making it difficult to use it more than an hour. Also, be aware that the rechargeable battery is not replaceable when it dies.

I actually have a headset with similar functions that cost me about 1/5th the price, so I'm not convinced this product is worth the extra money.

I got these headphones because I tend to put the TV on much louder than is comfortable for my husband, and the price was quite affordable. (That is to say, cheap.) Unfortunately, the saying, "You get what you pay for," applies in spades to my experience with this product.

I could not get the headphones hooked up by myself, and my husband, who is an IT guy, had to fiddle with them on and off over several days. He finally had to buy an [[ASIN:B000068O51 adapter]] to get it to work with our TiVo and TV combination, but while he could use the earphones once hooked up with little static, this was not the case for me. I had lots of static problems.

Here are the instructions we figured out to make it work with a TiVo, as well as it can be made to work once it is hooked up:

1. Pick up the headphones and the remotes for the TV and TiVo.
2. Stand directly in front of the TV.
3. Turn on the transmitter for the headphones.
4. Turn on the remote headphones by spinning the volume control dial on one side of the headphones. You might hear or feel a click when you spin the dial. A red light on the headphones will come on when they are turned on.
5. Press the Reset button on the headphones.
6. Put your finger on the Scan button on the remote headphones so you will know where it is.
7. Put the headphones on.
8. Press the Scan button.
9. You should now hear the sound of the TV through the headphones.
10. If you do not hear the TV, press Scan again until you hear the TV through the headphones.
11. You control the volume in the headphones with the volume dial on the side of the headphones.
12. You should turn the TV volume all the way down (or very low) using the TV remote since the TV remote does not control the volume of the headphones.

I rate this product as follows:

Ease of installation: 1 star
Ease of Use: 4 stars
Effectiveness of Product: 4 stars for IT husband, 2 stars for me, average 3 stars
Overall rating: 2.7 rounded to 3 stars

The most important thing to me about wireless headphones is range. It seems that the tech is not quite there yet. I see in some reviews that people are able to still be connected a couple rooms away in their house. I did not get this same result. Comfort and fit are top notch. I really could wear these all day. I do not run but I would imagine they would be rock solid and stay in place. I wanted to love these. I really wanted to love these. However the range is just not realistic (at least in the pair I had). If I set my phone down and walked more than a 5 feet away they cut out completely. If I put the phone in my pocket they cut out completely. My phone is a Galaxy S7 Edge. Sound when in range is good but the limitations in range are not realistic for everyday use. My search for a pair of bluetooth headphones continues. If you want to use these at your desk with your phone right in front of you I think you will be happy.

I used these while my husband was training out of state for a length of time. Both of the ones I used worked great the first night, but one went off by itself the second evening. Luckily, it was early enough to where it was still light out, and I was standing in the next room facing that direction when it went off. Otherwise, it would have scared the %$%@ out of me, thinking someone was near the door or trying to break in. I could see there was no one there, nor had there been when it first went off. The evening was still, there was no wind nor vibration, so I don't know what made it go off.  It does make a loud alarm sound, and it doesn't stop until you turn it off, so I'll give it that! It may have just been a fluke, but I didn't feel comfortable using it again. If I would have been in bed or asleep and it went off, I would have totally freaked!  I would suggest going ahead and trying these, but don't rely on them being perfect and be prepared just in case they go off by themselves.  I went ahead and went with a security system company, just to put my mind at ease.  It you can't do that at this time, I would give these a try.

It provided better overall sound for my anemic older Vizio TV. However, several issues make it quite different from other "soundbar" types. If you program your Comcast remote to use the Zvox functions,it hijacks other functions that control your TV! I have my headphones connected to the audio out, and now I cant use my Comcast remote to control them or any normal Vizio audio functions without turning off the Zvox manually. OL barely works as commercials are still as loud as ever. I still have to turn it up to get a decent level on shows,and theres quite a bump up in sound between 17-18!
