(Update: Since writing this, the listing title and product description has been revised to reflect it's not a 2-in-1 and doesn't have a touchscreen. The price has been reduced too.)

I saw "M2" in the model number, so I got a bit excited thinking this computer might have an M.2 slot for an SSD card. Before I even booted it up the first time, I took the bottom off and checked to see if it had that slot. No. No, it doesn't.

It does have a DVD drive, which might be a big plus for you. It also has a couple of USB 3 ports, a USB C port, an HDMI port, an Ethernet port, and a card reader.

You might be a little confused by how much RAM it has installed. It has 8GB. That "Optane" memory mentioned in the listing isn't RAM.

The display is 1366 X 768p, which is called "HD," but in these days of "full HD" and "ultra HD" and "mega-turbo HD" and super-tight pixel densities (or pencil dixities, which are important too, I think), 768p on a 15-inch monitor is starting to look a little 640 X 480-ish, if you know what I mean. 1366 X 768 is okay, not bad, it's certainly usable, but it's a bit of a sag to have a new laptop with what looks in comparison like lower res than is practically standard for devices now.

An IdeaPad isn't a ThinkPad, so it doesn't have that traditional trackpoint in the keyboard. But the keyboard has a nice light touch and the brushed aluminum palm rest feels smooth and cool. And it has a full tenkey pad.

Audio is good from the built-in speakers, a bit louder than most laptops, which is good.

Now I would write a few comments about Windows (Windows 10 comes installed on this machine), but I think it would quickly devolve into a rant. I haven't used Windows in months, having gone all in on Linux. So after a few moments noodling around with Windows on this laptop (and dismissing several popup notifications and ads in the corner, some of which appeared to be sourced from Lenovo, not Windows), I started making a recovery drive so I could try a complete wipe of the 1TB HD (which is a "hybrid" HD, a combination SSD and mechanical spinning HD, so you get a combination of SSD type speeds for boot or for wakeup and regular HD economy for storage) and install a Linux distro.

So I gave it a try and it's a no-go for me for now. The Debian Linux installer I tried didn't even recognize there was a 1TB HD in the IdeaPad. The problem, it seems, is that hybrid drives are often controlled using software and BIOS settings instead of a hardware RAID controller (which is needed to allow multiple HDs to operate as a single drive). And that apparently makes it difficult for a Linux installer to find the HD.

In order to install Linux on a hybrid HD like that, apparently you have to boot a Linux distro live from a flash drive or CD then go in and repartition everything. I didn't want to risk doing something irreversible right now, so I'm setting that plan aside.

Despite my gripes it's a decent computer with good specs and performance and it looks really nice.

This is a truly wireless security camera system. The cameras operate on four CR123 batteries each, and lithium-ion batteries are included. That's a big plus, because you can install the cameras most anywhere. Setup took me a little over an hour.

It might be costly to replace lithium-ion batteries regularly, so you might consider getting rechargeable batteries.

The cameras are not pan-tilt-zoom cams. They're fixed. But the mounts are little metal domes, so you can manually aim the camera most any way you choose. The cameras have strong magnets in them to stick them firmly to the mounts. You can also stick the cameras to any steel or iron surface. You might keep in mind that since they're only held by magnets, the cams could be stolen easily if located in easy reach.

You start setup by downloading and installing the Arlo app on your device (phone, tablet, etc.) Then you create an account, agree to the terms, and follow the on-screen instructions for setup. The free version of the app supports up to six cameras.

The Netgear Arlo camera receiver/router connects to your Internet router with an Ethernet cable. It has a wall power supply with a six-foot cord. After it establishes a connection with the Internet router, you then pair the cameras, one by one, with the camera router. That takes about twenty seconds each.

This is where annoying things started. The app has motion detection on by default. Six cameras started slamming my email inbox and notification banner with motion detection alerts. It took a while to find the switch to turn motion detection off. You get to it by clicking on "mode" at the top, then the name you gave your camera system, then click on "disarm."

There's no batch delete feature in the app (not one I could find anyway) to delete all those motion detection videos at once. I had to go through and delete them one by one.

Notifications said the base unit and all the cams needed firmware updates. The update for the base unit went smoothly. The camera updates did not go so smoothly. Almost all of them said "update failed - camera rejected upgrade request." I moved the cameras close to the base unit and retried the updates, one camera at a time. Success.

These cameras do not continually take pictures, which is probably a battery saving feature. They start taking video or pictures only when motion detection is triggered, or when you manually click on "live" on each camera's thumbnail picture. The live stream takes several seconds to start. So the best setting for security would be motion detection active, but that might mean a lot of notifications. If you want to just take a look at the cameras to see what's up currently, that's kind of a problem. Each camera has to be started, and there's several seconds of wait time. (Edited to add: Adding to the wait time is that it appears video clips are not stored locally but rather uploaded to the manufacturer's site then downloaded back to your device.)

Let me put it this way: If motion detection is switched off and you hear the sound of a varmint on your porch and you want to take a quick look or grab a quick snapshot with one of these cameras, that's just not going to happen. You have to rely on motion detection being on to take the pictures for you. With motion detection off, at best you'll be able to take a look after several seconds of camera startup and buffering. (Edited to add: And if the varmint is moving quickly, you may not get a picture of it at all---just the motion detection alert and a short video that didn't capture what set the alert off.)

In contrast, I have three IP cameras that are always on. I can open the app for them and see a live picture from all three cams at once and grab a snapshot from any of them. But they all require hard-wired power, so it's a trade-off.

When you start the app, you see thumbnails from the last time you ran the live streams, or from the last motion detection. Those thumbnails can be hours old. I don't know if it would be possible, but if the Arlo app and cams had a "refresh all thumbnails" feature, that would be a big help in getting a current look at all your cameras. Then you could start live streams if you choose to.

For some reason the app will only support running five live streams out of the six cameras. You have to stop one of the streams to start the sixth.

If you install the Arlo app on more than one device, only one can be logged in and viewing cams at a time.

(Edited to add: A couple of other issues with the app: If you haven't opened the app in a while, you may get a notice that your login token has expired and you have to re-enter your password. More seconds lost if you got a motion detect alert and want to take a quick look. And sometimes you have to dismiss an ad before you can go look at the cams. And on my Kindle Fire, the Arlo app tends to go into some sort of loop sometimes, and I have to shut down and reboot the device.)

Picture quality is good. It can be set to lower resolution to maximize battery life, or medium or high resolution. The cams also have a night vision mode that can be switched off individually using the app. This is handy if you want to position the camera to look out a window at night. If the night vision mode is on, the IR led will reflect off the window at night like a bright light. Turning off night vision mode will avoid that. However, this still requires the exterior to be well lit or to have an outdoor IR source. The cameras' built in IR illumination isn't long range. It will light an average size room though.

The manufacturer says the cameras are weatherproof and can be positioned outdoors.

The web site says the cameras have a 300-foot range line-of-sight. One camera I placed about fifty feet from the router had difficulty connecting. It seems that the number of walls and other items between the camera and the router can have a big effect on connection, which isn't unusual with any wireless devices.

I think for a basic security system, IP cameras might have a few advantages over this system. But this system has its points, such as install-anywhere convenience and fairly simple setup. For actual security, keeping the system motion-detection armed and just letting the cameras grab and upload pictures and the app send notifications is the best solution, I would think. If you want to monitor live pictures yourself, or even just glance at very current pictures from time to time, I'd think this system wouldn't be a workable solution.
Sound quality is better than expected for this price range.  They already broke though.

I really wanted to love this tablet. Unfortunately, the screen is just so awful that I was constantly annoyed. I loved the sound, using swype on the keypad and being able to cast the screen to my tv from the menu, but I couldn't handle the poor quality graphics. I tried any number of settings, contrast, changing the sharpness, nothing helped. Images always seemed to have a haze to them. Black text was just slightly grey, and the blacks were not crisp and smooth edged in images.

I tried it out for almost two weeks, and the final kicker was trying to view book previews (look inside) on Amazon. The images would flash for a second, then blank out like the graphics were too much for the tablet to process. No issues on my Nook HD or even my son's $39 no-name tablet.

Another problem was finding a cover to fit. This tablet, model number ending in 046US, the A8-40f, is about a half inch narrower than the 025US A8-40. I'd ordered a case from a seller that stated it would fit this model, but it did not.

I would like to give this a five rating but it is still too quirky to receive that. I deducted a star for each major problem-no control over storage and what appears to be an unstable OS. I switched from another android tablet that was giving me problems. My brother has the largest Kindle Fire HD and it looked very nice. I paid extra to get rid of the ads because they were too obtrusive. One would pop in while I was doing something and shut down that app. I wanted a device for reading e-books and listening to audio books. I also wanted something that had external storage that I could manage. Wrong. The app saves to the external storage card but the downloaded content goes directly to the device storage which makes no sense. Why have an external storage option when none of the larger content files will save to it? The sound is more treble than bass, but it sounds good. My device is only 8 GB, so it max'ed out quickly when I downloaded content. I like the thin form factor. This cuts down the amount of weight in my bag. I got the magenta with a purple cover. Maybe it is because this is the first time I am using it, but the OS is very jumpy and the screen is not as responsive as I would like. I have to tap several times to open an app or play a song. Once I figured it out, downloading from my accounts was easy. Unfortunately when I tried to view my internal content, the device went into a loop, then restarted itself and that took a long time. If I ever am able to download to my SD card as the instructions say, then I will be happy to upgrade my review. In the meantime, I am disappointed that this is not able to do what I wanted.

I saw this item in the military sales store and I thought it looked cool. It is an ereader, MP3 player and a video player. I only wanted an ereader with a better screen that my Sony Touch PRS600. The Sony Touch would have been excellent except for the terrible screen. This device is so much bighter and easier on the eyes. If only setup and installation of apps and ebooks were as easy,...

First, I must say I am computer savvy and I know how to set up new devices. This is not anything like an iPad, which some people seem to have issues with. I do not believe this device was meant to compete in that market. This is considerably less expensive and, therefore, we are getting what we paid for.

I really only wanted an ereader, but I did test the MP3 player. It has good sound through the headphones, and the speakers are not bad for a small device. The video player plays well, but I was not expecting it to be as good as my iTouch.

One con with this device is there is not much on board storage. It advertises 2GB, but the instruction guide admits there is really only 1GB accessible by the user for storage of media. I downloaded the Kindle for Android app and began to rebuild my library. I have so many books and I will max out the internal storage very soon. One way to make room on board is to drag and drop items from the internal storage to the SD card. Thankfully, it accepts up to an 8GB card (It may accept a larger card but mine is 8GB). That turns the con into a pro because I will certainly need the space.

My touch screen is responsive. If I don't want fingerprints smudging the screen, I can use my fingernail. Although the instruction guide does not mention the stylus, it does come with a small one. If anyone can tell me where I am supposed to store it, I would appreciate it. Right now I leave it at home for fear of losing it. I have another that has a cord so I can hang it on the edge of the slip case, which is quite sturdy and will protect the screen well.

I set up my Adobe Digital Editions account in my PC and activated the device after it was recognized by the software. That was pretty easy to do. I store all my pdf books on the SD card. It requires an additional steps of accessing my books through the Explorer app/SD card/digital editions. The Sony lists all documents or lists directly on the first screen.

The device has a Wi-Fi locater which works well. I went to several local free hot spots and the device detected them quickly. It does get a little quirky if you move from hot spot to hot spot because it has to locate and remember each spot.

I watched some reviews on YouTube and I think my device must be an updated version. The ebook pages turn quickly and the page auto flip function is a nice display. It is almost like turning a paper page.

The preloaded photos and ebooks are standard. The ebooks are 25 free classics you can get just about anywhere online. The preloaded photos are okay and I can add my own to store. There are three classical music clips to demonstrate the sound. The preloaded video is a marketing tool, okay for checking the screen clarity.

The battery life is fine if Wi-fi is turned off when not in use. Keeping Wi-fi on will drain the battery quickly.

One complaint was that it was heavy for an ereader. I believe the heft comes from the slip case. The device itself is very light.

Overall, I like this device, considering it was half the price of the Sony Touch ereader and has many more functions to include Internet connectivity. Although I still prefer my Apple iTouch for watching videos and listening to music, I like the option of loading other media on board, just in case. Recommended for those who want something inexpensive and smaller than a netbook or iPad to fit inside purses or briefcases.

If you don't mind abysmal customer service, then skullcandy is for you!

I tried to get them replaced and get skullcandy to honour their warranty. They ignored several of my emails for about 3 months. I called them out on twitter. Still nothing. In the end, they waited out the warranty and then told me the warranty had expired. Same thing happened to my daughter. And then to my husband.
Basically after they get your money, you are on your own. As long as you keep that in mind, you will be fine.

So I will see how long it takes this time for one to shorten out and them to ignore me. 👍
very cute and hangs around. sound quality not better than the phone. buy for novelty.

It works right out of the box; nothing to set up. It feels very cheaply made, though. I have a Roku so I only needed it for the volume buttons. It does what I want.

The pics of the Cabor Small Wireless Headphones looked like a couple other pairs I've owned, and I was looking for a new set, so I ordered them.

Unlike my other wrap-around outside ear headphones, these came coiled up. When I gently pulled them open and put them on, they shot off my head as they coiled back up. There's no way to stretch them out - they coil back up if you put them down. As a result, I find they're very fiddly to put on, and while I can get them on both ears so they don't come off, I couldn't run in them or do something active that involved leaning over repeatedly.

Soundwise, these were pretty good - not great, but definitely not bad. I didn't find the sound tinny or weird but pleasant, and very good for audiobooks. Once I found the tiny light, I found these headphones super easy to pair. The buttons are easy once you get used to them, but black buttons with black letters isn't the easiest to read.

My charger cable arrived dead, but we have so many cables that fit this headset that it wasn't a problem. By the way, the light on this headset is very small, and from some angles you might not realize it's on.

Overall this is an okay headset, but next time I'll buy a set that doesn't want to coil up every time you let go of it.

Ok, I loved these speakers, especially the option of controlling the volume with a button on the side, but they stopped working after a year. Not sure what made them stop working, but we were sad to loose them because of the great sound quality.

Nice set of bluetooth earbuds.  However,  I have very small ear canals.  Unfortunately, none of the rubber pieces are small enough to stay in my ears.  I did have some luck with the malleable foam, but I will likely have to keep checking them and pushing them further in every couple minutes I use them.  They do sound pretty good.

I was hoping for better earbuds than these.  The sound is pretty average, when you compare them to similarly priced headphones.  The noise canceling feature works fairly well, I can crank my music up to cover the sound of my son playing the xbox 360.  What I don't like is the comfort.  Smaller buds  would improve this I think.  I have them the smallest ones on them and they're still too big to fit comfortably (I have been told my ears canals are quite small though).  I need more bass.

Unfortunately I found these to be VERY uncomfortable.  They don't stay put in my ears, even though I switched to a smaller size.  The sound is just so-so.  Consequently, I gave these to my 11 year old daughter, who is using them to watch movies on her iPad.  I do have to say (and this is why I give it 3 stars) that the noise canceling works rather well.  Usually my daughter uses my awesome voice canceling Sennheiser earphones and can hear me pretty well still while we're in the car.  Yesterday she used these in the car, and I had a much harder time getting her attention.

I bought these from Costco, and was very impressed with the sound as well as the noise canceling capability.  However, after listening for about 30 seconds, it just shuts itself off.  Then it may or may not start again, only to have them shutdown another 30 seconds later.  I'm taking them back today for a refund.  In its place I bought Sennheiser pxc450 and am amazed.  They also are extremely well made, comfortable, and have amazing noise canceling features.  Anyway, I would've kept the Sony if they had worked correctly.

Is not soft plastic, one has to apply quite a bit of force to fit the Ipod in, the corners are the worst part.
And in order to increase or decrease volume you have to press very hard.

Was quiet cumbersome to install and there were two instruction manuals which were not exactly aligned so was confusing. Also mine had a slight dent (just little) but noticeable when screen is off. However I love the feel it is paper like especially with the sound.

I got this to use as a second monitor. It's not that great. The colors aren't bright and the images aren't all that crisp and clear. The power switch is pretty cheesy as well, I can see it going out before the monitor. It serves it's purpose as a second monitor but I would never use it as a main monitor.

It was easy to set up and connect to my phone and laptop. Projector met all my needs with the exception of  producing quality sound, you can barley hear.  Picture is nice but the sound.  I wish I could hook up to firestick

This record player is mostly my husbands. We listen to very different music. He's more Zeppelin, I'm more not. However, we both have our vinyls. This one is portable so he can use it wherever his little heart desires. I asked him to give me a few words about it after he used it for a bit and here is what he had to say about it:

"This is very attractive in the form of a suitcase with a neat clasp to keep your record player safe. Plus it's a record player and to this day vinyl is better than everything else, especially digital.
It has Bluetooth and a headphone jack. It can play your records and has an automatic stop. All this stuff is great and I want to really like this. Alas, there are some drawbacks. Firstly, and not of major importance to me personally, the Bluetooth has a bit of trouble connecting. I was trying to connect to a Google pixel 3 and though it does create a connection that's about all it does.
Secondly, the speakers really aren't all that good. The test of this was with Zeppelin 2 playing and when it just doesn't do John Paul Jones any justice then it just doesn't cut it.
You need to add speakers or get it connecting to something with a decent sound because no, just no.
I left it at a three because instead of being a really good record player it sort of turned into a half decent novelty item. For the price I can't really complain too much but if you really want to hear vinyl then try another record player."

There you have it folks. His opinion on the player. I will say one thing though. He's not really good with connecting Bluetooth devices so take that part of his review with a grain of salt. I tried to tell him to attempt to connect one of the little Bluetooth speaker things we have all over but he just wanted to try it on his phone. So I would check other reviews and see what others say about that first, just in case. Other than that the rest is pretty much how he feels and stuff. So, there you have it!

For an off-brand, it was okay. I would rather spend more money and get a higher quality player. I've actually paid less for a Sony one.

Remote control issues, some sound issues.

Since 2010, every time I’ve bought a new laptop, I’ve bought a new wireless mouse. I don’t like using the one on the laptop as it is too awkward and clunky for me.

The mice I prefer – Logitech. The most recent one I got was: Logitech M317 – Amazon code B08L8SRJRR; white with purple/pink side grip, flowers on top. Though I did get it from Staples (the branding is shortened to Logi).

To me, the brand doesn’t matter – I do try to keep my equipment the same, but the Logitech ones have never let me down. They’re also better shaped for my hand, though the ones of the last decade are smaller, which I LOVE. Last year when I got a new laptop for my birthday, I got the new little Logi listed above.

I saw another HP mouse on here, the HP 930 Creator, and though that would be awesome. It wasn’t. I was quite disappointed. Not that I didn’t like my Logi, I though the HP would be a bit better. And, the 930 was over $67. Many problems, but the main one – size. Far too big for me in height and width.

I saw this and thought it might be better than the 930 – was certainly simpler. I love the FLAT design. It’s about half the height of my Logi.

This, like the 930 has a width problem, thus small hands and those with dexterity issues will have some problems “getting a grip”.

Another issue with this – you need BLUETOOTH capabilities.

Function?

Connection: After turning on my computer’s BLUETOOTH, the mouse connected in under 5 minutes

Sound: A bit quieter than my Logi, as well as the 930 Creator

Scroll: A bit slower than the Logi, definitely slower than the 930

Battery Replacement: Logi – on the bottom, like usual; 930 (rechargeable through USB). This? The battery is on the TOP. You have to remove the top black plate to put the battery in. This is the feature I dislike the most considering how THIN the plastic piece is. Depending on the amount of force used – it could easily get broken.

Currently priced at $39.76, this is definitely a bit overpriced. I am not fond of it, and definitely wouldn’t get a replacement.

UPDATE: As of 3/26, the mouse keeps losing Bluetooth connectivity sometimes in as little as 15 minutes of non-use. I don't know if this is normal with the Bluetooth mouse, but it is definitely annoying especially when I have to reconnect.

I’m always up for finding cutesy phone protectors, and my newest phone (iPhone 11) has a lot of them on the market as opposed to my previous phone.

That’s not why I got my new phone though – the other one was dying in certain areas.

I loved the idea of this case, but in all honesty, it isn’t practical. It is about double the size of the other “snap” cases I had. There is a liquid bubble that developed after a day of having it. The sand is barely visible in this case.

Another problem? When the case is held, it tends to have a “cracking” sound when you touch it – at least mine does.

I’d honestly be afraid of dropping it, it cracking, and the sand/water getting into my device.

This is cute for display, but not functional for me.

As one major manufacturer has stopped their sales, and my mom has always wanted one of these – I decided to grab this as it is similar in style and size to the iPod Nano I still have.

This relies on an SD card for memory and no software – just transfer your music files from the computer to the micro SD card, which can be expanded by popping in a bigger one.

The problem is not really transferring files – it is the lack of user friendly interfaces. This also had ZERO instructions and I was forced to spend a few hours trying to get this “user-friendly” for my mother.

I am still TRYING to get it user friendly even after six weeks. I’m sure it won’t take that long, but I do have other things I need to do.

This would probably be best as a backup player for someone who is active and wants to take their music with them.

It is giftable in a box with everything needed and relies on a USB for file transfer as well as charging.

I have a few Timex alarms and watches and they have always been exceptional except this one.  Though I love the large display and plugging in my ipod, the quality of the music is just not there.  Also, the volume blasts randomly and it pretty much knocks me out of bed with a headache.  Other times the volume is so low that i turn it up and about 10 minutes, it blasts.  It's just unstable volume control.  It's easy enough to set the alarm and the time.  I like being able to control the display light to make it brighter or dimmer.  Timex is quality for a reasonable price so I am surprised that this alarm does not meet their or my standards.  The radio stations are full of static or some I can't even get although my other radios I have no problem getting the stations on them.  If you just want a standard alarm with a large display, this is good.  If you want to wake up to the radio, i would think twice...it might blast you out of bed or the volume might be so low that you wouldn't hear it.

The sound on these is as good as connected open air buds I have but they do not adhere well. They fit around my ears just fine but because the bud doesn’t go in the ear and it didn’t have the wire to add some needed weight. So kind of useless most of the time. The battery life is good and the case charges additional time.

I really wanted to love these. They have excellent battery life and the sound is excellent. I like that if I walk out of range for awhile and when I come back they connect automatically most of the time. However sometimes the volume will go up.
But the sensors are just awful and basically useless. If I want to play/pause I almost always have to do it on my device.

Many of the head bands have been improved for size and easier charging. This has a Velcro strap to adjust for any size to make this a comfortable fit. Some bands have the charging port at the control panel. This one has it on a wire that can be pulled through a slip in the fabric. However this ends up having it be uncomfortable to sleep on your side. You can push the plastic piece to the front but it might not stay put.
I also don’t like the control buttons, they are hard to use.
The sound on this is pretty good.
And finally I am not happy that this turns off automatically after a certain period of time. I woke up in the middle of the night and had to turn this back on and then start my audiobook again from my iPad. This shouldn’t happen but some of these do this.

This works surprisingly well, it was super easy to set up with 5Ghz, not sure why others had problems with it. The microphone  worked okay but it doesn’t pick up sound well at all. I used this to watch my pup while I was at work. It did need buffering a lot and you have to tap around to get the refresh button. It seems most of the issues are connected to the app as usual. The picture quality was great. You can’t turn it off, you can only remove it from the usb cable. I thought it was chargeable but it isn’t. Probably not great for security or watching a toddler.

Update: ugh, second day and they do not turn on and pair automatically and only one will connect at all. So annoying
These are the best wireless or Bluetooth ear buds I have ever used. I tried them out at work where it can be quite noisy and my patients had no problems hearing me while using these on the phone. I work in a call center and allowed my agents to try these. They said they felt great and they liked the remote feature, however they had a hard time hearing customers even at full volume.

The sound quality is not the best, and cuts in and out. The battery is terrible to charge and dies very quickly. They are nice when they are working as they should but that does not happen often.

I’ve used the Sudio N2 Pro Earbuds for about a month, and I like them. I typically wear them for about 2-3 hours a day while working at my desk, and I have two major pros and three major cons I’ve noticed during the last month.

PROS:
🎵 The earbuds are super comfortable! I have multiple inner ear piercings in both ears (rook, daith, tragus) and a LOT of earbuds hurt after about thirty minutes. I can wear the Sudio N2s for several hours at a time. Small, medium, and large silicone tips are included so you can get a good fit depending on your ears. Sometimes I walk around my house and do chores with these in, they haven’t fallen out once.

🎵 For earbuds, the ANC is good! I can actually notice a difference with the ANC on and off; with some earbuds that claim to have noise cancelling, there’s really no difference. The ANC on the Sudio N2s blocks out when the television is playing in the next room, and even muffles the sound of the heater right under my desk.

CONS:
🎵 Battery life is not great. With ANC on, I get 4 hours, maaaaybe 4.5 if I’m lucky. I put the case on my charging pad every other day, it seems. The case supports wireless charging, which is a positive, or via USB-C. I’ve noticed the earbuds don’t always turn off when put in the case and the lid is closed, which undoubtedly contributes to the faster battery drain.

🎵 The earbuds support Multipoint connection, or connecting to multiple devices, but I can only get them to connect to my Mac. No matter what I try, they will not connect to my phone (Samsung Note 20 Ultra). I tried every suggestion in the online manual, but I can’t even get the earbuds to factory reset.

🎵 The touch controls are VERY sensitive. I have to make sure I don’t have any video tabs open when I put them in, or the video starts blasting in my ear. The only audible cue I noticed was to turn ANC on, and that is “Noise Cancelling.” A beep indicates turning it off, and beeps are used for all other cues. I don’t know what does what, I just wish I could turn them off.

Although the cons slightly outweigh the pros, I still use the Sudio N2s every day. The comfort is a huge factor for me. I’ve tried probably 8 pairs of earbuds in the last year, and this is the only pair I can wear for more than an hour at a time.

The KONNEK STEIN True Wireless Earbuds are a decent set of wireless earbuds. The sound quality is good, I’ve been using them with music and streaming shows, and I haven’t been disappointed with the sound quality.

I’m not as pleased with the short battery life, touch controls, and lack of audio cues.

I get about 2-3 hours of playback per charge. It’s rare for me to battery drain earbuds, but with this pair, I hear the low battery chime every time I use them.

The touch controls and lack of audio cues go together. The touch controls are super easy to activate on accident. More than once I’ve taken the earbuds out only to find I hit Play while doing so, and they kept playing music. I also activate random controls when adjusting the earbuds in my ears … and I don’t always know what I’ve done. Did I turn ANC on or off? The audio cues are just beeps, not an announcement like “ANC on/ANC off.”

I like the design of the case. It has a sliding top, so you can actually clean the entire area where the earbuds sit. When you put the earbuds inside the case, a light flashes to show their battery level. The case charges wirelessly or via USB-C. There’s only one LED light on the outside of the case, it’s easy to miss when you’re trying to see if the case is charging or not.

I like the sleek appearance of the Monster Verse Wireless Earbuds. I have them in Black; the finish is matte black, on earbuds and case. I also like physical buttons on the “head” of each earbud, which you can use to adjust the volume, skip tracks, and answer/reject phone calls.

Unfortunately, the sound quality doesn’t live up to the sleek look. The sound is average, or a bit below. I’m not an audiophile, but I noticed that all songs I listened to were lighter than they should be, like I was listening through a blanket or muffler. Not so bad to be tin-can sounding, but the songs just weren’t punchy and true to how I know they should sound. Bass didn’t really exist. I notice the subpar sound quality even when watching a tv show or movie.

The earbuds don’t last very long, about 2-3 hours. The case does give an hour’s worth of playback with a 15 minute charge, which is handy in a pinch. I do wish the case had a better indicator to show how much battery life it has left, it just has one LED light.

The USB charging cable Monster included is super nice. It’s a braided cable with an adapter, to accommodate USB-C and USB-A. The case also supports wireless charging.

Comfort-wise, the earbuds come with 5 extra sets of tips in a blister pack. The earbuds have medium tips on, and then you have the option of small or large. I have a daith piercing in one ear, some earbuds are comfortable and some are not. For me, these are not. But the earbuds can be used independently, so I usually wear one if I use them.

After using my MacBook Pro all day, I always have a short adjustment period when I pick up a Chromebook. Compared to a normal Mac or Windows laptop, a Chromebook is very basic, very slimmed down on what it can do. Basically, ChromeOS is like turning an Android phone or tablet into a computer. ChromeOS runs on Google: Google Play for apps, games, books, etc., Google Drive for word processing, spreadsheets, etc., Gmail for email, Chrome for web browsing, and so on.

I know schools use Chromebooks but I don’t have kids, so my review is from the perspective of someone who uses a Chromebook for light browsing and streaming. For that purpose, it’s good.

The battery on this HP Chromebook lasts about 10 hours for watching shows and movies. I like that I can just grab it, watch for a few hours, and only have to remember to charge it a few times a week. Unlike some other Chromebooks, this one has only the standard laptop form factor, it doesn’t tent or fold. It also doesn’t have a touchscreen, which can be frustrating when trying to use Google Play apps on it.

The display is just okay, not very bright compared to my MacBook Pro, but then, that’s an unfair comparison to make. The sound quality (Bang & Olufsen audio) is good, making up for the display. The keyboard is not backlit and is missing some keys, like Caps Lock for a Search button.

The screen of the Chromebook has a black plastic edge that sticks out slightly from the white shell of the lid. I’m pretty gentle and careful with electronics, but I notice the black plastic edge pressing back into the white shell whenever I open the laptop. This is right where the webcam is. I’m worried that overtime, this area could break, since it’s already giving a little and I’ve only had the Chromebook for a few weeks.

The Chromebook charges via USB-C. It has two USB-C ports, one on either side, one USB-A port, an audio port, and an SD card slot. It has Bluetooth and WiFi; without an internet connection, a Chromebook is almost useless.

The Razer Kraken BT Kitty headset is not a serious gaming headset. The lighting effects and cat ears look cool, and it’s Bluetooth so no wires like the original Kraken Kitty -- those are the big pros.

Razer Synapse does not recognize the headset, so if you want to customize it, two different phone apps are needed.

The Razer Chroma RGB app handles lighting options. The Razer Audio app handles sound settings, firmware updates, and changing the auto shutoff timer.

Do I really want to use my phone to manage my gaming headset? No. I consider having to use my phone while I’m playing a game on my computer to be a hassle!

I did find that I could customize the lighting effects with my phone, unpair the headphones from my phone and then pair them with my computer to keep the lighting effects while using with my computer. But that is also a hassle, considering Razer has a program meant to handle this!

Sound quality is just okay -- it’s not great. I’m not an audiophile so it works for me, but I have less expensive headphones that have better playback, even to my inexperienced ears. The headphones do not have ANC and I miss that a lot.

The controls are basic, a volume wheel and a power button. The power button can be used to pause and play, just hold it in for two seconds and let go, and the music will pause. Hold in for two seconds and let go to resume.

The headphones don’t have a 3.5mm audio jack, they are only Bluetooth. The charging cable is micro USB.

I have the Kraken Kitty wired headset, and I wanted a wireless version because once I started using Bluetooth headphones, I couldn’t stand being chained at my desk by a wire. But I feel like Razer wanted to appeal to women gamers -- make it pink, slap on kitty ears -- and didn’t focus as much on quality or function.

I got my mother the Lifeproof FRE case for her iPhone 6. For the last year, she’s been using a cheap case I bought on Amazon, the Diztronic Voyeur Case. I didn’t feel it was protective enough, so I hoped the Lifeproof FRE would work for her.

Unfortunately, she didn’t like the case at all, and wanted it off her phone minutes after I put it on. I made her use it for a few weeks, and while she didn’t experience any sound problems, there were several quality of life things that sealed the dislike for the Lifeproof FRE case.

PRO:
—The built-in screen protector is pretty good. I liked that I didn’t have to install it myself, as it’s part of the case.

CONS:
—Within minutes of putting the Lifeproof FRE case on her phone, I dropped it. The back of the case is slick, some kind of hard plastic instead of the grippier TPU case. The Lifeproof case just didn’t feel nice to hold in my hand, and with the slicker plastic, I worried that my mom would drop her phone as well.

—The little “door” that protects the charger port was super hard for her to open. Every time my mom wanted to charge her phone, I had to come do it for her, since she couldn’t get the door open. I understand needing a tight seal for the waterproof protection, but there has to be an easier way to access the charger port.

—The small oval cut out for charging cords was too small for my non Apple Lightning cables. I have two that are Apple certified, AmazonBasics and Zerolemon, and neither fit.

—My mom found it impossible to manipulate any of the buttons. I assume the buttons will loosen up over months, but boy, they are super hard to press when the case is new.

My mom’s not quite the intended audience for the case, but as she plans to keep her iPhone for a few years, we want it to stay in nice shape. And you never know when you’re going to drop your phone into a snowbank or puddle, so having a waterproof case adds peace of mind. But I’ll have to keep looking for her, because the Lifeproof FRE had a couple of little problems that added up to big annoyances.

Not the best and not the worst sound. Really this was just suppose to replace the radio for the garage, but I dont think it will be a keeper. There is NO power button on the remote, so unless this is right next to you and you go through the overly complicated method of powering it on, the remote is a bit useless. For our purposes (keeping it up on a shelf in the garage) its just not going to work. The sound isn't good enough to make due. Oh well.

Hands down the best headphones I've ever put on for bass. I ran them through my audio tester and these picked up way lower tones than my Senn's which have been my long standing pair for bass. It does seem to come at that cost of picking up the higher notes, but honestly when pitches are that high, they are annoying and I'm fine with the headphones not picking them up. I don't need to hear a dog whistle...

Mid-range was true, sound was immersive, the headset was light and comfortable. A bit warm on the ears but pretty much all closed style headsets are.
So why the three stars?
OMG the constant never ending hissing. Unless you are playing something loud enough to cover it up, it is always there. Even when I turned off ANC, even when I switched to ambient mode. HIIIISSSSSSSSSSSSS. I tried to ignore it but it was always there. I work on the computer and sometimes I have to hear audio tracks and othertimes there is silence, I have to physically remove these every time I am not playing something or HIIIIISSSSSSSSSSSSSS. Honestly have no idea how other reviews aren't bothered by this, its the loudest hissing static I've ever heard coming through headsets.

If you are like me and do not have sound coming out the entire time you are wearing them, do not buy. They will make you insane with rage, RAAWWRRR.

If you are only going to wear them while listening to music, and want the best bass you can find, buy these they are AMAZING for that, seriously. But ugh that hissing.

When reviewing headsets, I don't just pop them on and hit play on a favorite song or take a call. I actually run them through a battery of sound tests from an audio site. I run all sets through the same test to make it fair. First on my PC and then on my iPhone XS. I find it's the best way to make an unbiased review.
• Bass: Poor with a limited range. It also wasn’t balanced between the earbuds.
• High freq: Better than the bass, but still a limited range. It was balanced between the earbuds much better though.
• Rattle: None, but it would be weird if earbuds rattled. Ok that’s not true, I stepped on a pair at the gym that rattled afterwards. Oops.
• Volume: Sufficient. I don’t blast my earbuds, because I like to keep my hearing. I could turn it low enough to not hear, and loud enough to be uncomfortable.
• Clarity: Isolated for the sound test they did fine. However, outside the site the clarity started to degrade, and on a call was bad enough to be an issue.

The sound check results were mediocre. Bass was lacking, as was the general range of the set. These actually did worse than their cheaper behind the neck set (Jabra Evolve 65e UC).

As for things other than sound, like usability I like to ask myself what I’m looking for and if product meets those expectations. So, here goes:

Would these last the entire workday?
Yes and No, if you take them off to charge during lunch then you will probably be fine. Otherwise no they are going to die out about 75% through a standard 8 hr workday. They require a USB port and their little case thing to charge. I had no issues as long as I remember to charge them at lunch.

Are they easy to use?
The basics, yes. All the extra features, not so much. I opened the box up and was happy to see the quick-start guide, unfortunately if there is a manual I didn't get one. I found a digital copy tucked away in the iPhone app, but nothing in the box itself. That made anything past the basics in the quick-start guide a matter of trial and error, until I found the manual tucked away in the App. For the price, that seems like a rather cheap move. There is a ton of useful info in the manual that is not contained in the quick-start guide.

Can I take calls seamlessly?
Yes, but for me at least the call experience was lacking. The voices on some but not all calls were a bit muddled, however they could hear me just fine. So poor marks for the sound quality, but high marks for the mic.
Speaking of mics, can I mute the mic easily?
Easily, yes. But knowing for sure if you are muted (we've all been there) only when using the computer dongle, on my iPhone using Bluetooth, eek not so much. Had to leave it to faith. That was a bit scary.

Plays music well (aka does it have range and bass)?
Meh. I have the sound review at the top. As you can imagine, lack of bass negatively impacts listening to music. I mean it wasn’t awful but it wasn’t great either.

Can I opt to hear people talking to me (audio pass-through)?
Yes, but it sounds super static and buzzy. The sound is not clear and crisp at all. Also, you can't just pop an earbud out and listen with one ear. If the earbuds are anymore than head-width apart they stop working all together. According to the manual, you should be able to use the right earbud by itself, but that was not my experience. It also would stop working (although it worked a bit longer than the left) once they were too far apart.

Noise-canceling abilities, can I at least block out the cubical next to me?
Sort of. You can block drumming blah blah blah sounds, but ringing phones and coworkers talking, not so much. Although it did take the edge off. The Jabra iPhone app for these has some cool ambient sound machine settings, waves crashing, thunderstorm, white noise, etc. Probably my favorite thing about this whole set.

Are they comfortable?
I didn't like them, but I am a petite human and have small ears. I also don't like the weird vacuuming pressure you feel when wearing anything noise-cancelling. I will give these neutral marks for comfort, I think if you had larger ear canals and didn't mind closed type headsets these would probably be fine.

Are these worth the price?
Nope. For the price these should be spectacular and check all the boxes. They are mediocre in sound quality even though they are packed with features. If you plan on just tossing them on and not actually testing the audio, go for it. They work. But for the price, they should handle music and calls equally well. They do not.

Overall, I will have to say I was rather disappointed with these. I also reviewed their behind the neck version (Jabra Evolve 65e UC) and was hoping I had just gotten a dud with that set. Well lightening either struck twice, or the audio on these is even worse than the cheaper behind the neck version. Darn, because I wanted to love these. I have a soft spot for gadgets with cool features. These had potential. I will give them three stars because if the price point wasn’t so high, they would be okay. Not great, but they’d get the job done. I also really liked the ambient sounds you could listen to on the app. A nice little extra that was unexpected.

Hope that helps!

I wanted to love these and for phone calls they are just fine. But when I ran a sound test on them it was obvious what I had begun to suspect, there was little to no bass coming out of the right ear bud. Just to make sure it wasn't my hearing I flipped them and now it was the left ear not picking up bass, so yeah its the set not my hearing. This was not a subtle difference either, the left blasted bass while the right barely produced it. Volume and higher tones were equal, between the two. This occurred on both my PC and iPhone.

Noise canceling was so-so, although these are only passive not active cancelling so I didn't have super high expectations. I also found them uncomfortable even with the smallest ear fittings. I could look past most of that if they weren't defective and rather pricey. Oh well.

It is stubborn about not wanting to go backwards. I tried everything. I even tried taking the disk out and putting it back in and darn if it doesn't keep a memory of where it was. I had to put in a different disk, let that start, then put in the first disk to get back to the track I wanted to listen to. It was an old lecture series and I missed part of it and wanted to re-listen.

The sound quality is decent. It's been a long time since I've used physical disks so I'm hard pressed to compare. I picked this up in hopes of listening to some old stuff.

It more or less suits my needs with some extra work. It's okay at best.

Where do I start with this train wreck. I guess, I'll start with the intended purpose. It claims it's good if you have a snoring partner it's so noise cancelling, so I figure, during quarantine, it should be enough to let me hear audio over reasonable outside noise. Other headsets do. This one just looked more comfortable.

The sound level is terrible. On high it sounds like someone whispering from across the room. I kept checking that I had it on right and at one point I took the thing off and pressed the speaker right to my ear. That wasn't much better.

It's ok as a headband, but even for that I wouldn't give it props for comfort. I certainly couldn't use it to exercise, which I thought was one of the key selling points.

Really, don't bother. I'll make do as I have to, but better choices abound.

Given the price point, the sound quality is sorely lacking on these. They perform about as well as the cheap ones available at the chain drug store.

Where they excel is comfort. I don't like wearing headphones for long, and I can tolerate these much longer than average. I'm quite pleased at the easy fit and how they don't annoy my ears. I'll use them regularly for that alone.

I use it primarily with an iPod Touch.

Connecting it up is easy. There are no codes to enter, no cross synching. Just find it, connect to it, and you're good to go. It takes over the iPod speakers, so there is no double sound or echo. No, you can't trick it into stereo sound that way. It carries the sound over a decent distance, though not through any obstacles, and provides decent sound across a range of musical styles. Certainly what you'd expect from a mini. The battery life is excellent.

On the first day out I was able to crash it. I couldn't decide what I wanted to listen to. I ran some stored music, closed that, ran Pandora, closed that, ran Sirius, closed that again and tried Audible, and the thing hung. No sound at all. I went back to what was working before, but still no sound. When I turned it off, the music was playing just find through the iPod speakers, so it wasn't the iPod that crashed.

Overall, I like it but don't love it.

For the price, it is not bad. I have a Belkin case also coming but do not have it yet, so I cannot compare this case to a name brand. I do have a ULUQ silicone protective case as well and I really feel like THAT case is secure.

With THIS case, I do not get that feeling. It definitely holds the airtag and keeps it protected. The sound is good and not muffled through the holder. My only worry is, as just stated, will it stay together? It would stay together from the top when attached to the included clip, but the bottom could seemingly open and that worries me. I decided not to start using it just yet and instead opted to just slip my first airtag into my wallet. When my Belkin comes, which is the brand offered on the Apple website, I will come back and update how this case compared to that case. Overall ... it would do a good job of protection, just not 100% sure it would stay together after some bumps and hard jostles. Does not make me feel secure that it won't fall out and get lost because of the case design. For that reason ... I could not recommend. it. Jury is still out.

Why do you need this?
The WiFi signal in the yard isn't that great. With this, the audio can be in every room, AND outside!
Any issues, free phone support (after you register the product), a rarity indeed.
Terrific device, BUT I'm having an issue.

I was going to video putting it all together, and now I can't get it to work! I'll update after calling customer support

Update 11/2/13: NO ONE can get it to work again. Good company, but this one product didn't deliver for me.

I was excited to receive these headphones as I like the over the ear design and they are cordless. The headphones are fine, but a little bulky if you are used to ear buds. I was hoping the sound quality would be better. If the song has a lot of base, it comes across all scratchy with static. It charges in its case fine. The case protects the headphones, but if you drop it, the case doesn't lock shut so the headphone will fall out. I haven't had any issues with charging (which I have with other headphones that have this type of charging).  Overall, they are average, but I wish the sound quality was better.

Easy plug-and-play compatible. Near instant Blue-tooth connection. Simple, accessible push button operation on the phones.

I've been using bone-conduction headphones for routine computer work for several years. I've found that it's not for everyone. However, the convenience and utility are worth a try. The bone conduction sound experience isn't hi-fi. Mental sound focus is situational and auditory input interchangeable and/or simultaneous between room ambient and machine.

The tone setting here is too treble IMO. Or, maybe, it's just different and I'll get used to it. The tone is not independently adjustable. These would be excellent out of the box if the tone was independently adjustable.

The rechargeable battery in the phones I've been using for 2 years died. This next-generation Blue-tooth upgrade for connectivity is noticeably improved.

60-day Update: I've been using these nearly daily. I've gotten used to the tone. The battery is lasting a week. I have a wandering range with this Bluetooth edition of say 75'. The fastest connection and link speed of any I've had. Quite happy.

Bright picture. Sharp image.

Limited mounting options. The lensing system limits projector mounting to a very few degrees from perpendicularity with the screen. It's missing the lens set to proportionately square the vertical projection. At 10' between screen and projector, a 20° down tilt from the ceiling mount results in irresolvable screen distortion/parallax. Does not work as the replacement of an existing 720p overhead projector.

Sony WH-XB900N Wireless Noise Canceling Extra Bass Headphones have great sound quality. Plus, for an over the ear headphone they are surprisingly lightweight. I also like how they bend to fold up and are really pliable. However, that's really where the greatness stops. Pairing these with any device I own is difficult or doesn't happen at all. These will not pair with my laptop. My laptop sees it's there. It claims it's playing from the headphones, but alas it does not most of the time. In addition, these will not play from iTunes. So, if you have an Apple device forget it. These will not pair with my iPhone 5. For two reasons, first, these are terrible with Apple devices/software and second, you must have the App to pair the headphones, which if you have an older phone won't happen because the App is only compatible with certain iOS systems. As much as I am angry with Apple for stopping all updates for older Apple devices (which work just fine otherwise), it's equally frustrating with App developers who do not design their Apps to be compatible with the older systems. So, most of my experience with these headphones is through the AUX jack.

Therefore, the sound quality is really good. I listen to a lot of hiphop and the bass is spot on. However, I do listen other types of music (pretty much everything) and I would have to say listening to Beethoven's 6th and Old Blind Dogs was a nice experience as well! The noise cancelling is a joke. I can hear everything around me still. In fact, I'm currently wearing these as I type this review and can hear the click clack of the keys, my son bump around upstairs, and my father just call my name. So, if you wear these on public transportation or at work, you're gonna hear everything as usual. But they are good headphones and comfortable on my ears.

The instructions are ridiculous. Can we stop with the picture instructions? They make no sense. I need words and should not have to depend on internet video reviews to get clarity on how to use anything. There is a way to play, pause, volume down/up by tapping or swiping, but I have no idea how to do it. Sometimes it works, sometimes not. They have a long battery life. I charged these weeks ago and they still have a charge as I use them now.

So, these have a great sound quality, the noise cancellation doesn't do anything, and you need to pair these with non-Apple devices.

Asimom True Wireless Earbuds, Bluetooth V5.0, TWS Bluetooth Earphones Auto-Pair Wireless Headphones are really nice earbuds and easy to use.  They paired easily and quickly with my iPhone 5.  They come in a case that charges them and they are already charged when I received them.  They come with a USB charging cord for the case and with extra earbuds depending on the size of your ear.  You just tap with on and tap to play or play.  It's pretty tricky at first.  I'm still getting the hang of it.  The sound quality is really decent.  The downside is that these do not stay in my ear and dropped out an onto the ground while I was out for a walk.  So, I'll only use these at work since if they fall onto the carpet they won't get scratched up.  Not as good as a product as the Asimom Bluetooth Speaker, which I also received, but still a decent product.  If you don't have issues with earbuds falling out your ears like I do, then this is great for you.

These over the ear Bluetooth earphones are just over the ear Bluetooth ear phones. They are not noise cancelling, so if that is what you want then you'd better pass on by. These are a basic Bluetooth Wireless Headphones.

Unboxing you get the headphones, and two different cords. One cord to charge the headphones (USB plug) and one cord to use the headphones outside of Bluetooth mode. I plugged them in my laptop overnight to charge it up and then took them to work to see how they would do. At work, I found out they do not cancel noise. I could still hear every single conversation around me whether music was playing or not. To drown out conversation, I would have to turn the sound way up, but I'd rather save my hearing. However, my purposes it's ok. I really just wanted the overhead head phones to indicate to people that I'm working. For some reason, earbuds just don't communicate that I'm busy. I had to use the audio cord in my mp3 (from a famous manufacturer) because I have a first generation unit that doesn't have Bluetooth ability. I felt that earbuds vs. these were no different. I decided to start with something bass inducing, so started with early 00's Hip Hop. The bass on my earbuds is better. I then worked my thru my R&B & Alternative lists, and then finally something with high pitched tones (strings) like Irish Folk. I felt that my earbuds had slightly better sound quality. However, I did not feel like was missing out on much.

Next, I brought them home and tested them out with my laptop in Bluetooth mode. Set-up was easy. My laptop has a Bluetooth icon and I just asked it to look for Bluetooth devices. After a few seconds, AmazonBasics Bluetooth Headphones popped-up. I told it to connect and then pumped up the jamz (it's always with a z). After a couple hours, I got up to adjust the thermostat on the A/C. I walked from the dining room thru the living room and into the foyer. I realized as I was walking back I still had the headphones on! I completely forgot! So, that means they are comfortable. A little heavy, but I obviously got used to it.

Finally, I tested them with my tablet (again a well-known brand) and I was not able to connect to it. I then tried to reconnect to my laptop and the laptop did not reconnect. The instructions are no good in troubleshooting this issue. So, now I have to connect via the cable all the time, which defeats the purpose. I can use the earbuds that I've been using. Plus, my laptop stopped producing sound altogether. Additionally, when they are playing everyone can hear what you listening to, so they will not be that helpful. If my son is standing next to me or sitting at the table with me, he can hear every word from my HipHop mix. Not ideal. Speaking of HipHop, another downside is that these, unlike a well-known brand with the name of a rapper/producer attached to them, do not fold up. So, they are big and bulky in your bag when you are carrying them around. I'm also afraid that something in my purse or mini backpack is going to do something to them. I also have to make sure I'm carrying a big purse to transport these around.

Pros:
-Wireless! (Don't disconnect from the device once you get it connected you'll never get it back.)
-Comfortable on the ears
-Easy set-up

Cons:
-Not Noise Cancelling
-Sound Quality could be better
-Heavy
-Does not fold up (Bulky to carry around)
-Must use the cable if you disconnect from a device. It will not reconnect.

UPDATE: The fix to my connection issue was on Pg. 6 of the instructions, but that's not how I connected the first time. Now, that I am reconnected to my laptop, the sound is like being underwater and goes in and out. So, it's tricky and sometimes you will have a set of wireless headphones, and sometimes you won't.

CONS:
Trackpad is horribly draggy even after changing speed and pressure settings. It is almost unusable so expect to buy a mouse.
Keyboard is a bit springy but not the worst.
Gestures are annoyingly sensitive (switching between apps and windows, Charms menu popping up) but can be turned off. This is more of a Windows 8 thing though.
Flipping around for tablet mode causes some programs to crash or freeze occasionally (MS Word)

PROS:
Light and thin
Good display
Priced better than the similar Lenovo Yoga 2
Can flip around for reading, movies or other tablet type activities.

Pros:
• Good price compared to other manufacturers / brands.
• Recordings automatically begin after ignition.
• Good, clear daylight recordings.
• New recordings will overwrite the oldest recordings when the memory is full.
• Can transfer recordings to your mobile device using the DDPAI App.

Cons:
• Does not include a TF microSD video card for recording (maximum 128GB). Wasted several days for ordering and receipt of a card.
• No rear camera included with this model.
• Poor nighttime low light recordings.
• The camera lens positioning creates glare and reflections from the dashboard, which distort the quality of the recordings.
• The DDPAI App was difficult to set up and pair with the Dashcam. After synchronization, the App is neither user-friendly, nor easy to use.
• Poor instructions did not adequately explain the use or installation of the “static sticker” (a thin, transparent plastic film which was included), nor the “electrostatic stickers”. It seems some steps get lost in the translation from the designer’s language into English.
• This model has no GPS, so you won’t have the vehicle speed label or miles driven on the recordings. This reduces the ability to review and analyze an accident or incident (for insurance and legality purposes). No map and driving route recording.
I recommend paying extra for a GPS Dual Dashcam which includes the Rear Cam.

If these were in a lower price point, they’d have more stars, but for the current price of ~$80, there’s a problem that really should not be there: a very high pitch whine in the background. It’s noticeable most when you have noise cancelling on with silence in the background, or in sections of music or voice that are quiet. It’s not terribly loud, but I can pick it up from time to time.
Other than that, the noise cancelling is pretty good, and the sound has good clarity and power. The treble isn’t super tinny the way some headphones are—EXCEPT when you bring the volume up. THEN, it does get tinny, and the bass doesn’t have quite the power you might like. You can hear subtle details in most music, which I appreciate, and pairing is easy.
As for comfort, the ear cups are a bit small and have a somewhat awkward fit, though they are lightweight and reasonably comfortable.
All in all, these would be Great headphones if they were in the $40-$50 range. In the $80 range, they’re just ok.

Definitely not a high fi way to listen, and not just because cassette tapes are only good for nostalgia and not sound quality, but also because playback can be a little hit or miss, this is a fun 80's throwback toy that also lets you record. Yes, you can re-live the low-tech days of messed up cassette tapes needing to be rewound with a pencil’s eraser end. This is a fun little gadget that might work for you (or might not—it’s a lottery!)

This is a pretty mixed review of an interesting concept that is pretty good right now, but has the potential to be great in the near future. At the current price of about $150, this is ok+ based on the following criteria:

Sound Quality: 2.5-3 stars
For the size, it's ok
When reviewing for sound quality, I compare speakers (and headphones) to comparably sized items, based on speakers I currently or previously have owned. I take price range *somewhat* into account (I don't expect $15 headphones to sound like $500 ones), but for anything over $100, I use the full range from the cheapest stuff I have, to my favorite brand, Bose.
So with that in mind, I have a portable wireless Bose speaker that is smaller and acts as the "5" on the scale.
The sound on this can get loud enough to not distort and still fill a smallish room or normal bedroom fine. The treble and bass are ok, though the higher ranges are tinny and the bass lacks depth. Overall sound from high to low and throughout the mid range lack definition. It's good enough for very casual background listening and for podcasts.

Alexa Feature: 4 stars
I have an iPhone and think Alexa has quite a bit more understanding and skill than Siri. When asked questions, from simple stuff like "what's the weather" to more complicated stuff like "I'm hungry. What can I make in half an hour?", the answers and follow-up questions are highly intuitive and thorough. Does she get everything all the time? No. But she does a much better job than Siri.

User-Friendliness: 2.5 stars
I didn't like the process of figuring out how this works, particularly the part of pairing with more than one device and also Having to use an app to make most of it work. It was a clunky, irritating process that more or less stayed that way every time I wanted to use this thing, especially for listening to music. It should be able to just play from your iTunes through the iTunes app and bluetooth, and instead, I was only able to make it play iTunes though Their App, which sucks when it comes to my music. And that brings us to the App..

App: 2 stars
No. Just no. Bluetooth exists for a reason, and if a speaker has bluetooth, you should be able to just pair and play. I had to use the app to play from my iTunes, and because I have a very specific way of organizing things, I was incredibly annoyed that something didn't translate, and my music was disorganized and basically impossible to search for with this app. Instead of being able to play what I want from one of my playlist subfolders, it disregarded my way of organizing things, and I ended up giving up. If I can't listen to my stuff easily with this, then like 75% of the reason to use this disappears, leaving me with an expensive alarm clock with weather report, recipe ideas, and some cool internet stuff. That's cool, but it's quite incomplete for what I need, and what I suspect many people want.

tl;dr version: sound is mediocre but doable, app is bad, Alexa is super clever and smart, and the experience has a lot of frustrating aspects.

Unfortunately, the sound on these isn't great, which is unfortunate given the eco-friendly approach in the packaging and product. The mid range is ok, though the treble and bass leave quite a bit to be desired. The bass lacks strength and intensity, while the treble and mid feel a bit canned, and there's an overall lack of definition.

Are these bad? No. They're better than many headphones, and are ok for the price. But for a little more money, you can do much better. Still, if this is the price range you want, and the environment is a priority for you, as well as supporting businesses that try to be responsible, it is worth considering these.

The buds are ok, though with small ears, they don't stay in great. As for the sound, it could be better, especially for the price. The overall quality sounds rather tinny, and it lacks detail in general and strength on the low and high ends.

I would have liked to see better sound quality and fit for this product. It's ok, but for the money, I expected a bit more.

I thought by the look and price of it that this would be an excellent sound system. Well, it is portable, very easy to use and pair, and looks fantastic....but the sound quality is terrible. The bass, even at a lowish volume, sounds distorted and fuzzy, creating a Lot of vibration and very little in terms of quality sound. For the higher end, it sounds tinny, as though coming through a can. Meanwhile, the overall detail in the sound is poor, creating a fuzzy output that makes nearly any genre of music sound flat. I have speakers a tenth this size that sound better. I would not recommend it.

While they are ok for the price in terms of sound quality, fit, and durability, they lack a fundamental function for what Many people use to play their music: the ability to receive and make phone calls. If you are using a smartphone, these are only headphones, not headphones with a function button (like the kind that come with an iPhone, for example), and not ones that have an output through which you can speak or take dictation.
That aside, the sound quality was ok, with a somewhat tinny, canned quality and poor capability in processing deep bass or treble. If changing the levels to decrease treble, you'll see some improvement in the sound. For anything spoken word like podcasts, these are fine.
The fit is not bad. Usually, these things are big on me (female with apparently small ear-holes, if you would judge by most headphones), but these were comfortable. The three sizes of rubbery earplugs always help and are generally standard, and the ear hooks also aide in keeping them in place.

Summary:
For the price, you get decent headphones that do not have an output function.

While the pairing process was simple, and the ability to make calls went smoothly, the sound quality was sub-par. One might expect this level of quality in a $10 headphone.
Here's why:
-The volume tops out at somewhere in the 80 decibel range, which is not a lot. It would be fine for background listening in a quiet environment, but if you want to listen to music loudly, which many people might, or if you are dealing with lots of background noise, then it's not even remotely adequate.
-Does nothing for treble or bass. Everything sounds right around the middle, flattening out most music.
-Lacks detail. You don't hear the quieter elements in music, and it does not pick up on individual parts. Fuzzy.

I wouldn't buy these. Bluetooth headsets can be very hit or miss. While it was user-friendly, this was mostly a miss.

The portability is excellent, as well as a few other features: it is rechargeable, very small, lightweight, and the pairing process is so easy. Unfortunately, this product has several downsides, and they are the ones that count most: the sound quality is bad.

I always wonder why products allow you to raise the volume far beyond the limits of what the product can sustain without creating distortion. The point at which the product does this is roughly halfway; it can only go to roughly 65-80 decibels before treble starts to sound horrible, distorted, and messy. That is NOT very loud at all. The sound, even at lower volumes, is somewhat fuzzy: you cannot hear detail in the music like you can with better quality speakers. Even With the distortion, at maximum volume, it doesn't get Very loud. That's mostly to be expected at this price point and in something of this size with rechargeable batteries, you can't hope for much more than this product has to offer. For that reason, it gets 3 stars. Roughly average--not great, not terrible.

Oddly, I got better sound quality from several cheaper headphones I own, but bluetooth has always been a bit hit or miss for me. Pairing was very easy (thankfully! some can be a pain), but the range isn't great. It's fine if you plan on putting your phone in your pocket, but if you are working out and want to set your phone aside, you only have about 10-15 feet, if that. Mid-range sounds are fine, but on the high trebles and low bass, it starts to sound a little distorted. The fit was ok, but I have very small ears and ear canals, so even the small inserts were slightly uncomfortable after a while. They stayed in place fine, but I used it for dancing, so the range and quality were not great for that. Still a pretty good product, though--just not as good as one might hope for the price.

This is the second "Creative" brand wireless bluetooth speaker with microphone, and so far, the sound quality has not been very good. The first, "Creative Sound BlasterAxx SBX10 Wireless Bluetooth Speaker with Microphone" was $127.04 (list price $149.99), and this one currently has a list price of $199.99. I cannot hear any discernable difference in sound quality, though this speaker is larger than the other. They are both OK for being usb powered, but there are better-sounding products out there for the same price if you are willing to sacrifice the speaker option.

I ran the same tests on this speaker as the other and got identical results:

This one gets a mixed review for the overall sound quality, but it does have some features that make it very useful. I will be reviewing its various features individually so you can better assess if this meets your needs or not. I used a decibel measuring app on my phone to determine when the speakers began to distort some of what I played.

Playing audio with Bluetooth or via USB with a computer:
-There is no noticeable difference with playback using Bluetooth versus USB connection to a computer, and it has a Very long range (I walked about 25ft away and it was still doing fine)

AUDIO

75 DECIBELS AND UNDER:
Almost all audio was fine: clear, undistorted, and with pretty good clarity (don't expect GREAT quality or clarity. Just Good.) Some types of music fared poorly even at this relatively soft volume. I used "Fortuna from Carmina Burana" to test the system's limits. (YouTube the piece if you want to know which song I refer to--you'll recognize it immediately) The chorus of singers sounded distorted. At higher volumes, even as lot as 85db, it was awful. Other types of music were fine (orchestra music, pop, hip hop, electronica), but sometimes the treble was a bit fuzzy.

75-85 DECIBELS:
This is the maximum volume the speakers can reach with the USB connection, so it can get loud enough for a small-medium party, but not Very loud.
It's hit and miss here. The treble and bass have some problems, especially treble. The clarity diminishes and any nuances in your music will generally get a bit lost or muffled. Choral music, music with higher pitched percussive elements, and some types of rock and orchestra music don't sound very good.

PHONE CALLS:
The voice of the person you are calling sounds a bit muffled--definitely not as good as headphones or the phone, but about on par with other Bluetooth systems I've tried.

The voice of the speaker (i.e. You) is actually clear! This part gets a solid review. With my built-in car Bluetooth system, as well as detachable ones I've reviewed, usually the person you are calling has trouble hearing you and can experience interference. Maybe that is because it is in the car and there's road noise, but in any case, the fact this one does, actually, sound clear to the recipient of your phone call is a BIG plus.

Overall, this is a good product when you compare it to other desktop laptop speakers. If you are comparing it to products specifically meant for enjoying audio, however, I would recommend the Pioneer Electronics Audition Series for a relatively inexpensive but high quality experience, or Bose if you are looking for something higher-end. The price of the Pioneer product is almost the same, and while it doesn't have Bluetooth unless you buy the attachment separately (about $70) and it only docks with the older iPhone and iPods, the sound quality of that one is stunning. If you want extra features like FREE Bluetooth and speakerphone capability, this one is ok for the price. Not great. Just ok.

Because this is basically the same as the "Creative Sound BlasterAxx SBX10 Wireless Bluetooth Speaker with Microphone", and the other is about $70 cheaper, I would recommend getting the SBX10 and saving your money. They are basically the same thing, so either pay more and get better sound quality with another product entirely, or pay less for the same thing.

I was disappointed to see this was not only NOT water-proof, but not even water-resistant, so you can't even sit it in the shower (supposedly). If it's for the bathroom, it should take that into account. As for the sound, it is ok. The volume doesn't get terribly loud, so if you are showering, you won't hear much. It's audible if you're sitting in the bath, but again, the sound isn't good enough to really enjoy music. Then again, radio doesn't have high quality sound, so maybe it doesn't matter so much.
