Ok product to have, though. The design is compact and subtle, and it can double as a radio to be used in the event of a power outage during a storm.

This thing has a mind of its own. I use it in my room for showing videos in class. Sometimes it will connect to my computer easily and sometimes it won't. IT does have an HDMI cord that you can connect to, but my smart board only has one connection and that has to run directly from my computer.

When it works, it has a decent sound for the money you are paying. You are not going to get a theatre experience with this bar... but it is better than the speakers that come with the tv.

This screen is nice but there are a couple of problems with it.

1- You can not turn the screen to a portrait position, its only in landscape. So the head is either cut off of the picture is shrunk so you can not see the picture well.

2- upload speed is really slow. I've had several frames and this is by far the smallest.

This frame however is different and neat in other ways.

1- it has sound
2- there is a daily weather update
3- You can upload videos
4- you can put the pictures in different "frames" so you can display more than one picture at a time. I have it set to show 2, so that they appear to be in portrait mode. However, the pictures are not centered.

Depending on what you want... determines how you will view this frame

Don't get me wrong, this sound bar is good. But compared to a surround sound system (for the same price) the "panoramic" sounds is not the same. It has a decent sound... but the price you pay just isn't worth it to me.

It was pretty easy to hook up/connect to my tv. The instructions were clear as well. Its not a bad system by any means... but the one that I already had (again for the same price) blows this out of the water... like not even comparable.

The sound quality of this soundbar isn't the best. I have several others and this one almost sounds like it is in a hole compared to the others that I have. It was a little difficult to hook up to my smart board at school, The only way I could attach it was by using old school aux cords. It is ok for what I needed it for, but I wouldn't be happy with it if I wanted to use it as my primary home entertainment system.

Don't get me wrong I love the concept of this tv... but it is a pain in my tail. It is ridiculously hard to install because you have to eliminate the cords. The look is nice and its very sleek and the picture is nice... however in my opinion I would just rather have a normal wall mount.

Connecting it to the internet was fairly easy and I don't have any problems with it staying connected to my sound bar either.

the frame over all is a very nice tv... its just a little too impractical for my taste.

These have so much potential to be awesome - but they unfortunately miss the mark.

The sound quality is great, the presentation is great, the color is great!

The problem comes in when you want to sync them with one another.

Whatever volume you sync the additional pumpkin at is going to be the volume that it stays synced at for the duration of the sync.

That means that if you want to adjust the volume at any point in time, you have to de-pair and re-pair them.

You also cannot sync different styles - the pumpkin face cannot be synced to the translucent pumpkin from the same company.

I was hoping for more of a surround sound quality, these really disappointed - when you turn up the sound, it distorts. It sounds muddled - I'm sure if your tech savvy you could amplify with a different sub or whatnot. This was for someone who is elderly and has hearing problems so was hoping for a no muss no fuss system. If you're looking to boost standard TV sound, this would work I guess, but not for surround sound.

This is an ok speaker. It is really easy to pair and use but the sound quality just isn’t there. It is lightweight so it is easy to travel with. I put mine in the garage for when the guys are working. That’s about it.

This works great as a Bluetooth for my laptop or even my iPad but I could not get it to work on my smart tv. I’m not technically challenged, I followed the instructions but it just didn’t work. The sound on this is amazing. The battery lasted me almost 18 hours of playtime and it charges completely in a little over an hour. It came with the USB charging cord but not the adapter.. It is fairly simple to operate as Bluetooth and the price is definitely worth it.

This is definitely a portable speaker. The small size is perfect for travel. It fits in my coat pocket. It is a nice design with the rose gold look. It took about an hour to charge it fully and a full charge gave me 9 hours of playtime. I guess because it is small that the volume doesn't go very high. The sound quality is awful. I've used many bluetooth devices and this by far is one of the worst. It would be perfect in a nursery maybe or as a backup device but it surely will not be my first choice. Also the sound comes out one end and the other end has the control buttons so while the music is playing and you want to turn it up or down you have to turn it upside down to do so. It's not a problem really it's just weird. I took this into my laundry room so if it in there working or if I go out back I can listen to music. It comes with the USB cord but not the adaptor and the user instructions. The price is really good but I guess that compensates for the sound. However, there are way too many bluetooth speakers out there that are this price or cheaper with a lot better sound quality.

This is perfect for a working environment. The noise canceling feature is top of the line so you can hear only your conversation and not any of the background noise. I love that there are three ways to wear this, one with out any band, one with the headband and one with behind the neck style. This was so easy to pair. The battery only lasted six hours with a full charge but it charges pretty fast. The voice control is amazing and definitely the best feature.  This comes with the USB cable, mobile charger, four ear hooks, and five ear gel tips. It is so lightweight but the earpiece is so large and bulky which makes it uncomfortable to wear for long periods. I really didn’t like the sound quality. The only way I can describe the sound is shallow. No matter how I adjust the the volume, the sound just wasn’t good and at this price point it should be perfect. It works great for calls just not music. The control buttons are large so it made it easy to make adjustments in volume etc. This looks great and works really well.

These are excellent headphones. Very comfortable with really good sound quality. What brings my review down from a 5 is that there's not enough information in the booklet. When using these headphones, of you take them off of one ear, they sometimes shut down. I think it's a feature that shuts then off, when not in use, to save battery life, but it's a little too sensitive and there's nothing in the booklet on that feature. Other than that annoying problem, they are great. If that problem is addressed and solved, these headphones would be a 5 star.

1 star - awful! Want my money back!
2 stars - bad but not horrendous
3 stars - decent/good
4 stars - really good!
5 stars - awesome! Definitely recommend!

Works as described. Just not too happy that the entire thing came 0% charged. Like other reviewers said it wasn't very loud, but I view it as a benefit for protecting our hearing. Needs quite some getting used to. The double click doesn't work like the double click you'd do on your phone. I felt like massaging the phone to move to the next song, pick up the phone or trying to turn the volume. Also you can use only one ear instead needing to pair both. For the price, I thought it's great.

I have more trouble getting Alexa to hear me on this echo. Though the base sound is very powerful when you play pop music. I still think it takes a long time to figure out what Alexa can do and that's kind of annoying because it's still in your app, not on the device and you can't talk Alexa into it. Because I haven't figured out how to watch my prime video or do calls, I can only use Alexa for music, timer and checking weather and so far she does it nicely. Just didn't like that my echo is hard of hearing.

This sound bar was a bit of a disappointment.  The sound quality is rather all treble and very little bass.  It plays, links up to bluetooth easily.  Some of the nicer aspects are that its mountable to a wall from the back, and has a nice little remote that makes it easy to hit the volume up and down.  Because of the lack of bass, I would really not select this particular model for a television or a large room....I installed mine in the bathroom for some ambient music while showering, and in a small space, the lack of bass isnt very noticable, but in a large room you keep waiting for the bass to pipe up in music, and it just never happens.  For a small space, or a very easy listening customer this unit is perfect-but if youre looking to jam to some booty music, rap, or techno, you would be very disappointed.

I purchased it because of the price and the color availability. I like it but it hurts my ear so I have to switch ears every so often to relief the discomfort.
Sound is awesome and I can listen to my music from the phone. It is very clear when receiving and making calls. The voice that tells me "call terminated" freaked me out the first time. Need to get used to it.

UPDATE: Lost it on a business trip down an elevator shaft! Not only did it hurt my ear, it kept on slipping off my ear and it fell off.

My daughter loves LOL Dolls, Diva is her favorite so she has been asking for these every time we go to the store. They are directly cut the sequined fabric bow at the top is just adorable and the sequins can change colors to silver to pink. It has a picture of Diva on each ear and is just so bright and fun to wear. The bad, I know these are made to help control volume for kids, but she can not hear anything. She will not use them with her tablet, she pulls out the cord, and then just leaves the headphones on like a headband. I could barely hear anything either. So for sound, this is a big Nope

I used these to organize my stereo/TV cables. The 1" version I bought accommodates 4 sets of speaker cables, a sub-woofer speaker cable, and a subwoofer power cable. It was pretty easy to gather the cables into the tubing and break them out as I got to each component. You can use an ordinary pair of scissors to cut/trim the tubing.

Unfortunately, it's really ugly. Though it doesn't look beautiful in the picture, it's even more unattractive when you see it in person. Of course that's just my opinion, but I think most will agree. I was afraid that would be the case, but I was desperate for a solution. This is MORE ugly than audio cables lying on the floor.

The tube is pretty thin/cheap. I bet these cost about a quarter to make (think thickness/weight of a drinking straw).

I think these would be fine to organize cables for your jam room setup, in your man cave, or in your shop, but for a nicer living area I would go with something else.

These headphones are pretty nice. The sound quality is decent and the noise cancelling is good enough. The problem is they only last a few months before they quit working. For the price I would've expected them to last much longer.

This speaker has an incredible sound, particularly for its size, and is very portable which is convenient.  But it is extremely frustrating because it's so unresponsive.  Using the assistants (Google, Amazon), there is a bit of a pause before it answers or confirms what you said and then there is a long pause before it follows your instructions.  For example, if you ask it to play music, there's at least a second where you aren't sure if it heard you or not before it says it's playing that music.  Then there are a couple silent seconds before the music starts.  This has led to us attempting to ask it again, thinking it didn't "hear" us, which just confuses it.  For using during a party or something where you just start it going and leave it, it wouldn't be a problem, but for regular use, the annoyance is not worth the great speaker sound.

The sound quality and noise cancellation of these earbuds are amazing.  The hear through option works relatively well.  I just can't find a good fit of ear tip for my ear.  I was able to find a moderately comfortable fit, but I could not be fully active while wearing them.  They often fall out of my ears.  I really want to like them more, but I just don't.

Audio support is a nice add-on, but normally not needed.  I had some problems with the computer going to sleep and not waking up through the KVM.  It easily let me switch between two computers either pressing the button or hotkey on the computer.  It is good for intermittent use.
sound does not work but at least provides some protection

Nice sturdy little radio. Good for taking with you to listen to the baseball game. It seems sturdy, but it only gets three stars because the sound isn't all that great, especially for the price. It seems that the days of a small clear sounding portable radio are over. This one also does not come with an adapter so you have to buy that separately from another company. Would I buy it again? Probably not.

Once set up these headphones are not bad for the price. The sound quality is good. However the instructions are useless. The promised aux cable was missing though the charging cable was included. Pairing too an inordinately long time but was ultimately successful. The cushioning feels firm though comfortable. Noise cancellation is good. They charge quickly and the charge lasts.

This is a basic tablet. Had no problems setting it up. The screen resolution is okay but it is slow. Sound quality is sub par, bearable but not the best. It is good for a kid or as a back up. It is fine for simple tasks where speed and optimum performance are not essential. The price is right. If you temper your expectations it is an acceptable entry level device.

This radio is best charged using the cable and charger. The solar doesn't work at all. I left it in bright sun for three days and nothing. There is also a rather flimsy crank. The buttons are hard to use. Sound quality is acceptable. The flashlight and sos function are excellent. I liked that the display shows the amount of battery remaining. It is okay.

This is a basic model. It is limited and there are no smart features. You can connect a roku but there is no bluetooth or wifi. Set up was simple. It is very light and thin. The picture quality is good, clear with vivid colors. Sound quality is disappointing. It is adequate but unimpressive. Much better after attaching a sound bar. I put it in my mother's room. She is just interested in catching her shows so the limited functions don't frustrate her.

I got this player for when I walk the dogs. I have large active animals and we live in an area where cell phone reception is at best sketchy. It is small and the hot pink color makes it hard to lose. It comes with a USB cable or you can use your own AA batteries. Sound quality is acceptable. It is not superlative but in fairness for something this basic, expectations are limited. Unfortunately it goes through batteries like nobody's business. It is inconvenient to have to carry around extras just to make it through a walk. It is better than nothing but disappointing overall.

If price point is your main priority these are certainly an option. Foldable, they come with a small drawstring bag. They pair easily and sound is adequate, not exceptional. The buttons feel flimsy but work and battery life is good. I did not find these comfortable. The foam is rather thin. They seem to straddle the line between over the ear or on the ear. I have a strong preference for over the ear. These are more on than over but not the most comfortable. I did like the headband though. the Just Ask feature is helpful and thit comes with an aux-in cable. The mic is okay. these are not bad phones for the price.

I got this thinking it would provide good entertainment for my mother. It is okay for what it is. It does not have a power switch but an old school pull much like a table lamp. this is great for my mother who has arthritis. It can be wall-mounted or used with the stand. I opted for the stand. It does tend to topple so generally we just lay it on a table. The remote is simpler to use than the buttons on the device. Sound quality is adequate. I don't like the open design; it really should have a cover to protect against dust and dirt. Yes, we do leave a Cd in there as advertised but that is a poor option. Sound quality is adequate for what it is but certainly not impressive. It does connect nicely with other devices. My mother uses the FM radio most.

What attracted me most to these buds was the fact they could be used wired or wirelessly. and that is what disappointed me most. Set up was easy despite the lack of included instructions. You do have to access the instructions online. sound quality is decent; not symphonic but adequate.  The noise cancellation works well when they are wireless but is non-existent when they are wired. They sound like any cheap bud when wired and I was expecting more. I am not a fan of controlling the noise cancellation and EQ via an app. I would prefer it be integrated easily with the button.s. Comfort is average. I admit to not being an earbud fan. these are pretty much on a par with others I've tried. They don't fall out and are no irritating.  Phone call quality is average. The mike does not provide noise cancellation and at most times this is not an issue. They do come with a little pouch. Other than the disappointing performance when wired, these are c certainly adequate buds with superb battery life.

When it works, this speaker provides adequate sound. It is water resistant and the battery life is quite good. My problem is that it constantly cuts out; will work for a few minutes then stops. The adjustment buttons are finicky. There are holes that let water through. When water is in the speaker it muffles the sound. It does sound better when you shake it out but the design could be improved in that regard. It's okay but the unreliable Bluetooth is annoying.

this camera is a mixed bag. Installation and set up was easy enough but the accompanying screws are junk. I wound up using screws from my brother's workshop instead. There are both wired and wireless options. If you opt for wireless be prepared to either hang the camera up high or have a plan for hiding the loose wires. I had hoped to use this for security but the tilt is and motion detection are insufficient. It does not read license plates. The instructions are poor. after using the wireless it just stopped working but when wired it is fine. I much prefer wireless. the sound quality was disappointing, too much buzzing. additionally, the wireless antenna is awkwardly placed on the side. so not really my favourite in terms of performance.

Basic and inexpensive this earphone will do the job. I was impressed by the ease of pairing and the length of time the charge lasted. It worked with sound  and clarity being adequate.I appreciated the car charger because I tend to use it most often in my vehicle.  It is simple to operate but that simplicity does come at a price. First there is no sound control and that is something that is sorely needed. The earpiece is not adjustable and rankly I found it uncomfortable with or without the wire loop. Granted I hate ear buds and the like but can and do use them. But I was conscious of this device the full time it was in my ear. Bottom line it works adeuately lthough not impressively. I do use it in my car and it seems durable. But it is not comfortable and it really needs a volume control.

These are essentially cheap earbuds with a feel good cause. I ad mdit, at the outset, I am not an earbud fan but use them when exercising and walking my dogs. These are fairly comfortable and come with three different sizes of ear cushions. the sound quality is okay but far from tolerable. there is virtually no bass. Better thn nothing but unimpressie een for ear buds. lthough it is en ogue to link products with corporte donations, this tactic leaes me cold. I prefer to donate to the charities of my choice, that I have vetted and feel passionately about rather than being assessed  a fee so a corporate entity can polish its reputation. If you are moved and wwant to py a surcharge for a subpar product, be my guest. So while these buds are more comfortable than most the sound quality is mediocre at best.

I am not a fan of ear buds but was intrigued by the wireless aspect of these. They fit but were not especially comfortable. the carrying case, charger and instructions should all be redone. The instructions are only in pictures and I prefer the written word. Yeah,it's not rocket science but the diagrams are not especially helpful. The charging case is awkward but the charge does last. It would have been helpful if the left and right designations were easy to see. I wore these when walking the dogs. While they didn't fall out, they did lose the connections continuously.Oddly when running on a treadmill they kept falling out but didn't lose connectivity.  Sound quality is acceptable for music but crummy for phone conversations. These are not noise blocking and they picked up a lot of static and background noise during calls. There are many good ideas that should be refined. I use them but they are not my go tos.

I consider earbuds a necessary evil when I am being walked by the dog. Our pace is brisk and music keeps me motivated as I am dragged along. but bus are uncomfortable, easy to lose and don't seem to have a particularly long life span.

These buds are attractive in appearance. the wood accent adds an organic touch, a pleasing nod to style.the instructions however are useless. They are in a teeny tiny eye strain inducing print that is hard to read even with a magnifying glass. However if you have ever paired a device you probably will be able to figure it out without wasting too much time. Pairing was quick and easy and the controls were standard.the phones are charged through a USB port. A complete charge takes about two hours and will last up to ten hours. Sound quality was consistent and good and I was pleased by the performance.

However the sticking point for me with buds is comfort. These felt okay inserted but I never became unaware of their presence. They feel hard and even with the different tips I can'tsay they excelled at comfot. More annoying was the cord and the closure. The oblong battery dangles on the back of the neck something I find irritating. While I don't run with the dog we do speed walk as our outings are as much about exercise as they are companionship. The magnetic closure comes loose. I could not get the cord adjusted to a point where it was comfortable and stayed on when we were walking. They are fine if you are working at your desk but I use over the ear headphones for that. However I have been taking them along with me for travel. They come with a convenient carrying bag. the sound is decent and the mic works well but I wish they rethought the cord design. I am using them but not in the way I intended.

These lightweight headphones are good for when you ar on the go. although they come without a carrying case or bag, they fold and are small enough to tuck in a bag or backpack. They charge via the included USB cable. a full charge takes about 2.5 hours but there is a 15 minute quick charge option that will extend your use by 2 hours. The mic is built in and the button controls (on/off, volume, change tracks, pause for calls and resume ) are on the ear pieces. There are LED indicators for the functions and when charging.

Comfort is okay. The band adjusts for different head sizes and does not bind. The cups are padded but the whole time I had them on I was aware of them. While they did not make my ears sweat or hurt, I couldn't say they were soft or cushiony or especially comfortable. They do not block ambient sound at all. Music quality was adequate. The base is impressive but everything else is fairly pedestrian. It does work well for making and taking calls. They do feel flimsy and one of my ear cups had to be popped back in. At the current asking price of roughly sixty dollars I expect more. They are okay for running errands around town but not comfortable enough for me to wear for an extended period. I liked the portability and lack of weight. Performance was adequate.Quality was fair to middling. all things considered they are average at best with only a superior bass and easy portability to recommend them.

I thought this would be ideal for my office, compact, portable and easy to use. If it had superior sound, so much the better. Unfortunately, it is adequate, not significantly superior to a clock radio you could buy at a discount department store.

On the plus size,, it is compact and light. It can use either batteries or electric and stands either horizontally or vertically. I was annoyed when I first received it that the release of the app had not yet occurred but set it up anyhow to use the speakers. While I wasn't expecting BOSE quality, I was hoping for something more than the tinny sound it emits. You can also play other mp3s, which is a nice feature. When the app is downloaded, the clock works and is easily readable. It is made of black plastic and is fairly inobtrusive.

This App Station is okay. It functions but is not in the least bit impressive in sound or quality. They remind me of the dollar store umbrellas I periodically buy for my office. They do the job without style or flair and if something happens to the, it doesn't break your heart.

The green one glows in the dark. That was a feature I wasn't expecting but has been nice to have! This cover is exactly as stated.  Silicone.  However I have been using it around 2 months now and the silicone has become lax on the top.  When I try to open the case the top slips off without more than a nudge.  I'm always putting it back on.  I do not take my ear buds anywhere.  They sit in my beside table where I listen to audio books in bed while the hubby is sleeping.  I use them 3-5 times a week.  This is important because I don't put them in a pocket,  purse,  booking, or any of the places I expect most people would keep thier earbuds.  If they have that much movement I can't imagine this case to work at all.  Maybe if you put a rubber band around it? The carabiner is a requirement. It holds the case on best it can and is the perfect size to open the case enough to take your buds out and back in.  If you are reading this,  you already know that finding a case for these jbl's is impossible.  I wanted something cute and pink.  I had to settle for lime green but hey,  it flows in the dark which means I can easily find it on my bedside table in the dark!

I love the case.  It is light and works exactly the way it is described but for whatever reason the volume and top buttons are not cut out?  I do not understand why they would be covered with material and not cut out, makes it hard to use those buttons and I am going to cut them out myself which sucks.  Other than that it what you expect for the price and fits my Ipad Air 2 nicely.
I returned this item. It was heavy and uncomfortable to wear. The sound was great!

Simple and sturdy transmitters of sound that can extend the length of your headphone cord, if necessary. However, I discovered that these cords work best when they are NOT plugged into the headset all the way, but part-way. IDK why but that's my experience.

I have had this headset for less than a couple of months now, and right off the bat, the headset body and retractable ear buds are very flimsy feeling but do function. The sound is good, although I do not understand why anyone wouldn't ave noise canceling turned on! That is absolutely horrible when it is not on! It amplifies and echos every single sound. Other headsets don't do this naturally, so not sure why it is even an option. BUT, I have been noticing that the battery seems to run low very quickly, and I thought it was just my imagination at first. After them being on the charger through the night last night, I only have 90% charge? That is not normal for just a couple of months! Does this mean, in the next month it will go down again? And then again? I should have stuck with LG, these off brands really disappoint sometimes. We actually have another BCS brand headset that had to be replaced once, and the second one broke very soon after replacement, so we gave up. I should have known.

I am still trying to figure out all of the functions for these earbuds, since it is all about how you touch or tap them. I end up just using the phone to control them since they don't react very well except for start and stop of audio.

These buds look pretty sleek which is one reason I got them, and live up to the claims for sound and battery life. But they are not comfortable, and they take turns falling out of my ears when I am talking which is very annoying. And yes, I have them in the correct ears (L/R). Also, having to take them out and put them back in the case when I am not using them is inconvenient.

I am going to return them and purchase my usual bluetooth headset, because at least I know they won't fall off and get lost. I paid WAY too much money for these to keep taking that risk, and to also be uncomfortable.

I really wanted to like this speaker. It comes complete with international plugs, an a/c wall charger, and two pouches which I assume is one for the unit and one for the accessories. It is somewhat attractive with a built-in stand that allows you to either place it on its side or in an upright position.

With most speakers, once you have paired it with your device (an Iphone 5s, in my case), you should be all done. This is not so with this unit. The speaker has a spring-loaded slide switch that you push on. It gives you a guitar confirmation tone so that you know that it's working. Now you must go to the "Settings" icon on your device and manually choose the Klipsch speaker. Then you will hear another guitar confirmation tone letting you know that it is paired. You must do this EVERY SINGLE TIME. It is ridiculous. Of course when you turn it off, it will give you yet another guitar confirmation tone.

The sound is very good, but the extra step of always having to re-enable the bluetooth connection through "Settings" totally negates anything positive about this speaker. There is absolutely no reason why my Sony SRSX5 and my JBL Charge automatically pair with my device whenever I turn them on, and yet this one does not. I keep trying to understand why the developers came up with this procedure, but it totally baffles me.

I know that other users have complained in the past about charging issues. Perhaps Klipsch listened to them and fixed this problem because I have not had any difficulties with that.

If you're gonna spend money on a good speaker, please look at the Sony SRSX5. It is an outstanding speaker with logical functions and exceptional sound.
Device is operational but the sound is not the best
Quality isn’t bad for something this small sounds a bit “tinny” but works. Battery life is about 2 hours, it does not hold a charge. I have to charge it every day for work.
You get what you pay for. Not bad for the price, I needed something quick for work, it needed to be small enough for my gym bag. It has a bit of a “tinny” sound but will serve its purpose for now.
This should work but I can't seem to get it working, but will try it on another TV, it could be my Vizio TV as I have had sound issues before.

I bought this because I thought that after charging it would glow visibly in the dark, which makes it easier to find, but it does not glow. The first day I used it, it had a subtle even glow, after that, no matter how long I exposed it to the light, it only (barely) glowed unevenly on one side and not on the other. Seriously, the glow-in-the-dark star stickers I had in the '80s glowed brighter and longer than this.
On the positive side, I do like the shape and the texture, and the cover is easy to install. I do wish the material were slightly thinner on the front, so the buttons are above and not below the level of the cover, but you get used to it quickly, so no biggie. It does have a design flaw where it holds the air tag, the material there is very thick and has no openings, so the sound of the air tag is too faint, almost 20 decibels lower than without the cover, you won't be able to hear it if it fell under the furniture or under the bedsheets/blanket. In any case, the 3-star is mostly due to the fact that it does not glow; otherwise, it's not a bad product.

I bought this during the mad Xmas rush to keep @ my desk @work. It's small enough to fit in the corner of my work cubicle.

Actually, my rating would be a 3.5

Cons: The volume control is inconveniently located in the right hand rear corner. if you keep it at the same volume,it's ok, you don't have to hassle with reaching to the back.

Pros: a plus, the inline MP3 player connection, conveniently located in front. the large numbers for the clock; the CD loading is conveniently located at the top of the unit; the inline is very easy to use and connects instantly at the touch of a button. the top is black, so smudges, ink from your pen or oil from your fingers don't show up as easily as on white.

For the $35 I paid at the register, it's OK for the money.

I was expecting something different. To me, this seemed more suited for a school-age girl or high school because of the fabric and plastic zipper pulls. It did seem OK but the denim was very child-like to me and also had a scratchy feel to it, so I returned it.

Um. These are not active noise cancelling (anc) at all. It seems you must keep the button manually pressed in order to have some slight anc. It was cute & lightweight & audio quality was ok. It was discounted with a coupon so it was a lot less which would have made it okay if you didn’t care about ANC.

These are on the higher end for price given that it feels really cheap. The sound is good but the quality doesn’t feel great. I’m not sure about battery life as I always charge it. This will not link with other devices if the currently link device is near. Bummer. I would have returned it but I’m tired of searching for one and I like the color.

There are some things I love & not love about it. Yes, I would recommended it for the price but I wouldn’t pay more for this.

PROS:
✔️It sounds great.
✔️FM is a great Feature
✔️Connecting to a device is easy
✔️Affordable
✔️Option for plugging it in instead of wireless
✔️Folds into compact size for traveling

CONS:
🚫Yes it sounds great but sometimes I hear static. Turning it off and back on seems to fix this issue.

I had to google this because I couldn’t figure out why I couldn’t connect. Each time you switch devices, you have to disconnect the one you’re connected to and connect it to the new device. I watch a lot of movies on my laptop and the sound was just not loud enough for me to put the laptop down and be 2 - 3 feet away from it. So, I bought the [[ASIN:B0036VO6IC Logitech Laptop Speaker Z205]].

The speaker was a bit smaller than I expected, but no big deal. The sound quality isn't bad, not the best, but okay. Unfortunately, the sound doesn't go much louder than the laptop speakers.

It's handy to have and my kids borrow it for their laptops, too. Over all, it's not bad.

Not easy to use the earbud controls - you have to use the app and the settings don't stick.  Ended up turning off all controls (volume, noise cancellation, Siri etc.) and just using it as plain vanilla ear phones.

I spend a lot of time untangling.  The one I owned before was flat and did not twist up, this one is cloth-like.  Also the sound quality isn't as nice.  I'm thinking about returning.  Stop-pause button went out on my previous one after a year and a half, so I was afraid to re-purchase.
Very poor sound quality. If I could return it, I would.
It says in the description "extra bass". Perhaps they're speaking about the fish?? RETURNED. I currently have a cheap set of Phillips earbuds that sound 100% better.
Not good quality sound,

so Ppl don’t get confused the speakers both look like the one that is covered in black mesh, no yellow is visible on either speaker, it says 36 Watts on the speaker not 180, they are pretty good I like the bass and sound 👌🔥. Got these to replace Bose companion 2 series 2 and gotta say they aren’t much louder than those old ass Bose ones so ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

The first week I had the unit I was extremely impressed w the power and clarity of the Nova300. Then it started making a very annoying high-pitch whine when it was on. Sent it back to Peachtree for repair.

A little buggy.  The volume could stand to be louder, but works.  The bugs seem to be in recognizing that you called its "hot word" (amazon/echo/alexa).  Frequently wakes up when it shouldn"t.  I love the concept of the Echo line, but we desperately need open sourced development on them.  And for god's sake make it easier to search the web for stuff vs asking for wikipedia - without signing up for some service.  Also the skills are nice, but you have to remember which ones you are signed up for in order to use them...not real user friendly.

This is the best thing I did for my laptop. I use my laptop in bed, about 1-1/2 hours when I get up and about 2 hours before sleeping. Because I place my laptop directly on the comforter above my lap, I feel a lot of heat quickly. My friend told me that it slows my laptop and shortens the life of the laptop, I decided to order the fan. I keep hooking this fan up to my pc whole time ever since I got this. This is super light weight that I can take this bundle everywhere in my house. There is a very quiet humming sound that never bothers anything. Also this has replaced the laser toy for my cats. They are attracted to the blue light that emits from the fan. Since the light are reflecting on my white comforter in many directions, I just have to move my legs a bit time to time. They go nuts chasing the blue light. I sometimes cool my over heated iphone on it too. I love this fan. Thanks!!

1 year update: Changed 5 stars to 3.
Just before Fourth of July vacation, the fan quit responding. This is after 11 months and a half since my purchase.
It was working wonderfully until the last moment. I felt my legs getting hot and realized that the fan wasn't working. I changed the cable, did not work, then cleaned the mesh that covered the fans and tried, still did not work. After coming back from vacation I consulted to store, but they could not do anything about it. Sadly Amazon did not list anywhere to contact the seller, so I could not return the item even it came with 1 year warranty. I am not going to buy item from the seller who does not list their contact information.

I really wanted to like this for the price point and description of being a little higher amps. Of course I did not expect nor need bose sound but needed better than internal from Mac mini. Even tested on my surface laptop and just could not get any sound level above like a 3 or 4.

Build seemed exactly what I wanted but if you can't hear anything what good is a sound bar.

I ended up returning it. Could have been a bad unit could also be user error but trying on multiple devices, doubtful. Picked up those top rated round type. Work well and sound good and can get up to like a 10 in volume.

Again love design of the sound bar and value but for me it did not work as expected. Could have been a bad unit.

Like many posting have stated the ear pads are well.. cheap and provide little comfort with minimal use. Just received my pair and put on for first use. After tweaking the EQ the sound is good. For the money this was a good buy and I would buy again at the sale price as long as I know there is a better ear pad replacement that will fit. The ear pad on button side came apart at seam in that 1st use. Maybe this is old inventory (thus sale price!) that sat in a warehouse and the heat got to them. In any event many who posted have had this problem so, it is either that or, the pads are very very cheap for a top brand headset maker with an original premium price! Not a positive endorsement of their (Soul not Amazon) quality control.

I contacted Soul direct to see about a replacement ear pad before trying to send back to Amazon. A test of their customer service.

The Jawbone has great sound, and people can actually hear you. The problem I have with it is that it doesn't stay on my ear. I've tried using all of the sizes in this kit, but the slim design of the loop just pops off, especially when you put on sunglasses. Also, I have now broken all of the ear things. I stick it in my purse and since it is such a small piece of plastic,they break very easily. If my work hadn't paid for this piece of junk I would send it back.

Update: I just realized this review went to the earwires. I don't like the jawbone. If you like it, the replacement wires were fine. They just don't fit my small ears - including the small size.

I got this card for my son so he could start streaming his gaming. This card looked like it might be the answer, but I think it comes up short. I do understand that it's not a higher end card, but I think we were hoping for more. The audio is very underwhelming and has to be boosted and the video quality doesn't really seem to be what I would expect from a 1080p card. Not only does it look mildly grainy to me, but is much darker than it needs to be and the color pallete seems off.

Yeah, it does most of what it is supposed to, but if you want to get serious and put out a quality stream, this might leave you wanting.

All in all, it's passable for the price.
The sound quality is ok but I wanted to be able to connect to a better speaker. Bluetooth and auxiliary cable options have not worked well if at all.

I’ve had this for 8 months with no issues, then I got an under-the-desk treadmill and the screens go black and immediately come back on ALL THE TIME. I’ve tried using different plug ins for the treadmill and computer, not it (my husband is an electrician and assured me this was not it.). When testing this theory and intentionally removing power and plugging back in, the monitor had a setting box pup-up…. Because it lost powder, great. But when the screen flashes that box doesn’t come up which tells me it’s not loosing power-it’s loosing a connection to the computer. After messing with it and becoming frustrated, I thought I heard a little zap noise where it’s located so when I started feeling around I got a very minor static shock on my finger. So my Inspector Gadget hat told me that I was generating static electricity with my treadmill and for some reason it was collecting on this dual monitor plug and basically shorting itself out. (This only happens when walking on the treadmill.) So, in all my Mom-knowing madness, I wrapped it up in a dryer sheet and it actually works for the most part. It might flash a couple times in a day but my office smells amazing. I will be looking for something else for sure. It’s really annoying.
very slim but sound quality is a little poor

So much fun. Had to wait to get it shipping was late. Product is nice if you get the keyboard. I would of returned it if i did not have this option. It is to klutz without. Now it is like a mini computer and  so fun. The batter life stinks. It does not last long at all maybe 4 hours or 5 that's it. The 7 and 8 inch last close to 10 hours. A 32 mb is perfect and i believe i can add. Extra memory card. Sound is fantastic. Problem is with shutting off and restarting it is hard to get it to restart without plugging in the cord , even when it is fully charged, and getting it to open up the start screen. I always buy the warranty so i have to call it in and this checked out. Good deal. I bought the package micro soft, keyboard, and fire for 144 good deal. Thanks Amazon you did it again.

Nice bright sound - wish the bass went down to 25 hertz but can add a sub. Bluetooth connection issue is that you almost always have to reconnect - doesn't do it automatically and each time you have to turn up the sound on the speaker because it seems to default to minimum after shutting down. Let me just put it out there, I need 3 - 4 alarms to wake me up in the morning, and I sort of believe after owning so many clocks I shouldn't need to read instructions to figure out how to operate one..... well... I had to...

Pros
- The light is bright enough to definitely grab my sleepyhead's attention, but not annoying enough to make me wake up on the wrong side of the bed.
- There's brightness control. I am totally okay with setting it at level 8 (out of 10 I believe).
- Can also use as night light (that doesn't blind you in the middle of the night because it lights up gradually)
- No snooze button (is it a good thing?)

Cons
- The alarm sound is very mono-tone, no option to change the volume (or I just didn't find it).
- For a alarm this size it's not weighted enough that if you try to just press the button the unit gets moved easily. I find this part annoying when I am trying to turn the alarm off.
- No snooze button (is it a bad thing?)

Love the color and cover design. Do not love the stylus loop - bad location and too loose. That thing is going to fall out of there - no biggie during COVID and I am at home 24/7 but it is not secure enough for me to travel with it anywhere. It also covers the on/off and volume switches - very annoying.

I gave this a three star instead of a five. The unit was easy to install, the picture quality and sound quality is great. It all works great. The dome lights are bright and work great. However, the company said they would not warrant the player for two years but instead a 90 day only, all because I installed it. They said if I had a qualified installer they would warrant the player for two years. This player was very easy to install and I am not going to pay someone when  I can  do it myself.  The wiring was straight forward and easy to hook up.

Purchased end of Oct2019 to Dec2019, the left audio channel has faded.  Not exactly certain where the issue is, both left and right audio was fine, but across a couple devices tested and the left audio is only 15-20% output volume compared to right.  The cable did take a few hard tugs as it did get hung on objects such as chairs or door nobs -- uncertain why the effect is faded sound vs no sound output - prior to "my issue" the sound quality was actually pretty  decent the bass was deep albeit artificially spacious-sounding.  I also struggled with the fit on my ears; admittedly, my ears are on the smaller side, thus I was constantly re-adjusting ear placement of the headphones. The noise isolating is just that if the ear piece sits tightly, make note that this is not noise cancelling as there is no active component to this product.
It solved my Hactintosh audio problems and it sounds fine, not great

SUPER comfortable headset. They honestly sound great but i expected a bit better.

Audio quality is good but no better than the competition in my opinion. Bass in the headset could be better.

Sounds quality is good.
When using noise canceling during phone calls it sounds equivalent to plugging your ears completely so you cannot hear yourself talking and end up talking louder (annoys everyone in the viscinity!) and picks up more noise on the mic, i.e. shuffling papers, dishes, bags (I can no longer multitask when using for phone calls).

Pros: I love the feel of the case. The slim genuine leather case sits well in my hand. It fits the phone perfectly and will hold up to 3 cards securely. The side rails protect the face nicely. There is easy access to the fingerprint scanner and volume control.
Cons: I have had the product for only 7 months and the leather is wearing away from all four corners. I generally carry my phone in a purse and rarely in hand or pocket where it could be scraped.
Bottom line: It is a good buy if you don't mind replacing it for esthetic reasons in less than a year.

Most people purchase this wireless keyboard to use at home with their TV or other media setup. I actually purchased it to use at work as a more ergonomic option. No, this is not billed as an ergonomic keyboard, but the main issue I was having was reaching for the mouse, so I wanted something with a built-in trackpad. Surprisingly, there are VERY FEW options available, particularly within a reasonable price range (<50) and offered by a name brand company.

Prior to purchasing this keyboard, I tried another which featured the trackpad front and center ([[ASIN:B004KN7PZG Gear Head USB Smart Touch II Touchpad Keyboard]]). Unfortunately, that product was way too glitchy, and the size was not ideal. I thought that the center trackpad would work well given that I'm used to using one on my laptop at home (a [[ASIN:B00IPQXZ62 Dell XPS Convertible 2 in 1]], which has a near-ideal keyboard), but that did not seem to be the case. When I began looking for keyboards with a built-in trackpad on the side, this one by Microsoft seemed to be the only viable option, although I wasn't looking for wireless.

I did like that that the keyboard is Microsoft, and I like the clean look and design. Compared to the prior keyboard that I tried, this one definitely has a more comfortable feel. Although it is small, there is adequate spacing around the keys, something the prior keyboard lacked. There is no number pad--the trackpad replaces this--but as I never used this anyway, this is no loss for me. All of the keys are a nice size, including the shift keys (these are sometimes skimped upon). Unfortunately, there is no "End" key--I knew that upon purchasing, but I still miss it. What I did NOT realize is that in order to access the Function keys, you actually have to HOLD DOWN the "FN" button. This is a bit of a pain for me, as I use Refresh (F5) constantly, so this is now a 2-handed operation. This keyboard is also missing any kind of indicator for CAPS LOCK.

The trackpad is okay. I still have my mouse plugged in, and unfortunately, I find myself using it too often, as the trackpad is not completely reliable. It does accept multi-finger scrolling gestures, which is nice, and it does pretty well with simple up-down navigation; however, I have found that side-to-side is much more uneven. I do like that there is a left-hand click button on the right side of the keyboard, and I have made use of this at times. But I've also found that sometimes my palm randoming activates the trackpad when I am typing, causing the cursor to flip to a new spot on screen, which is annoying. So, at best, this has been just average.

This keyboard includes other features that I don't use--e.g., a volume control, a separate mute button (are both necessary?), home and other "hot" keys, etc. I'm assuming that these extras would be more beneficial to someone using the keyboard in a home media setting. For my needs, this keyboard has been okay. The layout is decent, although it could have been much, much better with a few minor changes. Depending on how you plan to use it, I would recommend it with reservations.

I have owned my Sangean WFR-20 for a little over a month. I appreciate the sound and ease of navigation on the menu wheel and the remote. The speakers sound very good at low, mid and high volumes. The selection of stations is large (though a bit cumbersome to find on the radio itself - I highly recommend registering the radio and using the Reciva portal to identify "My Stations").

My biggest complaint is the unreliability of the connection. My radio is only about 3 feet (through a wall, though) from my router and the radio issues will occur at times when my other devices or computers do not have a problem. The issue is that the radio will disconnect and go back to "Initializing Network" status. Once the connection is resolved, it goes right back to the menu and sits on the "Stations" menu item. The backlight doesn't go off and the radio doesn't play. This is highly annoying for me as I use the radio to assist in sleep. It is too frequent that the lack of sound wakes me and I find myself messing with my radio in the middle of the night. I have downloaded firmware updates, but the issue remains. I have searched for solutions but the only reliable solution is to "unplug, plug back in, try again." I am hoping that future firmware updates can identify better network connection testing, redundancy or quick reconnect and "resume" functionality to go back to the station that was playing before. I haven't tried moving my router and trying a wired connection (after all, this is a wireless internet radio!).

The other minor annoyance is that one cannot see the time when a station is playing. I know what station I selected, so don't need it to be what is displayed the entire time the radio is on. Since it has a nice clock feature, I would rather see the time displayed unless I am using the menu. And given the fact I have to unplug the radio several times a week, it would be ideal if the radio could just connect to the internet to identify the real date/time and use a saved "Time Zone" setting to auto-set the clock. As it is, I have to manually reset the date and time each time.

Other than these issues, the radio is solid, good-looking, great-sounding and a decent value. I do think that the Squeezebox Boom (though pricier) is a better overall internet radio. Plus, it has an easier interface to control from your desk/laptop. The Sangean can be controlled remotely, but it isn't elegant.
Ordered these buds on May 6th and the right one has already stopped putting out sound. The left one still works as long as I have the mute bud in my ear. Oh well, that was a lot of money wasted.

Kind of disappointed! I had the Momentum over ear headphones & they were amazing. Their fit was the problem. I've seen they corrected this on the Momentum 2's.

So I decided to get the in ear Momentums but the sound signature is "weird". They're okay but not as "memorable" as the over the ear or their CX models.

Got a pair of these for Christmas 2014 for working out purposes.

PRO's
1. Very convenient
2. Works as intended
3. No issues of getting tangled or in the way of. My workouts

CON's
1. Not as loud as it could be. If you get a good seal to your ear they sound great and the volume is sufficient
2. But that's part of the issue. Trying to get and KEEP a good bud to ear seal is frustrating to say the least & a good seal lasts maybe a minute or two.

1.12.15 - I thought the magnets that clasped the 2 buds together didn't work but, oops user error the magnets do work very well I was not connecting in the most magnetic area.

Other the. That they're okay for the price I guess. Come to find out now in 2015 almost everyone and anyone who makes headphones are coming out with Bluetooth wireless headsets!!
On a scale from 1-10 is give these a solid 6.5 or weak 7
JBL needs to rethink the ear bud design & try to perfect the seal orrrrr crank up the amps so the volume can get higher
There is some type of nose guard??? I cut it off, felt weird to me. The speakers are move-able and the sound is pretty good. I use them for meditation and quite time. Soft fabric
Too dim for a large audience or use anywhere beyond pitch dark.

It's not always true you get what you pay for, but it's not a bad rule to live/shop by. And I'd say it perfectly describes this projector. It does a basic job and for what you pay, that's about what you should expect. No bells and whistles, not great quality, but "sufficient." It's up to you therefore to decide what perks/quality you want and how much you're willing to pay for it.

it is light, has a small footprint, has several means of connecting, all postives
it's a bit clunky to set for a height and some of the controls

Its clarity and brightness don't come close to matching my Epson (I often teach outdoors and can't use this projector as it's washed out in comparison), whether we're talking visibility or sharpness of text. That said, the Epson is 150-200 dollars more expensive. Is it worth it? I need that brightness and clarify for my purposes (showing lots of text) and settings (often outdoors). But if you are watching movies indoors in a relatively darkened room, then this will be adequate to that purpose and save you a good amount of money.

Sound is the same. Not as good as my Epson, and when we show movies in our driveway, I hook up external speakers, so I like better sound. But again, if that's not a big deal to you, it can suffice.

For the price, it's a decent value. I'd pay more for more, but that's a personal choice

This is a decent fan if you're looking for something pointed right at you from not far away. If that's the case I'd bump it to a 4/5 rating. I dinged it to a 3 because it isn't a very flexible fan it terms of usage save for that.

Pros
very small footprint
lightweight
seems solidly enough constructed despite the lightness
USB charge
swivels up or down, mechanism is smooth
looks nice

Moderate
As noted, you really need to be pretty close to it. This is not something you'll feel from four or five feet away. If you're working at a desk and have it there pointed at you you'll be fine. But beyond that kind of "right there" situation it won't be very useful

noise: It's noisier than some small fans and quieter than others. I'd say it leans more to the "quieter" side, and if the sound is noticeable at least it isn't at all unpleasant Just a noticeable whirr rather than a whine or clatter

No variable speed: normally I'd put this as an out and out con, but given how small a breeze this creates and how close you need to be, I don't think three speeds would have any significant degree of difference amongst them

Cons: no really deal breakers and major issues/annoyances

This is a decent speaker with some nice touches, but only for those who listen to music occasionally and are fine with "good enough if I can hear it" sound. Details

Size: relative small footprint--bigger than a lot of better sounding bluetooth speakers, but also comes with extras so can't fault them on size.

Pairing: paired easily and immediately with all our IOS devices--phones and iPads, and our Mac laptops. Never lost signal

Clock: nice and bright, easy to read, easy to set

Q1 charge-worked with all our compatible devices with no problems at all, couldn't be easier to use

battery life about as promised--we went 6+ hours twice

dual speakers are distinguishable

The downside as noted at the top is sound. It isn't horrible--it's clear enough. But it's definitely thin if not tinny, and lacks a full, rich output/range. We have a Denon, a Jam, and a UE Boom, and all are noticeably, significantly better, richer, fuller sounding. (they obviously don't come with clocks or wireless charging).

that said, my wife thought his sounded "fine". It's all in your expectations and desires. I would not use this as a listening device; she'd be perfectly happy with it. So know where you are in the "how good does my music need to be and how often do I listen to it" spectrum

Short story of the review is that these are just as they say they are--a pair of relatively inexpensive "basic" earphones. As such, they seem to be a decent value and have some good points, but if you're looking for sound quality over price, you'll want to go elsewhere.

Pros:
Packaging: small and minimalist as it should be

Provided with: multiple size earbuds caps and ear inserts (more on these later), a very short charging cable, and a decent zip-around traveling pouch

Pairing: No problem with any of my Apple devices. Instantly recognized and paired with an iPhone (8 and 6), iPad (Pro and Air 2), and MacBook Pro. Couldn't be quicker or easier each and every time

Comfort: This was an issue for me, though obviously this is a pretty subjective category. I had to step down immediately to the small caps/rings, which is no surprise--I do that with I think all of my earbuds. But even with the smalls I just couldn't get a a good seal or a comfortable, though oddly enough much worse with my right. The left was not "great" but was certainly good; right was a bad seal and wholly uncomfortable no matter what I tried. Weird.

Sound quality: Again, it's a matter of pricing here. I don't own many basics and it's been years since I've had a set of lower-tier earbuds, so it's hard for me to compare at an equal level. The sound is what I'd call adequate, especially for exercise or listening to an audiobook. But there's no comparison to my PowerBeats3 or Jaybird X2s, and not even to my Jabra Elites, which I"d call my mid-range ones. The first two are in a whole other class in terms of range, sharpness, richness, and comfort, while the Jabras are a good step up in both sound and comfort. Sound here is more than a little thin at both ends, and just not very rich or full. Less noticeable with an audiobook, but definitely not the buds I'd choose if I'm focusing on listening to music, as opposed to having background sound while I"m doing something else. Phone quality is pretty similar--adequate, at times a bit muddy.

Controls: easy, intuitive, and responsive

Overall, if you want a basic set where quality of sound isn't a deal breaker, or a pair of cheaper ones for places you might have to worry about forgetting them, these will suit the bill, assuming you don't have the same comfort issue I did. But for someone looking for rich, full sound, particularly for music, I'd strongly advise moving up the ladder

Ears is a mixed bag in comparison to similar items

Pros:
Highly portable: it's light and easy to carry in the hand, has a small footprint

Easy set-up: It paired easily with my iPhone, and setting up the wi-fi connection and then the connection to my Amazon account was quick and painless. Took no more than a minute or two

Alexa: This is my only Alexa device, so I can't say how it does in comparison to others, but it's so far been mostly (more on that in the cons) a good experience. It's responsive, and rarely requires a repeat of any given command so long as I'm within about 10 feet. Farther than that and I need to really speak up and occasionally repeat myself, but only once typically, not four or five times

Waterproof: I confess I haven't tested this, so I'm just going with the product description, but it's a nice feature to have for such a portable speaker

Cons
Wi-fi connectivity: While set-up was a breeze, I've had several issue with it momentarily dropping wi-fi. The first time I listened for half an hour and it dropped wi-fi once. The second time, it dropped wi-fi repeatedly, not once getting through an entire song in about 20-30 minutes of listening. The third time, also about half an hour, fell somewhere in the middle, dropping wi-fi three times. It's a momentary drop--about a 2-3 second pause, but it's sure an annoying one. If things change I'll update, but if this stays an issue I'll certainly not be using this even though I like the Alexa aspect

Sound: I'd put this somewhere between Pro and Con. It's not bad sound at all, but it's a little thin. I also have a Jam Heavy Metal and the sound on that is definitely richer and more full. It's not a chasm, but it is noticeable. I have a few others that I'd say the Blast is comparable to, so again, it isn't like this one is bad, just not the best of what I own.

There's a lot to like about this, and even despite the sound, I'd be tempted to use this over my Jam just for the Alexa, but the wireless is definitely an issue if that doesn't clear up

OK, I’ll preface this by saying that while I have used Windows machines, I prefer Macs. So get that out of the way early. As for this particular laptop:
1) it felt a tad unresponsive to me, not horribly so, but noticeably so, at least in comparison to my 2-yr-old Macbook Pro. Certainly faster than my other, older laptop (5 yrs old), but still things seemed to lag a bit disappointingly
2) It’s nicely thin, you can see the dimensions and weight. It feels a bit heavy to me in terms of true portability, especially for having plastic parts
3) I wish it felt more sturdy. The top is strong, and the hinge feels nicely solid and durable. But the bottom and keyboard sections--the black plastic parts-- feel cheap. And I’m not a fan of the slightly rough texture on the trackpad. Keyboard is a nice full size. I prefer a very sensitive, speedy trackpad, so default settings were slow for me, but easy to change. I also find the glare from the black border a bit distracting at times.
4) Wi-fi and Bluetooth set up were easy and quick whether pairing devices or connecting to my network. No problems at all.
5) This isn't a review of Windows 8, so I'll leave that alone save to say I'm not a fan. If you are, this is it.
6) The touch screen is responsive and pretty accurate, though for the life of me I can't figure out who is looking for a touch screen on a laptop. Obviously, some people must like it, but I can't imagine using it hardly at all due to the horrible ergonomics of it. If you're looking for a touchscreen laptop, this seems more than sufficiently responsive and accurate.
7) screen is colorful and bright. Sound is solid--nothing to write home about, but not too tinny. It is a laptop after all. Certainly fine for streaming youtube videos and if you're not picky, movies.
8) Not sure I'm buying the battery life based on a few days of use, but I'll update as needed

It's always hard to compare cross platform. Given a choice between this brand new one and my two-year-old Mac, I wouldn't even consider switching. But then, this computer isn't really aimed at switchers I'd guess. If I can imagine just starting out neutral--probably impossible to do--I think I'd find it a mid-range product: a little noticeably slow in some respects, a tad heavy but not deal-breakingly so, some sense of durability in the aluminum and hinge but feeling a bit cheap in the other parts, decent screen and sound, very quick and easy plug-and-play-and-connect set-up, a "bonus" touchscreen that I probably wouldn't use at al.

The home is a decent little alarm clock/speaker, though not always the finest in terms of design.

What does it do?
Acts as an alarm. Some people I noted were annoyed that you had to cycle through the minutes to set the time and alarm and while an hour button is easier, if you hold down the button it really zips through pretty quickly. In other words, you really don't have to plod through minute by minute. To give a sense of that, it took me 10 seconds to speed from 6:00 am to 10:00 am. So really, this isn't much of an issue in my mind. It has two alarms, which is a nice touch. The alarm can go to either the radio or to your input device, though that is a bit iffy depending on your device. It worked with my ipod touch but you're going to want to make sure your device works as it should. One problem is that it is not very easy to see in the dark.

Acts as a radio: the reception was quite good; I had no trouble with local stations. All tuned in well.

Acts as a speaker: the sound is decent for what it is. It certainly isn't going to replace your stereo or even a set of decent bluetooth speakers, but that isn't really its goal and for what it's meant to do, and what its probably target audience is (children, tweens, young teen) I'm sure it's fine.

Work with audio devices--this is a bit mixed. I've had variability with a range of Apple products. They all work in terms of producing sound, but the volume varied amongst them at times so that even with the volume all the way up on both devices it was surprisingly low. Not inaudible or anything, but not loud enough for good entertainment (probably OK for an alarm). You also just basically sit your device atop between two plastic "walls"--there's no cradle or anything and so there isn't much difference between that and just lying it flat next to or atop it. It charged my devices, but it's not a charging cradle, which would have been nicer. Instead there is a USB charge slot on the bottom of the device and you use your own charging cable. The same is true for the audio--you use a cable jack into your device (this one is provided) to link the two. It's an adequate design, if not an elegant one.

Glow/change colors: Well, it does do this. My response? Meh. But then, again, I'm really not I'm assuming the target audience. It doesn't do a anything for me, but kids and tweens might find it interesting. At the least, it isn't obnoxious (not too bright, not too fast-changing, etc.)

it's plastic, but it feels pretty hefty and the build seems decent if a little cheap. I certainly didn't have the sense that it would be fragile or break down soon or anything.

in the end, I'd say it's a decent little device for a tween sort. Not sure it's worth 50 dollars, but it's not exorbitant, just maybe a little pricey. If you're just looking for a speaker, I'd say there are bluetooth ones out there that provide better sound for the price. But if you want a speaker/alarm/radio/something to look at now and then, it's a decent purchase.
So far it works as advertised, but there is a slight buzzing sound coming from it. Will see how it works out, I have it behind my night stand so I'm hoping the noise will not bother me.

These cables really have a very forward sound, and almost are harsh in their presentation. Depending on your system, I guess this could be a good thing - for instance, if you wanted to bring a more laid back/warmer setup and give a real kick. But for me, it just wasn't pleasant to listen to. I much preferred the AC-14s, which really open things up and bring out detail without harshness.

If you don't believe power cables make a difference, I'd challenge you to purchase these and compare them against the AC-14s.

It's a well-made cable though, and some will certainly like how it affects the sound.

I found it odd, reading some of these reviews, which claimed that these Sonys were definitely better than the Pioneer BS22s. Very odd indeed. It makes me wonder if they either weren't directly comparing the two back and forth, or didn't have the Pioneers set up properly: ~6 feet apart, toed in toward the listener, ear level, grills off.

To my ears, the Sonys aren't much better than the Micca MB42x. They both have slightly elevated treble, and are rather thin and one-note sounding in their presentation. Not a lot of depth or punch.

The BS22s however, you really "feel" the music. The soundstage is very open, and everything sounds larger even though the woofers are only 4" compared to the 5-1/4" SSCS5s. There is depth and a musicality that just can't be matched by the Sonys, and it's apparent right away. It's like they almost disappear and you're just left with the music. Most speakers in this price range are going to sound similar to the SSCS5/MB42x, not many if any are going to sound like the Pioneers.

I must have switched back and forth 200-300 times comparing the two, trying to convince myself that the Sonys were better than they were. I got them at $73 and the BS22s at $99, so I really wanted to like the SSCS5s.

It was always obvious which speaker was superior though - not once did I say "oh, the Sonys really sound better here". That's not to say these are bad speakers, but I don't think they're worth much more than $73, the sale price. The Pioneers however I'd be willing to pay their retail price and a bit more. If you're really on a budget, you could be satisfied with these ~$73, especially if you're only concerned about watching movies. But if you are willing to pay $20 more for the Pioneers when they're on sale (or even at $129), I'd recommend it.

Just remember to set the BS22s up properly: ~6 feet apart, toed in toward the listener, ear level, grills off. Also make sure they're properly amped.

The SSCS5s are decent and cheap enough that I decided to use my old receiver with them at my computer. I'd probably prefer them over the MB42X slightly, but that's about it.

With a budget sub like the Dayton SUB-1200 properly placed (subwoofer crawl) along with the BS22s, you'll have a system that sounds very nice and hits above its weight class - trust me on that. It used to be that headphones were a cheaper investment than speakers and you could get a better sound for less, but this set up edges out my HE-500/Bifrost/Asgard 2 and it's actually cheaper. Didn't think that was possible.

This is a decent recorder, but the recording quality is pretty tinny. I was surprised that the Lamyik I also tried had better quality despite looking less visually impressive. I'm not affiliated with them in any way, just giving my opinion based on trying both of them. I have two recording examples, I might post them later.

I like these headphones. I have a problem with ear buds in general. They either fall out of my ears or they cause too much ear pressure and I can't wear them because it's too painful.
These mostly stayed in my ears. One fell out of my ear into a sink of soapy water and still worked. Another time one fell to the ground and now the buttons are broken, but they still play.
The sound is pretty good. I mostly listen to audiobooks. No complaints.
The battery seems pretty amazing.
Overall, I know I have a hard time keeping earbuds in my ears. I'm pretty sure it's my ears. They don't cause pressure or pain.
They're cheap enough to buy again when they stop working. Which I hate to say because it's not good for the planet, but it's true.

I llke the size and the easy book reading. Also great volume when using audio books. The stand is not usefull and very stiff.
Bought what I thought was ADD FREE, but alas, it still shows more Amaxon games between each episode..I HATE that.
I also object to how hard it is to get some apps if they are free.
After I bought the #10 at regular price, I expected it to be easier to use. And what does add free REALLY mean??

Seems sufficient when I connect to my phone to talk; my friends I sound loud and clear. But if you're recording, even just voice memos for yourself, I can't recommend. The recording is crackly, staticky, and full of pops. It sounds like a long-distance call.

I've been using a Sony X55 for 7 years and it finally gave up the ghost. The XB33 was the perfect size to replace it, however the sound quality was below par.

The X55 had a wonderfully balanced sound with the woofer and two tweeters giving tight bass and crisp mids and highs. The xb33 with just two woofers has almost no mids and the highs are muddy at best. The xb33 DOES play much LOUDER then the x55, so for parties this would be the better choice. However, my needs are for low to mid volume while camping, so I tried the xb43.

The xb43, with two woofers and two tweeters has the balanced sound I wanted. The size sucks: The xb43 looks and feels much larger and is MUCH HEAVIER. (nothing is free)

I returned the xb33 and kept the xb43.

This device is multifunctional but feels cheaply made. The plastic housing doesn't feel that well made and neither is the remote control. It works fine (for now) but I question whether this light will still work months from now. If I didn't know it was over $30 I would have guessed it was a $15-20 unit.

I plugged it in and immediately a loud, English-accented voice yelled out something about Bluetooth. Not a good first impression. The volume control can't be controlled on the unit itself (I tried). It can also be changed using the remote control. This is inconvenient if you accidentally misplace the control.

The colors and patterns are nice but don't stare into the projector light! (Easy to do because it's so big and round) I accidentally stared at the light source and it made my eyes hurt. Not a good sign. If using with children, warn them.

Note there is no batteries included with the remote. For the price, you would think batteries would be included. There is no AC/DC adapter either - it has to be plugged into the USB outlet. However, this is pretty standard nowadays.

The Bluetooth speaker (located on the bottom of the unit) works well. There are white noise sounds and the usual standard sounds (ocean waves, forest, etc).

Overall, the quality is average. The combination of the loud, annoying voice (and lack of volume control on the unit itself), the irritating lights, the lack of batteries for the control and the high price tag do not impress me.

I was expecting a portable lightweight Bluetooth speaker that I could pack into my bag. Instead, I received a rather chunky piece of plastic. The speaker is the size of a thick paperback. While it works well and has pretty good sound, it's not exactly lightweight. If you're going to the beach, this one will take up room in your bag, though you could certainly use it as a paperweight to hold down a blanket. But generally I prefer lighter Bluetooth speakers. So a mixed review.

I love the color and it's smooth to the touch, but it looks more durable on screen than in person. It's made of two parts - the cover is very thin and feels like cardboard that's been covered up with a thin layer of plastic (painted to look like faux purple leather) with the inside sporting a thin, microfiber interior. The second half is made of hard, cheap plastic (they call it a "polycarbonate shell" to make it sound fancier).

If it wasn't made specifically for the Fire 6, I doubt it would sell for as much as it does. As it is, I will use it as a decorative case for my Kindle Fire but it feels very cheaply made, so I would handle it very carefully.

At the current Amazon price, this set of two universal remotes is a great buy.

However, I'm not clear about why anyone would need to buy TWO remotes at a time when the purpose of getting a universal remote is to reduce clutter and the number of remotes you own. One remote handles 3 devices, while the other handles the 3 PLUS 3 other ones. So why wouldn't I use the 6 device remote alone, since it includes everything?

My guess is that this product is aimed at households with at least 2 TVs. However, the price is so cheap that you're basically getting an extra remote for almost nothing. It's wasteful but hard to turn down because of the price.

The packaging and the instructions are confusing. RCA claims that one remote controls 3 devices while the other one controls 6. However, the 3-device one actually controls MORE than 3 - it just uses one button to control the DVD/VCR (it treats 2 devices as 1), one button for the TV, and another for the combination Satellite/Cable/digital TV converter. The second device is even more comprehensive -it offers buttons for all of the above PLUS one for the DVR/Aux 1, VCR/Aux 2, and Audio.

The two remotes also look different cosmetically - the 6 device one is shiny and glossy while the other is a matte black. Not sure why this is.

Having one VCR, one DVD, one TV, one cable box and an audio deck with a set of speakers, I used the "6 device" remote. My audio deck with attached speakers, which are circa 1988, would not work with the codes. However, switching from DVD to VCR went smoothly, as did from TV to cable.

In conclusion, the universal remote functioned well overall and cleared up the clutter of remotes beneath my coffee table. I liked the battery saver function - if you by chance lost your remote between your sofa cushions, the battery turns off after awhile.

Now if I could only find a way to use my 3-device remote...
