I've had these earbuds for a few months now and thought I'd revise my review.

My main gripe with these expensive but ultimately underwhelming earbuds is that they make a "thwomping" sound inside your ear drum whenever you jog or walk fast with them. I was at the gym recently and the sound of the earbuds jostling about in my ears was distracting. I don't recall ever having that problem with cheaper earbuds. This sound persisted even after I customized the buds to fit the shape of my ear.

On the positive side, the sound is decent though the bass and treble weren't that impressive. Its most effective feature was the noise-cancelling feature, which effectively blocked out any other noise. It worked so well that I would never use these buds while driving, crossing traffic or walking alone home late at night. With the spate of iPhone robberies, it's better to be able to hear a stranger's footsteps behind you. It's perfect, however, when you're on a subway or a bus and you want to block out that annoying person next to you who insists on complaining about her day.

The set includes a microphone for your iphone, which I don't use that much but works well enough - I heard my friend's voice on the other end of the line in very crisp, clear tones.

What's convenient is that the buds work with even the oldest ipods around. From the classic 2009 model to the most up to date Nano. Sony was smart to do this - that means a lot of people, not just techies with the most up-to-date devices, can use this. As an example, a friend of mine still has a working iPod mini (don't laugh, he's a Luddite!) and we tested the headset on that too. Surprisingly, it worked! - though the volume controls did not work with such an old, outdated model.

Another convenience is the location of the controls, which are located on a box located on the cord, which prevents you from having to reach all the way down to your iPod or iPhone to adjust the volume. My second favorite feature is the included clip, which allows me to wind up any slack on the cord and prevent it from getting tangled easily. In the past, I've killed so many earbuds because I pulled too hard on the cord by accident, so this is a welcome feature.

This deluxe model includes a pouch that offers an array of different sized earbuds - one set is noise-cancelling, while the other isn't. This is overkill, though. I tried out different sets of buds but none of them fit just right. And the "thwoping" sound I mentioned earlier still remained.

So I have mixed feelings about this product. The "thwomping" (sucking) sound is its biggest drawback for me, as the buds work best when you don't move around a lot.

I'm terrible at learning languages. I studied French in junior high, high school and a few years in college, but I still had trouble speaking French fluently. I went to Paris a few times and even dated a French native who criticized every word I attempted, so I gave up. Despite this history of failure, I was curious to see if this Instant Immersion French kit would work for me. The box claims that it is just as good, if not better than Rosetta Stone because they refuse to spend as much on advertising. Hmm. I have a hard time believing that advertising is a main reason why Rosetta Stone is popular. The set comes with 4 CDs and the instructions recommend starting with the Ipod audio CD, though the same sheet of instructions say that it should be used as a supplement to the software. As I sampled each disc, I found that the set is really designed less for a serious French student than for a traveler or someone visiting France on business. There is no attempt to teach grammar or language structure, like present or past tense. The lessons all stress memorization and the ability to recognize and parrot standard phrases, remember a good amount of vocabulary (though not the context to use it). I was disappointed to find that it is structured more like a Berlitz language course. Using flashcards and games to learn language is nothing new, and the Oscar Lake game included is absolutely ancient, as I remember this game from 1998. The only "new" thing about this immersion program is the fact it offers an Ipod and interactive DVD option. The interactive DVD was fun to use though the video is low-tech. Also, the quizzes didn't work that well - I had to click my DVD remote arrow buttons several times before it registered my choice. Did all this it work for me? Did my ability to pronounce words improve? So-so. While I enjoyed playing the games and had fun refreshing my memory using the interactive DVD, the kit offers no real revolutionary way to learn language. It all depends on the student and how motivated you are. In that case, I'd probably do well with Berlitz if I'd only tried harder.

So, I do NOT like using my phone to control this. The basic controls are fine with the TV remote. There SHOULD be a remote too! Sound is good so far, though has to be done with the buttons on the unit as they seem to not be in the app. Should note, I do not know where mine was purchased as it was a gift that
was hand delivered to me as "house warming" present.

I don't like the fact that I have to keep using the iPhone to change the volume, change the station change anything. I know the instructions say I can press the sides for this but it just isn't that easy. I see lots of people around me using these all the time and I thought perhaps I was missing out on something, but truthfully, these are annoying and I'm always worried that I'll lose one, so I don't like wearing them outside my home. Good idea, just not for me. I will say the sound quality seems very good, but I haven't tried other brands so I can't really say for sure. Battery life seems short to me

I'm sure this is a quality product, as are the many other FiiO products I have owned and do currently own, but.........I bought it for a specific purpose. I wanted a BT transmitter that I could pair to TWE's and transmit the audio from my ROKU box. I hooked it to the ROKU using the optical cable and all I got was static. It paired effortlessly but no matter what I tried it only transmitted static. I ended up returning it and spent $18 for the MPOW TT-8047 Wireless 2-in1 adapter which I plug into the headphone jack of my receiver. Works flawlessly. YMMV

Ear tips are a totally subjective thing. What I might think are great you might think suck so take this with a grain of salt. I found these to be comfortable and secure and I have been using SpinFits for a year or so now but this particular model altered the sound profile of my BGVP DMG’S too much for my liking. I think it has more to do with the double flange design sealing of my ear canal than anything else and it would be an easy enough thing to remedy with the EQ function of my HiBy r6 or my EarStudio ES100 and I’ll do that in the future, but for now I’m going back to my standbys. The other thing I found annoying with these is if I move my head and put the slightest pressure on an ear pressing against my pillow the sound cuts out on that ear. Again I think it has more to do with the flange but it’s annoying none the less. My other non-flanged SpinFits don’t do that. Great products but this design just doesn’t do it.....For Me.

very frustrating that I cannot use the speaker when it is plugged in for charging- if it goes dead during a gathering you are without music. Will not charge when in the "on" position, either, so a couple of times I forgot to turn off, and overnight still wan not charge. sound is ok
Quirky and not reliable.  Can never quite figure out why.  Sound not that impressive.

For the relatively little money paid - this is an OK receiver. My previous Sony of the similar basic level has been playing nicely the last 7 years, until it died, so I thought I'll follow-up with the brand. Well, there has been one disappointment, but big enough (for me, personally) to return it and try something different. Issue may be subjective, nevertheless... the issue is a quite flat sound, in particular the bass. The non-audiophile (i.e. reasonably priced) receivers used to have a "contour", or "bass boost" function (even the previous Sony model had it), which greatly enhanced the audibility of lower frequencies when played at low decibels. This one lacks it (and it sounds like most of nowadays sold receivers are like this), hence the sound coming out is quite flat (also for treble band), unless you go really loud. In addition, the receiver lacks a sub-woofer output, so there is no chance to improve low frequencies.
Out of the other available receivers, I decided to pick (by recommendation) a little more up-scale (yet still reasonably priced) Harman Kardon HK 3390 (2 x 80W) Stereo Receiver, which has sub-woofer outputs - even though it also lacks bass boost, I am expecting it will revive the bass, even with my old Sony 10" sub.

The speakers do work but the sound quality is not the best. I bought them for my son to do his homeschooling with. When he is listening to a story being read out loud sometimes the speakers crackle with the voices. You have to have the volume down quite low to avoid this so they have to be used in a quite environment. For the price they are functional but if you are wanting this for anything other than light use I would not buy them.

My biggest complaint is the remote control. On my tv which include all the firestick has I can turn tv off on and control volume. WHY would you not have this on a remote? On what planet does not a remote control have a power and volume button. basically the purchase is just turn you tv in a smart tv. We use it only because all the stations are on one remote but have to have another to mute etc
Very fussy, particularly when working near the ceiling for surround sound speakers.  Hard to adjust and hold 8lb. speakers in place.

At $249, this unit is a good buy. The main unit sounds very good especially at higher volumes. It is very easy to hook up. Use a high quality HDMI cable to connect the unit to the eARC HDMI connection on the TV. TV remote (also LG) controls this system so it's a one remote setup. Nice!  Bluetooth connectivity is easy and painless. The only shortcoming I can hear is the lack of bass from the subwoofer. The bass volume is adjustable but even at its highest level there is room for more. Bass while streaming music is adequate but for TV viewing it does fall short. I am buying another sound bar for my other home but it won't be this one. I'll update this review against whatever unit I buy next. Stay tuned.

The first thing I noticed when putting the headphones on my 6 year old son was that they were too big for him, even on the smallest size.
I put them on myself and the smallest size was slightly big for me but almost the right size. The biggest size is way to big and I’m not sure anyone could fit that size.
I’ve attached photos with my son and myself using the smallest and largest size.
The sound of the headphones is good and they are pretty comfortable.
I think that the highest volume could be too loud for a child so I will make sure that I watch how high the volume is. When the headphones are on the highest volume I can hear what the person is listening too when next to them. This makes it helpful with making sure to have them turn it down. But I would prefer that the volume wouldn’t go that loud as an option.
I’m giving these headphones a lower rating because I bought them for my children and they don’t fit them as well as I hoped.

I'm glad they send two.  In applying the first one, when I peeled off the backing I watched dust come through the air and stick to the backside of this film before I could even put it on the camera.  Apparently, peeling off the backing generates a powerful static charge.  The film was ruined.  On my second attempt, I peeled the backing off slowly as I applied to the camera.  Much better results that way.

This device connects via USB to your computer. Unfortunately, music played from the computer is interrupted with occasional snaps and pops. Creative Labs' knowledge base reveals this to be a common problem, depending on your computer, operating system and other intstalled devices. If you are an unlucky one whose computer set up is not compatible, forget it.
I did find a work-around, which is to unplug the USB connection and run line-out audio into the transmitter's line-in jack . This delivers clean sound, but with no remote control of music selection.
Disappointing not to have it fully functioning, but enjoying good sound through the work-around.

Update 2/28/09 - I returned the product to Creative Labs and received a replacement. No luck - skips in the music stream persist when using the USB connection. It appears that computer resource conflicts impair other USB speaker units also. (e.g. Logitech Z Cinema 2.1)

I bought these speakers to complement my home theater system - my old EPI's had expired. As front speakers for home theater, where you can supplement base with a sub-woofer and voice with a center channel, these are very adequate. However, for pure music listening I would recommend going a step or two up. A primary attribute of great speakers is "presence", where the listener is aware that there is music in the room, but not aware of the speakers. With these, I am always aware of the speakers - which I believe is caused by overly bright highs that give a slightly unnatural cast to the sound. My old speakers had presence, but alas; I cannot afford the thousand bucks or so it would take to replace them with speakers of equal quality.

These were the first wireless headphones I ever purchased. Although I bought them via Amazon, they're not coming up in my old orders - no surprise, I suppose, considering it was sometime in 2009 or 2010. The reason I'm reviewing them now is because I recently needed to use them when a cheap pair of Kotion wireless headsets died on me and my old ASUS was waiting in a drawer to try them out again. When I first got them, they were nothing but trouble. Wouldn't connect reliably, wouldn't hold a charge.

Strangely, almost 10 years later, after I charged them briefly and plugged the dongle in... they work great! Sound good, holding a charge, connecting easily to my PC for use. I'm guessing that wireless drivers have come a long way in the intervenining years, as there's no problem in using them with my PC now. The only problem is that the foam they used in the earpads completely disintegrated, but those are easily enough replaced with spare foam pads available here on Amazon (I've ordered the "Zotech 4 Pairs 2.5'' (60mm) Foam Pad Ear Cover for Philips Sony Headphones" which I believe will fit fine).

All in all, they've become my backup wireless headphones. Not bad for a 9 year old wireless device that's been sitting my in drawer doing nothing!

That's a line from a Gin Blossoms song, that fit's these speakers. I wasn't looking for something to sound great, just something that didn't sound terrible, was small, and I didn't need another A/C power cord to run. This fits the bill and they will work when I just need a temporary or non-musical speaker.

Otherwise, the sound is tinny and mediocre. They will work for what I need them for, just don't expect great sound.

PS-Read all the other reviews about the annoying lights and didn't think it was a big deal. My new PC powers the USB ports even when the computer is off, so these lights are on 24/7 unless I unplug them from the computer. Annoying and useless.

Good sound for the size and the cost. A cut above your average computer desktop speaker. My biggest complaint is that the cords that connect the speakers are a bit too short and hard to work with if you have anything other than a simple install of the speakers on either side of your monitor. It would be better to have these cords detachable.

The manual may not be very clear but to be able to start you need to setup a  direct wifi connection to the device's wifi RX-BF... via phone, tablet or computer.
Once connnected to via wifi-direct, you go to 192.168.203.1 to get to the settings page to setup your home wifi connection.

Once completed, you can start casting via phone, tablet, or pc.

Performance: I used casting devices in the past and this device appears to be using a technology similar to miracast in the past although it does not state what casting standard is being used.  When the settings is at the advertised max of 4k 30fps, and when casting videos, I received frame drops but more disappointingly the sound cuts off every split second.  Changing the setting to 1920x1080 60 fps, the sound drop issue is fixed.  But there is still noticeable frame drops.  It appears to like 15 to 25 fps range.
The best connection quality would be to use the usb transmitter but quality is still marginally better than the other options.

In summary, 4k casting is best used for viewing documents and photos, while using the transmitter at 1920x1080 is manageable for streaming videos.

The sound/mic quality is extremely clear and clean, so no complaints there.
Two issues - The set is somewhat bulky and does not fold, thus taking up a lot of space in my laptop bag. The other issue is that it sits a bit tight on the ears, making it uncomfortable after a couple of hours. It's a little easier on the ears if I move the cups slightly forward, but then that lets external sounds in. That said, it could be the shape of my head, and you might not have this issue.

I needed a quality headset at work, and at the gym. I have been using the $ 10 Sony 'over the ear' clips - these are cheap, better than apple's default buds, but the sound quality leaves a bit to be desired. I also needed something with a microphone for the occasional call.

First, the good - these Klipsh do appear to have great build quality, are very comfortable, and provide great sound isolation. (I had comfort issues in the past with a $200 Shure 'in-ear' set that I enjoyed listening to, until they unfortunately found their way into the washing machine).

However, the sound is just marginally better than the $10 Sony. Also, they are a pain to use in the gym, especially if you are on a treadmill. While they do a great job of cutting out he ambient noise, there is the constant 'thump thump' of your movement being transmitted back to your ear.

Update: My wife purchased the Bose Mie2i a few days ago. Although a bit more expensive than the Klipsh, these sound much much better (especially vocals), although they do not have the sound isolation of the Klipsh.

Bottom line: These Klipsh sets are good, but not worth the price premium. (If I were to do this again, I would go with the Bose)

Waiting for someone to now combine the best of these 2 headsets!

Hard to rate this headset. For the $30 ....yes, they are 4 or 5 stars. My problem is that one of the ear pads fell off my $300 Bose headset. I was mad, so I purchased these. When I put them on, all I could say was OMG. The sound quality was so terrible. My advice do not compare them. You will be very disappointed. But remember for the price they are five stars.

I do a LOT of work in front of a computer, and was getting these for when I work at home. At work, I use a Logitech 930 headset that I really like. I got these so I wouldn't yank my laptop off the desk when I get up. I got bluetooth, thinking they'd be easy to sync to my various devices. So, here's my breakdown:

Range
I can go upstairs and grab a few things or go two rooms away and I still get a signal. The range is pretty good on these.

Playback Sound
The playback sound quality is okay. Not blowing me away, but alright. I listen to music, no vocals, to block out the office noise and keep my head focused. The playback audio goes into tin-can mode when the mic is enabled. That's something I didn't realize as a limitation of how bluetooth handles the two signals. That took me a while to figure out.

Microphone
The mic is okay. It just flips me out that the playback goes into "phone mode" when the mic is enabled.

Battery
Well, I've only had these a couple of months. But, the battery seems to go at least as long as I can stand to keep them on my head. Max has been about 2 hours at a stretch before giving my head/ears a break.

Fit
I'm an adult and my head is average-sized, not large. After maybe three months these cans are still a bit tight. The cups don't quite fit entirely over my ears and get uncomfortable after maybe two hours --like, *ouch* uncomfortable.

Heat
These cans get pretty hot after maybe 45 minutes. Hot like I just got out of the shower and I need a towel in my ears hot. I don't think I've ever had sweaty ears like this before from a set of headphones.

Sync
I've easily sync'd these to Ubuntu 14.04 & 10, Windows 7, and OS X Mavericks.

Would I recommend these to a friend?
No. I like not having to carry a dongle around since bluetooth is in all of my computers (one has an $8 dongle that works just fine.) But, they get so hot, and are still not comfortable on my head and ears after maybe 100 hours of use. So, for the $50 price tag, I'd probably have to say no. If they were $25 and just to make the occasional phone call I might recommend them to a friend, but not to wear for any period of time. If they were just a bit more comfortable, and breathed a bit better, I'd change my mind. Maybe in the next revision, Photive?

I must admit I was taken in by the reviews. However, the reality doesn't match the hype. Sound quality is slightly better than the $25 buds they replaced and they fall out just as frequently when I run. I've only had them a week so will persevere for another week but something this simple shouldn't be this difficult to get used to.

The most popular review on here, Kyle’s from Oct 2018, has a lot of good points such as praising the system where it works right and suggestions for how it could be improved such as the need for a duress code.

The only major thing that review missed is the range extenders.
They are almost worthless.

If you read the reviews of the range extender when sold as a separate item you will read about some of the issues.

Issue 1: They are weak. People’s reviews and reviews from electronics publications find these extenders to be underpowered. There are many more powerful z wave range extenders in the market.

When I called tech support about this they blatantly told me they knew about the poorly performing range extenders.

They told me that some of the Ring compatible smart outlets made by other manufacturers, like GE, include range extended and that they work much better than the Ring range extenders.

At least the tech support person was honest in admitting that their extenders sucked and that compatible third party manufacturer extenders will work better...I guess?

There is a page on the Ring website that list all the Z wave devices made by third parties that are compatible with the Ring system.

Unfortunately you can’t buy the best reviewed and most powerful Z wave range extenders on the market because Ring does not make them compatible with their system because they want you to buy their crappy extenders of course.

I guess we should just be grateful that at least some of the compatible smart plugs have signal extenders built into them that are better than Ring’s.

Issue 2: They are dumb. The algorithms for determining what path a device takes, in terms of whether it connects to a certain range extender or the base station, is horrible. This flaw includes the range extenders themselves when they try and decide whether or not to connect to the base station or another range extender. (I have two Ring range extenders).

If you have one range extender 20-30 feet from the base station and then place another range extender 20-30 feet from the first range extender branching out in the same direction there is no guarantee that the second range extender will connect to the first range extender rather than trying to connect to the base station.

Maybe this is because the signal from the range extenders is so bad that the devices are programmed to connect to the base station if at all possible, even if the signal is weak.

One support tech even told me a “funny” story about how a friend of theirs has a range extender just fifteen feet away from the base station in their house and but the range extended chooses to connect to another range extender that is more than 40 feet away rather than directly to the base station that is just 15 feet from it.

Ha ha ha, it’s SO funny when your expensive electronic product that you bought to keep your home safe does not work correctly! Hilarious!

A secondary criticism is that if the signal to the keypad isn’t strong enough the keypad alarm might not sound.

I have two doors between my keypad and the range extender it connects to.
When the doors are open the keypad usually sounds the alarm, when they are closed it never does.

It would seem obvious to any rational person that the issue with the alarm not sounding is the signal strength but the tech support people swear up and down that that is not possible.

Even when the doors are closed the tech support people claim the keypad reads as having an adequate signals strength ( the tech support people can see the signal strength of your devices but you can’t).

They are actually sending me a new keypad but I am not hopeful it will solve the problem.
It seems obvious to me that the command for signaling the alarm requires a better signal than the other functions of the keypad.

Maybe the signal for the alarm is only sent out once while the signal for the other functions are repeatedly sent out until the base station acknowledges them? Who knows?

The point is that it seems like a design flaw and if you plan on having your keypad more than a room lengths away from your base station you shouldn't count on the alarm on the keypad working.

I will update this review with the performance of my replacement keypad.

The last thing I will say is that the price of 11 dollars a month for monitoring the entire system regardless of how many devices you have, including any cameras, is a great price.

I hope that this type of price is here to stay. If they pull a bait and switch where they significantly increase the price of monitoring after they initially get enough people to buy the system I will drop this system like a hot potato and sell it used on eBay.

I'm on my second pair of these. The sound and noise cancellation is fantastic, although you can hear a white noise hiss when all is quiet.
There are two problems with this headset. The first is that the on/off switch is cheap. It broke on my first pair, and now the second pair is ready to break as well. The second problem is how hot your ears get wearing them. My ears are practically sweating and I have to hold them open to get fresh air under the cups. I'm sure it's because they need a seal to do the noise cancellation so well. But it means they are not comfortable for wearing over an hour.

I listen mostly to jazz in the background while I’m reading or on the web, usually at low volume - sometimes rock at louder volumes. I’ve bought any number of blue tooth speakers, as a hobby I suppose, always in search of the ‘best’ sound.

I recently tried the UE Megablast and while okay, they don’t hold a candle to to crispness and range of the UE (smaller size) Boom 3’s. The M-Blasts can be better loud and have some nice control features but they give up crispness for volume found in the Boom 3s.

You can save yourself some money and get unbelievably good sound from the 3’s. IMHO, these are the best by far, and uncannily the least expensive of over 10 other good home brands, costing as much as $400. Unless you’re filling a large room with loud music I’d say the Boom 3 is the best speaker in this portable class. They are superlative in sound from low to high range at easy and medium volume.

Enjoy, and don’t worry about missing any sound - you’ll pleasantly hear it all crisply, just not quite the volume, albeit plenty loud for any home room, especially if you pair two, which is still a value!

This is an update after buying Apple’s AirPods April, 2020. I bought Creative’s mid range units at $80. I’ve kept these as they were a big improvement over cheaper ones. They are hard to connect to my iPads and I didn’t think I was hearing all the jazz I was listening to.

Maybe I’m a little fogged but I had a heck of a time understanding the pairing procedure re above instructions. I finally got them paired but only the ‘main’ unit shows as connected ( L & R) on my iPad even though both are connected??? Persistence paid off.

I couldn’t figure if the sound is adjustable, e.g. using both buds or just the main?

Otherwise, they sound okay and work fine for the money. They’re twicethe sound and quality than Tozo 10 @ $50, which I bought earlier. I wasn’t quite sold on these at $80 and wondered about the sound output by spending $125 - $200, more, i.e. to pick up anything I might be missing? Well, the AirPods are ~$250 but went on sale for $235, so I bought.

There’s a big difference in price, admittedly but there’s also a great increase in quantity and quality of sound (re my review of AirPods),
Plus, the AirPods connect easily with Apple devices. The others do not. Bottom line, for limited use but good sound quality I would recommend something in between on price, maybe Apple’s earlier $150 ear buds. Unless you want to splurge, then it’s a tossup if the high end is worth the price for casual listening. To get by, the Creative units would work, albeit missing the luxury of full sound delivery.

Lots have commented on the sound on this guy being loud, there's a point where at 4000 rpms is going to be nosier no matter what you do, there's physics involved in why it's so loud. I can't say that's the fault of the company. I ordered 2, and the first one came with a kind of grinding noise, like the fan was rubbing on the inside. The 2nd one I ordered was perfect, nice and quite (as quite as 4000 rpms can be, which should be kind of a low hum) So I contacted the company and they responded quickly in sending out a replacement for my first fan.

Low and behold that one also had a grinding whine to it. I'm not going to bother returning it, I'm sure it's just quality control. a 4000 rpm 80mm shouldn't be this cheap, so I don't expect it to be perfect. In any case it does work great, most fans get up to about 4200 and 4100 in my server. Does a great job of keeping all the HDD cool. I really love it with asrock rack server mobos that can have granular control of their PWD fans. Once you spin these guys down to 2600 or under It's as quite as my HTPC. And they only get loud if things get really hot. So they do the job well enough for me.
Comfortable, but sound is not as good as my older model.

I am having a love hate relationship w/these ear buds.

What I like about these ear buds was first the price...these are much more affordable than some other name brand blue tooth earbuds, but the performance also explains the price differences.

The sound: These do sound really good.

Noise Cancelling: Very good for earbuds, maybe even a little too good. I run w/these and still want to be able to hear road noise.

Fit: These fit me very well and stay put while running. To me this is probably the best part. I have not had good luck w/earbuds staying put while running or lifting hard. These do that. I find myself checking them often, out of habit, and they are tightly in place.

Battery Life: I've not had an occasion where the batteries have run dead. I use them, put them back in their case and they are ready for my next workout.
Telephone calls: Works well while making and taking phone calls.

The not so good:

The functions: Too many. On/Off, pair, pause, really are the only things I need.

Pairing: I can only get these to pair to one item. If I pair to my phone, I cannot pair to my watch. The first time out of the case they automatically paired to my phone. When I tried to also pair them to my watch, following the very complicated pairing sequence of button pushing, I could not get it to pair. I had to completely unpair these from my phone to get them to pair to my watch. Then I could not get the earbuds to pair back to my phone.

I also get a lot of static and drop off while in these. It's not on common for one of the ears to lose sound while out running or walking. I also get a static sound pretty frequently which requires me to pause and restart playing music.

In the end, I do not think I would buy these again unless they come out w/a better version. If they could make earbuds with this fit and work like some others, they would be perfect. Until then I'll use these until they die and probably not replace them w/more SkullCandy earbuds unless some improvements are made.

I've had several different pairs of earbuds, all purchased from Amazon and none were name brands. So far, with the wrapping ear piece, this pair seems to stay on my ears much better than the buds that just pop into the ears. They paired easily to my iPhone and connect automatically each time I take them out of the case. The sound is decent or at least decent enough for me. I do not use these for just listening to music or videos, I have better over the ear headphones for that purpose. For me, I just use these for running, working out or maybe while working around the yard. For that purpose, the sound quality is pretty good. The only suggestion I have is remember to take the clear tape off the charging contacts; I did not realize it was there and my earbuds were not charging each time I put them back in the case. On the upside, I did learn that the battery life is excellent on these earbuds. I cannot say how long they actually lasted before I charged them, but I probably went on 5 or 6 runs before the first ear bud died. With the tape off the contacts, they do charge automatically each time they are placed back in their case. A nice feature is that the case can be charged either with a cord or by setting the case on a charging pad. The price was reasonable. I would recommend these wireless earbuds to anyone looking for a set. Since I cannot fully say how long they will last or how durable they are, I will reserve the 5th star until I have owned these for a while.

Updated 12May21: Ok, I really want to like earbuds, but I cannot. As many times as I have tried earbuds, they just always feel like they are coming out of my ears, even w/the ear wraps on these buds. Having to continuously re-seat the ear buds in my ears while running just doesn't make for a comfortable run. So, I went back to a pair of wired BT headphones; which sit in my ears much better.

Camera easy to use (plug and play worked instantly). However the camera and picture quality looked grainy even in a bright room. And haven't been able to get the microphone to work. It just doesn't pick up and sound.

Sound quality is awesome.  I ended up returning them though because they are a pain to put on.  I gave it a few days of use just to see if it'll get easier but they are just not easy to put on.  One of the sides also kept coming out.

This a great item, it works well and is easy to use.  I gave the sound quality 2 stars and an overall of 3 because the aux out jack is very noisy(alternator whine) I have tried many different cables and it doesnt go away, the whine can also be heard when using the FM mode in the lower frequencies.  It's not bad for the price and it wouldn't be fair to give it 2 stars.

At first these rocked! Then suddenly the buttons on the cups would not work. They turned into dumb bluetooth headphones. After about an hour of wear the top of my head would start hurting. The noise canceling is ok - works best when music is fairly loud. Sound quality is great. Doesn't do highs too well, bass was excellent. All in all, I ended up returning these. I am looking for something just a bit more... perfected.

They sound great, fit great, I love that they're push button instead of the overly sensitive tap buttons... But they turn off and disconnect SO FAST after pausing your audio. It's so bad it's a deal breaker. You have to turn them back on after any pause and it's incredibly annoying.

EDIT: Leaving my original review below, but it seems it was a faulty base that gave us an extremely short working range. We were able to exchange our package and it's working now. The cameras do work for us with pretty good picture and sound. The motion detection has good timing. The night vision is good, too. However the company is still a nightmare to get a hold of so I'm knocking a couple stars. A product like this needs easy access to help, and they do not offer that.

Original review (if you're having this issue, exchange your product before you decide to return it!):
These cameras do not work unless they are within 2 feet of the base station. We have tried numerous things to fix it, and nothing has worked. Arlo's help video recommend the Netgear Nighthawk router as the best provider of range, and that's what we have. Our wifi is not the issue.

Their customer support is a joke. The live chat option just does not work. Their call center has extremely long wait times. I can't even post on the community support board because I'm not verified- and the verification email they are supposed to send will not come through no matter how many times I request to be verified.

I really regret not listening to the bad reviews.
Sound as not as good

My daughter loves these. (Pink) She used them at school for 2nd grade. Comfortable and has room to grow. Sadly, near the end of the year, the sound began cutting in and out. We checked and discovered that the microphone was doing the same. I have a message in to the seller about it because the listing seems to mention an 18 month warranty. I was hoping she’d be able to use these through elementary school.

Update: seller responded promptly to send a new pair.

This headset does cancel noise, and the sound is clear. That part is fine. For the not-so-fine parts: they're really tight, and they cancel noise almost too well.

The tightness:
Right away, I felt that they squeezed my ears too much. I left them to stretch across several hard-bound books for a few days which loosened them up for a while, but they eventually go back to their original tightness that I can't wear them for more than 15 minutes at a time. My ears get squashed and they hurt to leave on, and I don't even have a big melon head!

The noise-cancelling:
While they do block out outside noise, they cancel my own voice out too, and I feel like I'm talking into a blanket by myself - I can barely hear myself talk. It's very disconcerting.

All in all, if they weren't so darn tight, I think I'd like them better. I had to dock 1.5 stars because of the physical discomfort, and .5 star for the talking-into-an-echoless-void factor. The sound quality is good, though. So, if you have a smallish head, and you like having all the outside sound shut out, they may work for you.

My right earbud just stopped working. I purchased these less than a month ago and all-of-a-sudden the right ear stopped working. Aside from that the sound quality is excellent. Softest setting is still quite loud.

(Update) replacement pair got the same problem. Right ear is going out and I'm 2 days passed the return window.

These walkie talkies (supposedly FRS) are cheaply made, they’re cheap plastic. They absolutely excel at creating static over your voice and that of anyone else. What a great feature. Instructions are crummy, and incomplete. Too much trouble to return, so I’m throwing them in the garbage.

Amazon offered a very persuasive deal to turn in my previous Kindle Paperwhite for this one.  I wanted to listen to Audiobooks and my old version did not have that capacity.  I don't think I would do this again.  I lost some of the features like the controls on either side to click through pages.  The lighting of the screen is not as good as the screen on my older version.  I feel that I gave up more in the way of READING, than I gained for Audio.  If I had it to do over, I'd simply buy a different device to  listen to audiobooks and kept the older version of my Kindle.

Battery life was great, however, the volume level for making it louder didn't seem to be working right. I had the volume turned up all pretty high on my iphone and still had a hard time hearing the music over background noise around me. Lack of bass made me only give it a 2 star for sound quality, but you get what you pay for.

I bought these to use with my PlayStation controller when I'm traveling so I don't disturb anyone with my video game noise.

Unfortunately, the sound quality from these things is pretty bad, and they hurt my ears if I have them in for more than 10 minutes. I used them a couple times and have retired them. Debating on throwing them into the electronics recycling pile at work.

I used to buy JVC Gumy ear buds pretty frequently back when iPods were popular and smartphones still had headphone jacks. I remember them being very comfortable and decent sound quality for the $10 price tag. In fact, I used to sleep with them in my ears since I have tinnitus and listen to white noise on my phone every night. Either I bought a different model this time, or the quality has gone down.

I suffer from tinnitus and listen to white noise or meditation videos on YouTube while trying to sleep--otherwise the ringing is just too distracting. I have been using earbuds for the past two years, but for various reasons no longer wish to use them. So I ordered SleepPhones, hoping they would eliminate the need for uncomfortable ear buds.

I have tried these for two nights in a row. Both nights I woke up with the cord around my neck; the band had shimmied to the top of my head (read: speakers not where they need to be); and I was sweating from the fleece (maybe I need to wait to review until the temperature has dipped below 80 degrees where I live). Plus, the speakers only offer any significant volume when my phone volume is turned on high--even then, I wish I could get it a bit higher.

I was really hoping these would be a good alternative to earbuds, but I think I will continue to be disappointed and am out $35...
Love the clear volume!
Not real good sound

The first one I got was great - for an hour. Then the picture froze. I powered off and back on and I could get picture but no sound. I tried changing from HDMI to RCA cables, same thing, Swapped to a different DVD - same thing. I sent that one back and ordered another one - same model. The 2nd one would not power on. DOA
3rd on is great. Seller was very kind and helpful. I really like this model because the remote had buttons spaced farther apart so an adult doesn't need to use a stylus to avoid pressing 2 buttons.

Comfortable and great sound quality.

The one thing that had been a selling point was dual BT device connection. With two devices connect you get constant break / hiccups in playback. Very annoying.

First things first. The camera from this provider does NOT come with all the mounts seen in XS100i un-boxing videos. It only includes a bar mount, which can hardly be considered a "full mounting kit". I purchased this with the intent of mounting it on my motorcycle and bicycle helmets. In researching replacement mounts, the offerings from Polaroid are next to nothing. I found that the Ion air pro and Monoprice cameras use the same ball and socket style mount. The problem, (for me) is the issued ball and socket mount raises the camera over 2" over the mounting plate, which is not something I want on a helmet. I have since ordered a 1/4-20 to gopro adapter, and believe that I can mount it closer to my helmets using gopro mounts and quick releases.

I really like the torpedo style shape of this camera. The vibrate feature is awesome, as the recording LED can be hard to see in bright light, or can't be seen at all depending on the cameras location. The switch on top is large and is easy to manipulate with gloves.

The two (yes, two) apps used to control this camera from a smart phone are very, very clunky. The "File" app crashes frequently on my Samsung S5. There is a noticeable lag when using the phone as a view finder, but it is still serviceable for lining up shots.

Video wise, I've only used it in 720P @ 60fps. When given plenty of light it produces gorgeous videos. The results in low light aren't as promising, but still viable. Using the included handlebar mount introduces a lot of camera shake when used on my v-twin motorcycle.

Audio is good, but a tad muffled from the waterproof case.

All in all I'm happy with the camera despite it's short comings. I'm using it primarily as a "dash cam" and for that it gets 4 stars. Only knocked it down to 3 because of the false advertising concerning the mounts.

I purchased a green silicone sleeve along with it. Hair tends to stick to it, but I'm otherwise happy with it. It gives the camera an extra layer of protection, and makes it much easier to locate in low light. The fit is tight and lines up with the lines of the camera. 4 stars for that.

As I have read in reviews since the purchase, I so wish Fire was more user friendly with my apple/IOS stuff like Dash lane...use it so often and cannot use it on this new reader.
It does a bunch and is a great reader/audio book device but I miss the flexibility of the Ipad
Sound quality is only ok but for the price not bad
Gets the job done but definite downgrade in sound quality. Big time difference in tone and volume and disservice to higher end listening

Meh. I got my first AirPods recently. I was thrilled with them. So much better than corded headphones.

I upgraded to these because they are supposed to be “better”. Not really. They are less comfortable. They fall out all the time. They are slimey and gross feelings when sweaty.

The noise cancellation is real. It’s amazing how much it cuts out though I rarely want to be cut off like this. I can’t hear the doorbell (I literally missed being informed about a gas leak in my neighborhood because of this) and it’s dangerous on a bike. If you leave it open for ambient noise there’s a lot of crackling sounds from wind or it shifting in your ear.

Also the mic seems poorer - or at least my family complains more they can’t understand me more often with these than the previous hard AirPods ( the ones without the silicone ear piece.)

When I saw this I jumped on ordering it. One thing I hate about compressed air is whatever that additive the put in there to keep people from huffing it. That stuff gets all over the air and in my nose and throat and is very unpleasant.

Will this replace a can of compressed air? Not exactly. But for many uses it'll do. Plus it has the ability to be used as a vaccum, which I do like. And I'll for sure try this before reaching for the air can simply due to the above reason.

The LED light on there is useful and unexpected. I didn't realize it had the light. Although it only faces the side of the air duster. You don't have light when vacuuming. Seems like they could have reversed the motor direction for vacuum and then the light would work for vacuuming as well as blowing air.

There are 3 speeds. The fastest speed doesn't push anywhere near as much air as a can of air. But to be fair a can of air has a tiny tube shooting the air out and even the smallest attachment on this is maybe 5-10x as large as that tiny straw. So it can't possibly push air as fast. Maybe I'll try 3d printing an attachment that can take one of those tiny air can straws. They also could have employed some type of venturi effect to get more air out.

Is it enough air flow to be useful? Maybe? In some cases it will be. And when it isn't I'll grab a real can of air.

The vaccum is nice. I can probably see myself using that more often than the duster. I did a quick pass over my audio mixer and my keyboard with the vacuum. It pulled out most of the dust. So that is a plus.

But there's just something satisfying about using a can of compressed air that this doesn't match. And it's partially due to the noise. This thing is pretty loud. You have a motor in there spinning up to 10k RPM. It's louder than a dremel.

The good stuff: I bought these for listening while sleeping. When they're working they sound great. I haven't had them long enough to know about the battery life. But for my use I'm sure it'll be fine. They fit in my ear well enough and are smaller than the echo buds. There's no discomfort when side sleeping on them.

Update - after some time I found that there is some occasional discomfort when sleeping w them in.

Can't beat the price. If the issues are all resolved they'll end up being an amazing value.

The ok stuff: The noise cancelling appears to be passive not active. Meaning that outside noise is dampened because you have something in your ear. Not because it's cancelling the outside noise. This is actually preferred to me because I HATE talking on the phone with active noise cancelling when you can't hear your own voice. I bought these for nite time use so neither is really an issue for me.

The bad stuff: One ear, usually the left ear, will cut in and out. So the sound cuts off and back on over and over. Then it won't for a while. Then it will again. Seems like a connectivity issue or something. Listening to music right now the left keeps cutting out. It's unusabale like this. I wrote a note to their warranty group and if they do something about it I'll update this review.

Update - NEVER heard back on the warranty thing. I contacted them using the warranty link provided and nothing. So if you have a prob I would return them to Amazon.

Second is that sometimes when I take the out the earbudlittle rubber ear thing stays in my ear. Seems like a problem. We'll see. Also it's a little difficult to get them out of the charging case as there's nothing to grab on to.

Side note.. I previously tried the Echo Earbuds ($90) and they also did the thing with the left side cutting in and out. They were also larger and uncomfortable for side sleeping. So I returned those. My apple airpods earbuds and max headphones don't cut in and out. So it's not an issue with my phone's bluetooth.

For the price, the build quality is great. No noticeable issues with sound quality that I can hear. My main issue is that these are not easy to tell red vs white. There is tiny print on each housing that is colored red or white. It blends in pretty well with the gold/bronze like housing and I feel that the paint will easily rub off. Overall a great value, just wish they used normal white/red caps on the housings to differentiate.

QC did a poor job; these were the replacement set.  The 1st set the led lights worked, but no sound.  These the led lights DON'T work, but I have sound...so i'm done with returns and keeping them.  They get the job done, just with no cool lighting darn it.

Spot objects up to fifty miles away?? I don’t think so. That is a claim by the company in their ad.
I found this to be awkward. I wear glasses and do not care for binoculars for this reason. I was really hoping this would help me get a closer look at the birds in my yard (it will) and maybe take hiking or to a Packer game.

Nope. It’s simply too big for me. To use occasionally at home it will be okay to get a better look at a bird but it’s not discreet enough to toss in a purse or small bag when trying to get into a football game post 911. Not if you want anything else in your bag. And I do. Or if you want a small bag for hiking.

Yes, it gives decent clarity to whatever you’re trying to see, but I found myself feeling nauseous afterwards as I sometimes get with binoculars. Even taking my glasses off. My husband felt the same and he doesn’t wear glasses, is an experienced hiker/backpacker and hoped this might come in handy. He felt the same as I did. Too big. No lense cap & it’s just a bit awkward even with the use being fairly simple. Not a big fan for the price point.

Let me start out by saying that I bought these mainly for streaming on my iPad. I purchased these as a replacement for a pair that I really liked that broke off in my iPad.
These came very quickly. Like ordering them at night and getting them the next morning quickly. So I immediately plugged them in.

Pros: Sound good when you are streaming video YouTube/Prime, etc. I watched several hours of Ray Donovan & a variety of YouTube videos and these were good for that. I don’t know that they block out much ambient noise or have much noise cancellation.
* Plug in/remove very easily to both my iPad Gen 5 and iPhone 8.
*Magnetic ear buds really do help keep cords from tangling.
*One year warranty
*MFI Certified

Cons: There isn’t much bass to speak off when streaming music/watching music videos. I purposely played a variety of music and on a variety of platforms hoping they would pick up the differences, but they did not. I had to really crank it up to get the even close to the sound I wanted. I did notice better sound with the music on my phone than on my iPad but that’s not where I’m going to be using these most of the time. And I still didn’t consider it great.
* I found the buttons to be clumsy. The last pair I had were flat and so much easier. I kept fumbling. I did like the options they gave, I just wish they were smoother to use.
*Ear buds are one size fits all so hopefully the size medium they send fits you. I used the small pair from the ones I was replacing and they fit/felt much better. They sounded a little better too. Didn’t notice any change in noise cancellation.
*I did not receive the silicone pouch. Mine is the burlap bag pictured like you would get at the dollar store.

I have found with the numerous reviews I’ve read that the plug in breaking like I had with my other pair is fairly common. I read it about this brand too. I honestly don’t understand why when lightning plug technology is there with charging cables, they just can’t seem to get this right...baffling.

Updated review!

Not sure about the noise reduction yet as it was pretty quiet tonight, but that will change & I will update!
I think this was a great price point and excellent value!

Update: I don’t think they “reduce ambient noise” significantly, but I do still really like these.
Love not needing the dongle adapter, also really like the volume/pause control. It is just below your chin so it’s really easy to access.

The 3rd time or so that I retried plugging them in, they still were not working and then the metal piece stayed in my iPad & the rest came out. Fortunately I was able to pull it out with my fingers. NOT HAPPY! Really like these too...Amazon gave me vendors email so I can find out regarding warranty. Hoping they will at least send a replacement since I’m already beyond the refund timing. Will update. I did not pay additional money for a warranty.
Since I need headphones I ordered these, PALOVUE Earflow in-Ear Lightning Headphones Magnetic Earphones, this was the pair I was going to get initially but got these instead. Every pair I’ve researched has negatives but the Palovue’s have about 75% positive reviews and a year warranty so I went that route. And they aren’t terribly expensive at $22.

*January 26, 2020: The vendor response was fantastic! I received my replacement headphones in the mail today which makes this a 3 day turnaround from when I first contacted them. I used the product support option, talked with Amazon digitally, got the vendor email and went from there. Their service moved my review back up to 3 stars. I initially had my review at 4, put it down to 1 when they broke, but the customer support puts it back to 3 because I really do like these headphones. They stand by their one year warranty.
The replacement pair I purchased, listed above, is not worth it. I was disappointed. The magnetic earbuds are the best feature. They are my backup pair.
I have found with the numerous reviews I’ve read that the plug in breaking like I had is fairly common. I read it about the other brand I bought too. I honestly don’t understand why when lightning plug technology is there with charging cables, they just can’t seem to get this right...baffling.

Sooooo, I bought this Fitbit for myself randomly. I was so excited to receive it and it looked very sleek and nice! I wore it just about everywhere. Three weeks into having it, I traveled to New Orleans with the Fitbit on my wrist... I arrived at the hotel late in the evening and realized something felt different. So I checked my pockets, and looked around the floor of my hotel room, when I finally realized what it was. My Fitbit was gone! No where in sight. Not anywhere on the floor, no where. I had no idea it was missing, and I was so sad. I had no idea where it was, so it literally popped off my wrist somewhere at the airport or in the taxi, and I didn't even realize it until it was too late. I even bought an App on my iPhone to help me try and find my Fitbit, but that didn't work at all and it was a waste of $4.99. I don't have $89 to spare to buy a brand new one, which also sucks.

It's a great product, but I personally recommend spending the extra $30 for the Fitbit Charge HR because it is like a watch wrist band, rather than just a snap on one, so you don't ever have to worry about it just popping off! If I ever got a new one, I would most likely buy the Fitbit Charge HR.

Good points:

Bad points:

Looks like the motion detection is now working correctly. Bluetooth was cutting out and crackling when playing music. Had to contact tech support and after updates, it seems to be working fine. That being said, the device shouldn't need updates as soon as you get the tablet. That's a bit off putting.  But so far, the problem seems to have been resolved w/the updates. Alexa is okay, but doesn't connect w/many of the electronics in my house (and they're all fairly new).  But it's good for weather, raising and lowering music, etc, without having to do anything. Picture is good. Power and volume buttons are too small and difficult to find easily, but overall it is good for watching videos, reading, etc. If you're used to using a lot of Google apps, this isn't the tablet for you. Overall it's fine considering the price.

I purchased this for a desktop computer on which there is absolutely no room for traditional speakers, as the speakers from the monitor were just not cutting it. These are an acceptable substitute. They put out more sound than the monitor speakers, by a small margin.  I also hooked these up to my MacBook and saw about the same amount of improvement in the sound compared to the built in speakers. This unit fits nicely on the top of the screen, and for travel the included travel bag is a nice touch. Nor does it take up a lot of room in my laptop bag. Easy to set-up and use, just not quite there with the loudness/performance for the price. Still better than a lot of laptop speakers.

UPDATE: 11/15/14 Just found out that you can NOT transfer overdrive (library) WMA format books. I didn't realize it earlier because all the books I'd put on it were in MP3 format which do work fine, but some library books only come in WMA and apparently the sport only supports DRM free WMA, which means not library books.
UPDATE: 11/8/14 Wound up w/problems w/this clip & had to return for replacement. Was w/in 30 so did thru Amazon & just got new one in. Will see how it works. This happens occasionally w/clip+ & zip so not too worried. Still think the clip+ is the best, followed by the zip, then the sport.
UPDATE: 10/5/14 I have since found the Pause delay has gotten much worse than when I 1st tried it & can last way too long like others said - sometimes about 15 seconds when resuming play - which may not sound like much, but it is. It becomes very problematic in that it takes so long you don't know if you pushed play again or not. If you push it again too soon then when it finally does come on it immediately goes off again. Sometimes it's taken me up to 6 tries to get it right & that is ANNOYING! Also, it tends to go to have a delay before playing after you FFWD, which again can cause the same problem. And, as others said, the FFWD is Very Slow. Sometimes when I try to FFWD I have a pause issue & then somehow it goes back to the start of the book & then I have to start all over w/the FFWD - again - very irritating. The bigger screen seems a waste too, as the book cover is shown in a tiny square that's hard to see. In the zip it fills the whole screen & is actually bigger, so what was the point of the larger screen? I don't know who at SanDisk could actually think all these usage & design changes were good ideas, as far as I can see they've only come closer to ruining a good thing. If they wanted a new & improved clip, they should've kept all the features & workings of the clip+ & just added a larger color screen, a more durable clip (& a longer battery time is always nice), but changed nothing else. Each newer model, even the zip, but especially the sport has taken away more than it's gained. For the meantime, I've reduced it from 4 to 3 stars & must say the sport model is the worst of the 3. I'll be writing to Sansa support to see if there is some sort of software fix. If there is, I'll revise this review again.
------------------
Original Review:
Works fine with audiobooks. Read a number of bad reviews & 1 that said couldn't use with library's Overdrive Media system, but I did not have any real trouble with it. Yes, it's true, doesn't have a MSC setting, but I xfr'd books from OM w/no problems. The only difference was I normally make a new folder under audiobooks & name it w/book title, series # & author's name. When I made a new folder it wouldn't let me name it. Instead I simply chose Audiobooks, then in the first box where that showed, went in and typed a / then how I wanted sub folder to be named, then continued as usual. It make the sub folder as I named it and xfr'd the files there. When I checked my books folder, they were all there under the folders I'd named that way. I'd had this same problem once before with a clip zip, and it's not a major impediment, it's actually a bit faster, really.

With Audible, I've never been able to activate or deactivate a device, I always have to contact them to reset. Also at 1st it showed the internal drive space as the external drive space even tho no card was in the clip. I chat'd them & they logged onto my pc, activated it, renamed the drive it was showing as & now it works fine. They even fixed another problem I'd had w/Audible software crashing when I tried to delete books on any of my clips. They said the drive identification problem was specific to the clip sport, but they fixed in in almost no time & I would've had to call them regardless of which clip type I bought. It is slightly bigger, about 1/4" taller, 1/8" wider & 1/16" deeper but it's still darn small & the bigger screen makes it a bit easier to read. I haven't tried in sunlight but I can't read either the clip+ or zip in sunlight either, I just find or make some shade. I listen only to audiobooks so I can't comment on playlists or other music functions.

Re the power button, I don't have a problem w/it working, but I would prefer a separate button, don't know why it was removed. Re the pause/play delay. Yes, there is one. It's about 1-3 seconds from pressing pause & about 2-7 seconds for pressing play again. I didn't find it to be an extremely long delay, but again, would prefer they fix that issue but it's not a deal breaker for me, I just have to remember to wait those few seconds & not try pressing the button again too soon! I can see where if you are doing something where you're operating the functions w/o looking it would be irritating.

I haven't tried copying cd books that I've ripped w/windows media player, but I know that the order always gets messed up with clip zips, so I've always only used storage on micro cards with the clip+ for those books. They changed something when they made the zip & I'm guessing the sport won't be different, but I'll add a post if I find differently. I use the zip & now the sport for Overdrive & Audible. I always keep 3 clips at any given time as they tend to die in about a year of daily use (2-10/hrs per day) and any Overdrive books I've stored for them can't be put on a different clip, but they're cheap enough that works for me. The clip mechanism breaks sometimes (I have 2 working zips now w/broken clips) but I then use 2 part epoxy & glue a potato chip clip on and they don't last as long but can always glue a new 1 on as long as the clip works. Also, sometimes a clip dies & if holding down the power button for a long time doesn't work, I've found if I wait a few days sometimes then I can connect to usb on pc & it starts working again.

Yes, all clips have specific issues and the old clip+ is still my favorite and I'll always keep 1 of them that works, but for the other 2 I get what ever's on sale at the best price. I wanted an 8gb this time because I don't like to put Overdrive books on storage cards & it was only $10 more than a 4gb clip+ (for some reason their price has gone up recently). I, too, hope Sansa keeps making the clip+ because it's still the best one out there (because it can play copied cd books) but to me the zip & sport are pretty equal except for the mildly annoying pause delay, but if I can get an 8gb sport for same price as a 4gb zip, I'll live w/that! Sansa CLIPS are still by far the BEST & CHEAPEST & ONLY SMALL MP3 players that work well for audiobooks, so I'm still a loyal customer. ALSO THEIR CUSTOMER SERVICE IS VERY HELPFUL. They always replace any that break w/1 yr warranty, they help w/problems even after & sometimes can fix by updating software, etc. So for all those folks who had a problem, call Sansa before you give them a bad review! I use them for many hours every day & have for years now, so I know of what I speak. (Also, don't ask me why, but I've found the purple clip+ tends to have tighter audio jacks which cause static if headphone is not fully connected & it's harder to push jack all the way in, so just stay away from the purples - tho they will replace it if you have problems. Never had any trouble like that with black, blue or red one's.)

Yes, the developers have cheese for brains & the only 'improvement' in the newer models is larger screen w/color & graphics which can make book identification by cover image easier to figure out even if can't read type & the other changes in my opinion make them not work as well as the clip+. Those differences may not matter with music, but do for audiobooks. Each type has some flaws (& battery time is never as good as advertised, I'd say 8 hrs for clip+ & zip) but they're still better than anyone else for a no hassle, easy to use, tiny clip that you can wear w/o dragging on clothes or falling out of pockets & their prices can't be beat! I've looked & looked over the years & have never found anything better. So I still say thanks to Sansa for making the clips!
The sound quality is decent but it’s very hard to stretch even just for couple more inches.
Nothing too fancy here.  The sound quality is just fine but for the price it is ok.

the sound quality of the mic is poor when you use an extension of the earbud. I can hear fine but people on the other end complain they can't hear me. I have to take the extension off to talk on the phone.

Look better than they feel. The band area has material over it but there isn't padding between the material and the plastic. If your head is sensitive or you wear these a long time it probably will get uncomfortable. The ear padding is excellent, so I don't know why they skimped on band padding.

Sound wise, they're great for listening to music on my phone. But using my Roku app for private listening with my tv the sound is almost muffled. It's not as clear as listening to music or watching something on an app on my phone.

For calls it sounds like I'm far away, similar to how someone sounds on speakerphone. Defin9itely need to speak loudly to be heard well.

Power isn't everything. My intention was for the A90 to replace an old portable DAC/Amp combo that is only rated at 1.6W total at 75Ω. I figured the massive increase in output power paired with a much higher-end DAC would sound heaps better than the little DAC/Amp combo I've been using for the last 7 years. Sadly, the A90 made everything sound a bit thin and lifeless. It's like it has the negative characteristics of an overly clinical sounding amp without any of the positives like extracting detail.

It's not a horrible amp. It's just not a great amp. Maybe the A90 would sound better when paired with muffled/veiled or extremely warm sounding headphones. For Sennheiser HD800's or HD820's though, which are inherently bright, it's a horrible match. The A90 sucked the soul from the music with those particular headphones.

The chain I tested with the A90 was a Naim ND5 XS2 streamer > Nordost Silver Shadow BNC > Schiit Gungnir Multibit DAC > Cardas Clear XLR > Topping A90. There's usually a Schiit Mjolnir 2 at the end of the chain and it sounds amazing. I didn't expect the A90 to outperform the Mjolnir but I did expect it to outperform my little DAC/Amp combo, especially when being fed such a good source

All I can really take away from my experience with the A90 is DO NOT pair this amp with bright headphones. Can't comment on other headphones but avoid this amp if you've got HD800's or 820's.

Good cable but needs to be unplugged and plugged back in sometimes. I have it running out of an Omega Fenix sound card into a Schiit Gungnir Multibit DAC. The DAC has a "buy better equipment" light that comes on when you're not getting a good quality source going into the DAC. Sometimes it will randomly come on during a listening session and I'll need to unplug the cable and plug it back in. This doesn't happen with the optical input or a shorter Coaxial cable. I need this longer cable though to run it around the perimeter of the room into my DAC versus straight across the room in the middle of the floor. So it seems like the length of cable could be what's causing the quality to drop off sometimes.

Unfortunately I'll be returning these. I swapped them out with some Chord C-Line interconnects which run $75 for a 3 foot pair and the difference was night and day. Lots more clarity, better soundstage, and the low end really tightened up. After seeing these improvements I decided to take the leap and go step up to the Chord Clearway interconnects which run around $180 for a 3 foot pair. I'm hoping that I will see even greater sonic improvements when those arrive.

To be fair, I did like the sound of them. They didn't sound bad but when I did a direct comparison with the Chord C-Line's I realized that they just weren't hitting the mark. With almost $8k into my stereo it seemed dumb to skimp on the cheapest link in my system and not spend a little more money for a lot more quality.

These are decent cables for the price. Better than Monster Cable products where you're paying more for the marketing costs versus the actual materials that go into the cable. I would definitely recommend these to anybody who has a lower end to modest system that isn't extremely revealing. If you have a higher end system though I wouldn't make this your end-game cable without auditioning some other cables like the C-Line's mentioned above.

UPDATE: I have since bought a couple of other cheap extension tube sets that looked similar. As it turns out, this set is actually very good for a crappy tube set. They all seem to cheap out on the electrical connections, so, especially when you're linking more than one tube, they can loose the auto signals and the camera may give you an error. But these work enough of the time to be useful. ALSO IMPORTANT: These are better for internal reflections than most. They have nice masks (baffles) in the tubes and have shiny bits hidden. That's crucial for good macro. Otherwise you will have hazy photos. SO I UPGRADED the rating from my original review below.
NOT ALL OF THESE TUBES THAT LOOK SIMILAR ARE THE SAME!

If you're using these for professional work, buy Canon tubes (or Kenko are supposed to be good).

ORIGINAL REVIEW
These tubes are sold under many names (The flippy metal release tabs and the smallest tube being 13mm instead of 12mm are a tip off).

I didn't really think the quality of extension tubes mattered. They're hollow tubes with some wires running through them for electrical contacts! Hard to mess up. But this set (at least the one I received) is messed up.

Sometimes my camera (Canon 70D) will just throw up an error when these are attached. Often just after snapping the shutter.

NEVER did autofocus work.

NEVER would more than one tube hold on to the connection to the camera long enough to give an exposure without an error.

I did manage to get some photos with auto exposure working, but always with manual focus. I don't think the image stabilizer was working either (from all the shaking). I didn't test it by switching it off.

The mounts are plastic, but not the kind you get on a cheap lens. More like the kind you get on a cheap kids toy with fake chrome. NOT smooth. You get a sort of sandpapery feel when you turn it into the mount.

I'm throwing mine away. I won't pay up for Canon's tubes (at that price - I'd buy the macro lens first), but there has to be something better than this.

I have never had an e-reader before. I used to read a TON, but then I grew up and life happened, so wanted to get back in to it.

I purchased both the Paperwhite and the Oasis. The Paperwhite seemed like a great device, but I could tell immediately how much more my eyes liked the larger screen on the Oasis along with the warmth feature. The warmth feature was the biggest factor for me, as it made it look much more like an actual page out of a book. I've included a picture of the Paperwhite (on the right) and Oasis (left), both set at the same brightness, but with the Oasis's warmth setting on. You can also see there is no white Kindle logo on the Oasis, which I found ever so slightly distracting on the Paperwhite. The quality of the screen on the Oasis is also much better than the Paperwhite - text is more clear and crisp. If you commute a lot or size is important to you, Paperwhite is definitely the way to go.

I was really overwhelmed with the Oasis at first, just because it was so new to me. I'm pretty good with new tech, but the whole environment was slightly overwhelming because it's not just as simple as getting a new device on a platform you're already used to (ie, Windows, Android, Apple, etc). Once I got past the learning curve, I started to actually like it a bit. However, the way the Kindle sorts and handles your books could be much better. You can organize things in to 'Collections', but it still doesn't feel like enough. I recommend looking up Calibre and going from there.

My biggest gripe is the ergonomics of the Oasis. Although it's not much heavier than the Paperwhite, it feels like it because of the shape of it. It just feels heavier because of the weight distribution towards the center, and is awkward to hold with that bump/excessive weight distribution that sticks out. I am a 5'9" woman with 'normal' sized hands, so I can't even imagine how this would be for someone with smaller hands. I bought a case immediately because the shell is ridiculously slippery, and in my opinion, a horrible choice of material for something you're going to hold for hours. Looks pretty, but not very functional for an e-reader. I bought the 'Ayotu Skin Touch Feeling Case', and it is awesome. I ordered a couple of others and this one stood out among all of them big time.

Last gripe is that the screen is pretty slow and laggy at times. I know it's an e-reader, but it's a very expensive one that doesn't do anything else (which to clarify I am absolutely fine with BUT, see next point), but at that price, it should really be perfect.

A positive feature of this that is nice is that you can flip the device around and the screen flips with you, so if you are right or left handed or just want to switch sides during reading, that is super helpful.

I do like it, but am considering whether or not I am going to keep it due to the ergonomics alone.

The other issue is that I'm not sure the radio ever fully charged. I plugged it in, and a red light came on, which I assumed meant it was charging. However, after a couple of hours, the light never changed. So I'm not sure if that is merely a power indicator, or whether it didn't charge, or if it's designed not to indicate its charge level.

...but I first bought a considerably higher-priced, brand-name waterproof mp3 player that did not work at all. (I sent it back.) At least this one plays music. I'm spending an hour in the pool every day, and I just needed something I thought was pretty simple, a lightweight player to play the music I put on it, without too much sophistication; playlists would be nice but not mandatory; turn it on, swim an hour, turn it off.

At what I paid for this (24.99), I figured this would probably fit the bill. Well, my initial experiences were horrible. After complete insanity not being able to figure out why the danged thing kept playing songs I'd deleted from the player, I thought to call up "Get Info" on my Mac, and it soon became clear that the player is MS-DOS/FAT 32. I hooked up the player to my partner's Windows 8 system, and there was a ..Trash folder stuffed full of all the stuff I'd tried to delete. When I deleted this folder, then plugged the Aquacube back into my Mac, it was clean and I was able to copy mp3s back over from my Mac. I was afraid maybe I'd deleted something needed for the player software to work, but I'm listening to all the music I just copied back onto the player now and it's working fine. Shuffling, but fine. I at first had just copied over my directories set up by artist/album, but this time I wasn't going to take any chances; I copied the mp3s directly into the root directory.

For what I bought this for and what I paid for it, as long as I put the work in ahead of time to normalize the levels and determine the right range of beats per minute I need, it's going to be fine. I do use a timer I keep by the side of the pool to make sure I get my time in, so I'm not going to depend on this player to play so many songs in a certain order to alert me. Maybe there's a way to do a playlist with a squeaky clean (from a PC) player, but I'm too burned out from spending days on trying to get this to work properly that I probably won't fool with it. (I'd asked the company a question about playlists and got no response as of this writing, so forget it.)

The headphones are adequate. Not great sound, but they stay in my ears. It's a good thing they aren't as good as my other headphones, because I couldn't handle the volume on the good ones. Dang if I can figure out how to adjust the volume. The manual is pitifully written in just about every language I've ever heard of. Oh, and the USB end falls out of the port very easily, so be warned. I've taken to clipping the player to my Mac cord in an effort to keep it from pulling out and giving me the error that I didn't eject the disk properly.
