The earbuds I received for review don't have external volume control.  I have to adjust the volume using my phone or whatever device I have these plugged into.  I had my husband call me and the call button on the earbud cord worked fine. These are fine for in the car and yakking on the phone but if you want to listen to music it would be best to get a much better set of earbuds.  These don't have any bass to speak of, and the sound is thin and tinny.  You get a couple more pairs of bud covers for a better fit.  No instructions come with these but it's not really necessary since they're easy to figure out.

This is a great idea and I see that it works really well in other people's cars, but I just can't get it loud enough.  I don't want it ear drum breaking or anything near that, I don't like it super loud anyway, but when driving the road noise nearly drowns it out even when it's at full volume and my speakers are turned full up on.  Besides that, I had trouble finding a blank station and only found one, but when I connected the device and my car radio to it I got too much static.  So, I tried using the auxiliary cable since the instructions said if you can't find a blank station then use the aux.  I have a 1996 Honda  Civic and it has an auxiliary port so I connected the Guanda transmitter to my radio through it and Bluetooth to my phone.  The static was gone, but the volume was still a problem.  I like that I can use a micro card that has the music I want on it, but it will always have the volume problem.  The device looks very nice and is basically intuitive.

The sound quality is very good - no complaints there.  Connecting to my laptop and pairing went fast and easy and the battery life seems long.  Using the volume controls on the outside are intuitive and easy to operate.  The reason for the 3 stars is because these headphones have a very limited range.  If I move more than one room away, especially if behind a door or wall, they cut out.  If I'm using my laptop (most of the time) I have to carry it with me when going room to room while using these.  Also, though I have changed the earbud covers to different sizes, I just can't keep these in my ears.  They actually pop out and I'm always trying to get them back in.  I've never had this problem with earbud before.......I don't know what's wrong here.

This is a great boombox, imho. I like everything about it so far. It's bigger than I expected and has a nice, hefty weight to it. It feels substantial to carry around. The CD player works great, and Bluetooth connected within seconds. It's basically intuitive except if you don't like the flashing colored light show then you will have to read the instructions on how to turn that function off but it isn't hard to do. I turned them off and later turned off the boombox. When I turned the boombox back on the lights did not turn back on which will save on battery power.

The radio is clear and easy to tune either by hand or use the search function. I really like this thing. It's very reminiscent of boomboxes of the fairly recent past and has a good sound for this price. As of this review it costs $95.99, which I feel is a fair price. It doesn't get super loud but when I fully crank it up I don't notice any rattles, buzzes or distortions. It does get pretty loud though. It has a rubbery coating all over it that I like though it's not at all waterproof. So far I've been powering it through the power cord and haven't tried batteries yet but it takes 8 "D" sized batteries. I sometimes use these [[ASIN:B00WF0V3YU 8 Panasonic Eneloop Spacers 4 C Size Spacers, and 4 D Size Spacers, for Use with Eneloop Ni-MH Rechargeable AA Battery Cells + Battery Case]] in devices that require the larger sized batteries and they work well with my AA rechargeable batteries. It just makes buying big batteries not necessary.

Overall - a great boombox for the price. I love being outside on the patio in good weather and streaming my favorite podcasts and music via Bluetooth. And having the CD player is a great and useful throw-back to boomboxes of the past. It also has USB port, Sandisk port, headphone jack and a "line in" jack all easily accessible from the front. It's not the kind of boombox that has an internal battery that can be used to charge small electronics so don't expect that cool perk. But I still like everything about it and look forward to many years of using it.

UPDATE: 9.11.17 - We wanted to use this boombox during a power outage due to Hurricane Irma blasting through our area. It takes 8 D cell batteries which we had. However, inserting them into the battery compartment was nearly impossible and it took 2 people to do it. It was ridiculously difficult and I will never attempt that again. I'll dig out another radio instead. I've deducted 2 stars for that terrible design flaw.

There's a lot of reviews already about this product. I wavered for a good while about deciding if I wanted to accept this Cloudbook for review and now kind of wish I hadn't. As far as I'm concerned, the Cloudbook is like a merging of a laptop and a chromebook with neither giving the features that are special to each one. As far as it being a computer, it runs on Windows 10 of which I have great suspicions and doubts. If you remember, I believe most everyone received an offer for a free download of Windows 10 as an upgrade from whatever Windows program they were currently using. I have read from several sources that it was offered only as a way of installing NSA spyware on your computer. We are being watched and monitored at every turn. If you don't believe me, next time you are driving take a look at all the cameras on poles along the roads and highways and tell me we aren't being surveilled. Smartphones, smart TV's, smart refrigerators, dryers and washing machines are simply ways of letting TPTB know what we are doing at all times. How many loads of clothes you washed, what you are doing in your bedroom and on and on. So, what does all this have to do with this little and cute computer? It has Windows 10 installed.

If you are o.k. with that then overall it's not a bad machine. I really miss having a disk drive to load my own personal programs and don't like having to download stuff from the internet via the app store or some other internet source. And since it is a computer but has very little space for storage, you have to have an anti-virus program. It comes with one but it's only good for 30 days and you have to purchase it or get another one. Most of your stuff will be stored in the Cloud (like a chromebook) unless you opt for a Sandisk or external hard drive. And if you buy an external hard drive for more storage why not get a regular computer instead that has more bells and whistles and possibly a disk drive?

It looks like a chromebook and I have had to put a label on it to distinguish it from mine and my kids chromebooks. I'm having a hard time getting used to Windows 10 and it takes a long time to finally get on the internet. I have taped a piece of paper over the camera lens staring me in the face - call me paranoid if you wish but I don't like people in my house uninvited. The "shift" key is way too small and I'm always missing it.

As far as specs go they're listed on the main page but here they are again for your convenience:

11.6" HD Widescreen ComfyView LED-backlit Display (1366 x 768 resolution, 16:9 aspect ratio).
Intel Celeron N3050 Dual-Core Processor 1.6GHz with Intel Burst Technology up to 2.16GHz.
Windows 10
Intel HD Graphics
2GB of DDR3L Onboard Memory.
32GB Internal Storage
Secure Digital (SD) card reader.
802.11ac WiFi (Dual-Band 2.4GHz and 5GHz).
Bluetooth 4.0
Webcam (640 x 480)
High-definition audio support.
Two Built-in Stereo Speakers.
1 - USB 3.0 port
1 - USB 2.0 port
1 - HDMI Port with HDCP support.
Microsoft Office 365 Personal 1-Year Subscription (activation code included).
2-cell Li-polymer battery pack (4200mAh).
Up to 8 hours of battery life (Video Playback).
2.54 lbs. | 1.15kg (system unit only).

If you are already using Windows 10 then it should be easy to navigate, but I feel as if I'm learning a whole new OS though I use Windows 8 on my other laptop. It only detected two of my Bluetooth devices and I have several. If you want Word processing you must redeem your card number inside the box before a certain date or else it expires. And it's all cloud based so your data is out there and not in your pc safe and sound.

I will modify this review as needed, but I have not used this computer since a few days ago and probably will not be using it much at all. I like my chromebook better for web surfing, and it doesn't require an anti-virus program because it's totally cloud based but I never use the cloud. I store the stuff I want on my old desktop or other laptop. And my chromebook has access to a word processing program without having to buy it.

I really, really REALLY wanted to rave only wonderful things about these earbuds, and they're o.k., but I'm not really sure that they are any better than many less expensive ones out there even though the basic sound quality is very good. I was looking forward to trying out the noise cancelling aspect, but shortly after I started listening through them and using various annoying background sounds I have pretty much come to the conclusion that they sort of help with that, but not a whole lot. I had my family talk in the background while listening to a podcast and though I used the electronic noise cancelling function I could still very easily hear them talking. I put a movie on Netflix that my daughter watched and it nearly drove me nuts the other day because I was trying to watch a YouTube documentary at the same time with my other set of earbuds and I could hear the movie as much as the documentary. So, I put the same movie back on the TV and pulled up the same documentary on YouTube and tried these earbuds out on them. I could hear the documentary a lot better than before, but when I listen to other things it seems like sometimes these work well and at other times it's like they aren't working at all to cancel any background noise. I guess it depends on what your listening too.

I can't test these out while flying because I rarely fly anymore so I will have to leave that rating to other reviewers. But for what I've done it basically seems like when you turn on the noise cancelling function all it does is make what you are listening too a little louder. I find myself turning it back down. I dunno, I think if had spent $60.00 on these I would be a little disappointed. They feel well in my ears and several other sizes of earbud covers come with these, and everything can be placed in a small, zippered case that comes with the earbuds. A battery is also included in the package though you can still use these to listen and not use the battery powered electronic noise cancelling function. What I found terribly lacking is instructions. The one page instruction sheet is scant at best, and does not give me nearly enough information about how to use these earbuds, much less how to use the 2-pronged adapter that comes with them or how to make a conference call. They do tell you how to answer the phone by pressing a button on the left earbud cord. The video on the product page doesn't help a whole lot either. Not everybody is tech savvy.

Overall- o.k. for the most part, the sound quality is very good but the noise cancelling function really doesn't work all that well and the instructions are lacking.

I'm having a serious problem with the Denon DHT-T110 TV Speaker Base that apparently the other reviewers are not having. I called Denon Technical Support and after spending a lot of time behind the TV set making sure all the wires were hooked up correctly and then pressing different buttons on the Denon Speaker base, they can't figure out what is causing this problem. And the problem is this: No sound signal is going to the Denon speaker base through the TV from the Roku player. The Roku works just fine through the regular TV speakers and is connected directly to the TV via HDMI. When the input on the TV is set to stream via the Roku no sound comes through the Denon and it turns off. If I increase the volume on the TV speakers you hear sound. If the input is changed to TV with the TV sound off, sound will come through the Denon. Also, if a DVD is played on the DVD player which is connected to the TV, the sound comes through the Denon. It just won't put out sound when the Roku input is being used. And that's a real bummer for me because we watch a lot of Netflix and Amazon streaming through our Roku. I am using the digital optical cord included with the Denon Speaker Base. I have it connected to the Digital Optical "Out" on the back of my Sharp 37" flat screen TV to the digital optical "In" on the back of the Denon Speaker Base.

I will keep working on this problem, and if anyone reading this has any idea that might fix it please say so in the comments section. I would love very much to have it work and to raise the star level to 5. When sound does come through the Denon it's great! Loud, clear and no buzzes or rattles whatsoever like when the volume is turned all the way up when using the TV speakers. I love that it can get loud and there's no rattles or weird vibrations. and the night mode is very useful since the TV room is located underneath the main bedroom and my husband has to go to bed early since he has to go to work early. I like to stay up late and watch Netflix/Amazon or other streaming channels through the Roku (oops! That doesn't work through the Denon) and I keep the volume down lest it wake him up. I was really looking forward to using the Denon night sound function.

The Denon tech suggested hooking everything up to another TV to see if the problem is the Roku player or my TV. Unfortunately, I don't have another TV to test out the units to try and isolate the lack of sound from the Roku player to the Denon. I was really wanting to use this for night listening, but since I can't I will take the Denon to my mom's nursing home and hook it up to her small, flat-screen TV. Since she's half deaf, it might can help her hear the sound better. I will update this review afterwards.

I'd really just like to give this tablet 3 1/2 stars but it's definitely not over 4. It has 1GB RAM and 4GB storage and comes with a MicroSD slot for additional storage.

Here is my list of features and my opinion of them:

It takes approximately 36 seconds to fully boot up. The colors are fairly vivid on the home screen but that can't be maintained when actually using the device.

Intuitive. I didn't have any trouble getting familiar with this android and it didn't ask me a ton of questions and passwords to finally get started using it and surfing the net.

Wi-fi connection is pretty good! I haven't been dropped a single time yet and it seems to find my router fast and connects quickly. Movement on the net is not fast but that is because I have inherently slow internet service. I will take it with me to other wi-fi spots and see how fast it moves. But I'm o.k. with the speed so far.

It's not heavy, but not a feather-weight either. My guess is that it weighs approximately one U.S. pound.

Google based Android with several apps already pre-loaded. Google app store has a large selection of free and apps to purchase. I downloaded the Kindle app and so far it works nicely on this android.

Resolution: (1024 x 600) 7-inch display. I'm not thrilled with the resolution. It is not very clear especially when being held horizontally. If I want to look at picture on Facebook for example, I have to turn the android vertically to more clearly see the pictures and even then they are not very clear. I'm not really complaining since it costs less than $100.

Color quality - most definitely could be more vivid. Color is pale and reading posts on FB and blog sites can be somewhat difficult depending on the color font. FB is definitely washed out/faded but for what you pay the color is o.k. However, the color when using app games like mahjong is a bit brighter and slightly more vivid.

Sound effects are good when playing games but you've got to use earbuds/earphones when watching a movie on Netflix or watching YouTube videos. Otherwise, when the sound is turned up loud enough to hear, it can be mumbly sounding or the case of the android vibrates. Sounds fine with earbuds, no complaints there. However, you will have to furnish your own earbuds since it doesn't come with any.

Camera/video - barely above useless. I took some pics and they were fuzzy, faded, grayish and really not ideal at all. I guess the camera is better than not having one, but I wouldn't use it for an important occasion. Video is equally grainy, fuzzy and washed out. Camera lens works both ways, towards you/away from you. You can instantly upload any video or pictures to several social networking sites like FaceBook, Twitter, etc...

Battery life - I have only had this android for about a week now and have used it intermittently so I don't have a firm grasp on battery life, but so far I would estimate that it will go at least 2 hours before needing a recharge. It was very nice that a USB/AC outlet converter was included along with a USB cord (albeit short, approx. 18 inches). Will recharge fairly quickly (about an hour from depleted battery) when not in use.

Scrolling - This could be better. I am still trying to learn how to finesse this particular android's scrolling needs. It sticks a lot and when it finally scrolls it will ZOOM scroll very quickly and I have to try and stop it before it goes too far. And sometimes when I try to get it to scroll down it will go the other way and scroll up! It seems to like a firm scroll and does better when I apply more pressure to the screen and scroll slowly. But that doesn't always work either. The scroll feature can get irritating.

Bookmarks - it seems to only save bookmarks in icon form. I can't get it to save my bookmarks in a list. Also, I have accidentally added apps to the wrong category on the home page screen and cannot seem to delete them or move them to the correct category. So, most of the apps I use including game apps are all in the "tools" category.

Screen rotation function works alright. It will flip rather quickly to vertical or horizontal. Netflix seems to work only in horizontal. Interesting because my other inexpensive androids will only allow vertical for Netflix. (I have had several less than $100.00 androids in the past few years). The Kindle app with rotate depending on how you want to read. I like that a lot because I like having a choice.

The clock function seems to be very accurate. My other androids clocks would drift but this one seems to remain accurate time-wise.

Does not read well outside in natural light even with screen brightness set to highest setting. Might not be good for poolside use unless you are in shade.

It does not have Bluetooth capability.

It has GPS tracking (which I have turned off) and parental controls (which I do not need to use). One of the advertising features of this android is that it can be customized for up to 4 people's differing tastes. Kits are sold to change this android into your favorite characters such as "Hello Kitty", "Barbie", "Spiderman", etc...for your kids to use. Personally, that doesn't appeal to me and I'm going to be the only person using this android, but it can be specially set up for whatever your children would like. But you have to buy the kits separately.

I have only had this android for a few days and am still becoming familiar with this device. As I learn more about it or need to update what I've already written about it I will do so. So far, I am fairly pleased with it and it's functions. It's better than the other less that $100 android devices that I have bought in the past but still has some buggy issues like the scrolling. I don't go for the individual customizing gimmick but if you like that then this might be the android you been looking for.

And finally, here are the specs:

Display 7" 1024 x 600 pixels
Storage: 4 GB + Expandable MicroSD slot
RAM: 1GB
Networking: Wi-fi 802.11 b/g/n
OS: Android 4.1 Jelly Bean
Battery: Rechargeable 3800 mAh battery
Cameras: Front Camera (300K) & rear camera
(2.0MP) W/ Built-in Microphone
Other features: Micro-USB Port, Stereo Headset (not in mine!)
Parental Controls

I can't get this system loud enough to please me. I often like my music loud and raucousy! It says 40 watts but if you want some volume to fill up your room I don't think you'll be happy with this system. Right now I'm listening to, "Boogaloo Chevere" (tropical) and I have it cranked up to full volume and it's just not coming through like I expected. I have the sub-woofer bass turned full volume but I hear little bass and the horns and voices sound squeezed and strained. I'm thinking that the cheesy-thin auxiliary 3.5 mm input cable that comes with this system might be the reason. It's very thin and weak. Definitely needs to be more robust. Granted, I'm listening to music on my PC downloaded from I-tunes, but I think the set of 25 watt Logitech speakers (Logitech Z313 Speaker System) I had on before sounded better and at 1/3 the price of these. Where's my 40 watts of power here?!

I have this system set up straight from the box using what was included. The speakers are supposedly wall-mountable but no hardware was included so they're sitting on my desk, one on each side of monitor. The sub-woofer tower is underneath my desk and even with the bass turned up full I can only detect minimal bass output from it aurally and when I put my hand over the top of it I can barely feel any vibrations coming from it. I'm really kind of disappointed......why did they include such a cheap audio cable???

The satellite speakers look basically like a pair of binoculars turned up on their side. They look alright and are steady enough on their stands. I don't think I would mount these things on the wall anyway. I haven't tried connecting 3 different inputs yet, just my PC, but you can hook up to 3 external devices. The control knob is easy to use. You have to turn the big black knob to control the volume and to turn it completely off. The sub-woofer control knob is also on the main control knob. I have my control knob lying on floor beside my CPU. I have to reach down and pick it up to use it or else deal with having more cables on my desk.

My biggest disappointment is the way the classical guitar comes across on this system. I have to have the volume turned on nearly full blast to try to hear all the tones and colors of the instrument. My own home classical guitar recordings come across very weak and muted out as compared to the sounds on the Z313 system. Believe me, I am not hard of hearing and can hear a fly pooter, so I know what sounds clear and loud and what does not. But again, I think it's due to the cheap cable. I'm going to find a much better cable, try it out and report back. So for now, the 3 star stays.

UPDATE 9.28.12
I bought a Monster cable for twenty dollars and it only helps improve the sound minimally. I'm really surprised that this is the most volume I can get for 40 watts. It still gets loud for most types of music, but the classical guitar just doesn't carry as well on these speakers as it does on the cheaper set of speakers I had before.

The main thing about this radio that I really DO NOT like is that it has a permanent battery that must be charged via a USB cable. The cable must be connected to a computer or to a special adapter that can be plugged into any regular household outlet in order to charge it. The fact that the battery can only be charged and not easily replaced as in AA batteries to me, defeats the whole purpose of having such a radio. I consider the ability to listen to shortwave from an emergency aspect, such as if the power grid went down or for some other catastrophic reason. It should work for a while but when the battery dies, so does your ability to get news and information about your local area as well as other parts of the world, unless you have a way to charge it. And if the battery totally dies (I let mine completely expire), you will lose all of your settings including time and date.

I also don't have any use for the recording function, iPod player, and e-reader. They are nice extras but not necessary for a shortwave radio. Most people probably buy shortwave radios for their ability to pick up shortwave radio signals from around the world and not for it's recording function. If you should need it in the event of an emergency of some sort, will you be wasting it's precious battery energy listening to your iPod? And no one takes a radio like this to a pool anymore....they use their iPod, iPhone or whatever for all of their listening needs. Personally, I consider these types of radios to be stored away and used when things look ominous outside or other unfortunate global events are happening.

The owner's manual was not easy to understand, and the radio itself is NOT intuitive at all. If you don't have the poorly written manual to go by you will be spending a LOT of time trying to figure out how to work the controls on this radio. It was a lot of work just to get a few stations programmed into it, and somehow I still managed to delete them all. One aspect that I DO like is that it is very easy to turn it on. No need to fumble around looking for the on/off switch. Just push any button or turn the tuning knob and the screen lights up with the time and date. However, you must then proceed to use one of the functions for it to remain on. It only stays lit for exactly 3 seconds.

It's certainly better than no radio, but it's not very practical and there are better ones out there. It looks nice, has a decent overall sound quality for a small radio, is a easy size to deal with and comes with a black pouch to carry it in, but good looks can only get you so far. It's what's inside that counts. Also, for what it's worth, the black tuning knob on my radio fell off. I was able to get it back on, but what if I lost it in the dark and couldn't find it and a hurricane was coming towards my area?!!!

The sound quality coming from this set of speakers is really very good. I like to listen to classical guitar music and after a few tweaks and adjustments I got what I feel is decent sound for set of $35.00 speakers. I have no complaints about that at all. I like being able to play my iPod through them while leaving it connected to be charged. The speakers are attractive - slim, and black and go well with my desktop. The subwoofer sits under my desk and away from my big feet and adds a very nice quality to the overall sound.

My two complaints led me to giving them only 3 stars despite their good sound. My first complaint is that the iPod docking station was a pain to put together. It took quite a while to figure out how to assemble it despite reading the directions. Also, as another review has noticed, I can hear people talking faintly through my speakers when they are turned low. And no, I'm not schizo. I first thought it was people talking to each other in my neighborhood street outside my window, but as I leaned in closer to one of my speakers I could hear a woman talking through it. It sounded like a radio show, or a phone call. Weird. I was not connected to the internet but playing a rather boring game with the sound effects turned low. Maybe I was picking up signals from the TV set downstairs, who knows - there's so many different types of signals flying around now days. It's not happening now although they are still on so I don't know what's causing it. I hope this won't become a consistent problem because it was rather annoying.

Other than those complaints the speakers are quite nice. They can get very loud which my previous computer speakers could not do. The sound is not distorted too much when at full volume but the plastic case does buzz and vibrate some. But, I was just testing them and don't plan on using them full blast volume. I wanted something which I could clearly listen to mainly classical guitar since I record myself playing and need to carefully hear what I just did. I have listened to some of my previous recordings through them and feel these speakers do a good job clearly sounding the timbre and other natural sounds made by a classical guitar. It's not recording studio quality, but for a home recording I'm o.k. with them.

I got this for my brother, who enjoys this season and he said that it works pretty well. It fits onto his hat easily and is camo so there is a nice blending in with the rest of his outfit. The video quality is decent and because of that it is a great price. It connects easily to his phone and creates images and video with clear audio that he can send and save; the only thing is the files can get kind of large depending on the type of video you want to shoot so keep that in mind. My brother's area is overpopulated with deer so the "ethical" hunting and resulting meals are the only thing that I can concede to otherwise I would not feel right; but this is a valuable teaching and learning tool while out there.

ADT is a renowned security company and this camera is a nice extension of their products. It is easy to install and I like the customizable features. The only issue we had was with the battery life, which meant we had to charge/plug it to feel confident enough to have it at the office when we were there so much less these days. Otherwise the audio and video quality is great.

The headphones are designed well and comfortable, but the bass delivered was somewhat disappointing. The noise cancellation and battery life were great though. I see that these have since been discounted and at the current price point they are a much better buy.

I don't really like in-ear buds and use around ear headphones at home. This seemed like a decent on the go solution, but they seem like more trouble than they're worth. I haven't had issues with disconnecting or not having native English voice prompts, but they just don't seem to "do it" for me.

By nature of the fact they fit on the outside of the ear, they're not the loudest even at max volume. The design is nice because it allows me to hear people talking without having to pause the music or remove the headphones, but I wouldn't consider these as possessing any noise canceling properties.

They don't fit snug either and if I manage to get them into a position where they don't move around a bit, they'll begin causing discomfort after a brief period. I feel like I'm constantly adjusting them, which leads to me triggering the very sensitive touch function. I'm not positive how the touch functionality works, as it sometimes pauses the music as expected but often randomly controls volume.

They work and everybody's different, but they're ultimately too touchy, don't fit well and aren't loud enough.

Overall the sound quality isn't poor but placement is going to play a bigger role in quality achieved. The remote feels cheap and flimsy, but is the only way to alter advanced sound options. It's a fairly average product and it seems for everything to like here is something that disappoints. Most of all, I have issues with the sound dropping for periods. I've tried multiple sources and all three input methods and it still seems the sound cuts out at random times before coming back. A middling product that I can't fully recommend but also wouldn't consider trash bin material.

Overall, the product works. You're going to get audio that's a bit better than the cheap speakers on your computer monitor, certainly louder audio, but not necessarily the most crisp audio. They're tuned toward the low end and the audio feels like it has good body but seems muddy on the high end. Ultimately better than nothing but not amazing. You can shut off the RGB lights, which I was worried you may not.

Better than nothing but certainly not better than their price.
